stories.Headline: Microsoft unveils six specialized AI models at Ignite to rival OpenAI and Anthropic on cost
stories.Summary:
Microsoft unveiled six specialized AI models at its Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, and its executives pitched them against OpenAI and Anthropic. Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft's commercial business, said anything possible in Claude or ChatGPT could be done better with Copilot and for less. Jacob Andreou, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, said Anthropic and OpenAI force compromise on power and collaboration with simplified viewers and editors. Microsoft AI released a new batch of its own MAI models built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. CEO Satya Nadella announced on the same stage that OpenAI's GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

The lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price, on benchmarks Microsoft chose. Microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2. Andreou backed the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees, putting Copilot at $30 for an everyday AI user against $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude. For advanced users of each company's agent tools, it showed $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude, with most of the Claude figure estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic's $20 enterprise seat. The numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads, and reflect enterprise pricing that adds usage charges to a per-seat fee rather than the flat monthly subscriptions individuals pay.

Althoff said simply that anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less. Andreou said everyone has seen Anthropic and OpenAI embrace documents, slides and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration. Andreou said the full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription, which means Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter. A Microsoft spokesperson said AI is not just a technological trend but a transformative tool that, if adopted wisely, can yield significant returns. The same spokesperson said seeing AI as a long-term investment rather than a short-term solution can shift the narrative around its costs.

The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft's core business, having introduced new Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards last week that compete more directly with Office. Anthropic is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects. Anthropic's Claude for Microsoft 365 lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks. That product has less than a tenth as many weekly users as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday, citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report said.

Microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers, but another role was on full display during the Ignite keynote Tuesday: competitor. The stance is notable given that Microsoft still sells their models too. A Microsoft report highlights both the investment and potential rewards of adopting AI for small business owners ahead of integration. The report points out that AI can reduce labor costs through automation, optimize decision-making processes and enhance customer engagement. The report notes that implementation often comes with upfront expenses from software licensing fees to new hardware, plus training, maintenance and updates.

Nadella kicked off Microsoft Ignite with an Outlook outage mea culpa, saying we have work to do. The articles leave open what the remaining MAI models beyond MAI Code 2 and MAI Cyber 2 are and when they become available. They leave open how Anthropic's expected IPO this week turns out and how its financials and long-term growth prospects fare under scrutiny. They leave open whether Microsoft's cost comparison changes enterprise purchasing, given that the figures rest on Microsoft-commissioned GigaOm research and Microsoft-chosen benchmarks. They leave open whether customers stay with Copilot or switch, beyond the internal data showing Claude for Microsoft 365 at less than a tenth of paid Copilot's weekly users.

stories.Headline: China and ASEAN designate 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation
stories.Summary:
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations declared 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation on Monday, November 16, 2026. This announcement occurred as the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol prepares to enter into force on December 1, 2026. The upgraded deal moves beyond traditional trade liberalization to cover emerging areas like the digital economy and green development. It aims to shift the regional relationship from simple market opening toward deeper institutional cooperation and coordinated standards. This new framework will address global challenges by creating a more stable and predictable regional market and industrial chain.

The protocol, signed in October 2025, includes a standalone chapter on supply-chain cooperation for the first time in a bilateral agreement. It covers hard connectivity in logistics and digital infrastructure, plus soft connectivity for electronic payments, invoices, and bills of lading. The agreement empowers a regional market of nearly 2.1 billion people through high-level commitments and improved customs procedures. China and ASEAN will establish sub-committees on standards, small and medium-sized enterprises, green development, and the digital economy. These measures will reduce business costs by encouraging the mutual recognition of conformity assessment results to avoid duplicate testing.

An official from the Ministry of Commerce of China said the upgrade reflects a commitment to multilateralism and free trade. The official stated that the deal will create a safe and open environment for digital trade and investment. MOFCOM will support local governments and industries by organizing targeted outreach and training for enterprises to understand new rules. The ministry noted that these arrangements will provide fresh impetus to Asia-Pacific economic integration amid global trade uncertainty. They believe that improving system compatibility through digital cooperation will enhance the competitiveness of regional products more than tariffs.

Poh-Yian Koh of FedEx China said AI adoption must translate technology deployment into better decisions and measurable customer value. Robin Li of Baidu warned that AI risks becoming a bubble if it does not translate into practical business value. Yang Ting of Agilent Technologies noted that AI helps life sciences customers make faster decisions and improve data quality. Fang Ling of Alstom stated that AI can improve rail reliability but requires rigorous validation in real operating environments. Winnie Ma of VF Corp said realizing AI potential requires responsible governance and a combination of technology and creativity.

China has remained the largest trading partner for ASEAN for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has led for China for six. In 2025, the value of bilateral trade between the two sides exceeded 1 trillion dollars, up 18 times since 2002. Business leaders recently met at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, to discuss AI productivity. Executives highlighted China's AI Plus initiative and its large manufacturing base as key opportunities for multinational companies to validate applications. They noted that China's digital infrastructure and market scale provide a strong environment for the adoption of new technologies.

The two sides will now review relevant provisions under the protocol's future work plan and hold further AI consultations. APEC economies are called upon to share practical experience and expand digital skills to make AI applications more accessible. The Ministry of Commerce will continue working with ASEAN to advance practical cooperation and implement the new trade rules. The articles do not state when the specific sub-committees will be formed or the exact date for AI consultations. It remains open how businesses will specifically measure the tangible productivity gains mentioned by the various regional business leaders.

stories.Headline: New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago schools weigh leaving Google Search as Google refuses to unbundle AI
stories.Summary:
New York City, Los Angeles, and Chicago school districts are considering using alternate search engines this month. These three large districts are reacting after Google refused to remove artificial intelligence from student search tools. The conflict began because Google will not provide a search version that lacks chatbot features. Some schools across the United States are now blocking the AI or seeking other providers. This situation has created a firestorm of criticism from parents, education leaders, and government officials.

Starting next year, Google will automatically turn off AI products like Gemini and Search for schools. Administrators can choose to turn these tools on, but they cannot disable the AI Overview feature separately. Education accounts for K-12 schools will no longer be allowed to separate these features starting in early 2027. This means schools that reject AI must give up the entire Google Search service for students. Google has offered a guided learning feature to help students sort out problem-solving ideas step by step.

Kamar H. Samuels, the chancellor of New York City schools, said the district refuses to accept this binary. Chris Phillips, Vice President and General Manager of Google for Education, stated that search and AI are inseparable. Google claims that these two technologies are deeply integrated and cannot be separated for school users. The company argues that its new approach is necessary because the tools are now fundamentally linked. Google maintains that schools can opt out, but they must lose the search tool entirely.

Parents and teachers in Chicago protested at the Google office, fearing AI will replace teacher feedback and guidance. They worry that direct AI answers weaken deep thinking and may provide inaccurate or misleading information to students. Los Angeles has temporarily blocked all generative AI tools on student devices across all grade levels. Frederick County passed a K-12 AI ban, except for adaptive scenarios and specific AI teaching courses. A California lawsuit alleges a thirteen year old girl received suicide information from Gemini on a school laptop.

Google's ecosystem of Gmail, Docs, and Chromebooks has become essential infrastructure for many American public school classrooms. Chicago Public Schools uses over 400,000 Chromebooks for student research, communication, and completing various homework assignments. The district has already blocked ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini on all school-issued devices for safety and privacy. Chicago previously considered opening Gemini to high school students, but parents and the community strongly opposed that plan. Many authorities are dissatisfied that Google provided no stable way to turn off the AI features.

Chicago Public Schools is currently testing technical means to block the AI Overview and AI mode separately. If Google does not provide a separation option, the district will switch to other search engines. Other districts may struggle to find alternatives due to the administrative costs and tool gaps involved. The articles leave open whether Google will make concessions on its core rule regarding bundled AI services. It remains unclear if other large districts will join Chicago in a collective boycott of Google Search.

stories.Headline: LeBron James sues PlayVision over AI app Bron using his likeness and nickname
stories.Summary:
LeBron James sued the makers of an AI sports-betting app on Tuesday, saying they deliberately violated his publicity rights and trademarks by calling it "Bron" and using artificially generated images of him in their marketing. The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in New York, according to the Associated Press. James is a Philadelphia 76ers star and NBA superstar. The app's developer is PlayVision Inc., which is based in California. The app is called "Bron."

The complaint asks the court to block the makers from using James' name, to give up any money they've already made and to award damages, including fair market value for the use of his name as well as punitive damages. James' lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter on Nov. 5, after which the startup removed the ad from its X and Instagram accounts. The company took the ad down, but not before it had been reposted and viewed about 1 million times, the lawsuit said. The ad attracted about one million views on X within a day, according to the lawsuit. The marketing campaign this month featured an image of a person resembling James, down to his tattoos, voice and No. 23 jersey, sitting in a locker room and scrolling through the app.

James' attorneys called it "a willful, bad-faith tactic" to use the player's fame, likeness and nickname to promote "a new and unknown product." The lawsuit states that "Defendants did not care that they had engaged in illegal conduct to gain notoriety for their previously unknown app." It says they "intentionally created the false impression that Mr. James endorsed and was affiliated with their Bron App, in an effort to drive downloads and paid subscriptions." Gupta responded to the attorneys' demand on social media by writing that the app would get a new name, but no new name had been adopted by the time the lawsuit was filed. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday.

Messages sent by The Associated Press through the app's website and to email addresses for its founders seeking comment were not immediately returned Tuesday. The lawsuit notes that James typically commands tens of millions of dollars for such endorsement deals and that he already has an exclusive deal with the prediction market platform Polymarket. It alleges that the app's marketing was especially harmful in part because it showed the AI-generated James scrolling through bets involving NBA players. The lawsuit said "The integrity of NBA competition -- and the public's confidence that players are not betting on the games they play -- is of paramount importance to the league, its players, and its fans." It added that "Any suggestion that an active NBA player is betting on NBA games is therefore far from a trivial matter, and it should not be used for clicks and views."

The app's developer, PlayVision Inc., was launched by chief executive Anish Gupta and chief technology officer Marc Zoghby in 2025, with backing from the startup accelerator Y Combinator, as a program that would use artificial intelligence to analyze game and practice footage for sports teams and fans. This year, the company released its "Bron" app, which it says does not take direct wagers but charges a subscription fee for services such as bet tracking and odds comparisons. Bron is described in Apple's App Store as a "sports analytics and betting research app with live odds comparisons, data-backed picks, player and team trends, a multi-leg Slip and bet tracking." The listing says it does not accept wagers. PlayVision participated in Y Combinator's fall 2025 batch.

James is seeking damages and a court order preventing the defendants from using his name, image, likeness, and voice, as well as the Bron name. The lawsuit claims the founders calculated that the publicity would outweigh any potential legal consequences, effectively treating the alleged violation of James' rights as a marketing expense. It argues that James' endorsements are "uniquely valuable," adding, "That is why defendants decided to steal it for themselves." However, the ad remained available through third-party reposts, and the company had not changed the app's name as of the lawsuit's filing. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday.

stories.Headline: Trump administration considers requiring US firms to disclose use of Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration is considering a plan to force American firms to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This effort was reported by Reuters on November 18, 2026, citing three people familiar with the matter. The administration wants to discourage reliance on this technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger Beijing. Officials hope to reduce the use of Chinese AI through a name and shame campaign. This approach aligns with a broader anti-regulation stance on artificial intelligence within the current government.

The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy discussed the plan for companies like Airbnb. Airbnb uses the Qwen model from Alibaba to power its AI customer service agent for its users. Under this proposal, companies would be required to post their use of Chinese AI models on their websites. The plan targets open-weight models, which make core components available for anyone to download and adapt. These models include DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi, which was developed by the company known as Moonshot AI.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in July that the administration could sanction Chinese AI firms for intellectual property theft. He specifically mentioned the distillation process, where smaller models are trained using the output of larger American models. OSTP director Michael Kratsios said in April that China steals intellectual property from US labs on an industrial scale. The Chinese embassy in Washington stated that politicizing technology stifles global advances and they will safeguard Chinese businesses. The White House, the Treasury Department, and Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Representative John Moolenaar of Michigan welcomed the report, calling disclosure an important step in managing potential risks. Representative Andrew Garbarino of New York joined Moolenaar in launching a congressional investigation into Chinese AI use in 2026. They sent letters to Airbnb, DoorDash, and Anysphere, the maker of the AI coding tool called Cursor. DoorDash uses Kimi for internal tasks, and Anysphere's Composer 2 model was built on a version of Kimi. SpaceX is also affected because it bought Anysphere, though the company did not respond to comment requests.

Chinese open-weight models are popular because they are cheaper than proprietary tools from US labs OpenAI and Anthropic. In October, Chinese models were the three most popular by token usage on the marketplace platform called OpenRouter. The US government itself used an Alibaba model on a website to search federal regulations despite FBI accusations. Concerns grew after reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang having an affair with an alleged spy for China. This situation highlighted unpunished cases where Nvidia AI chips were smuggled into China, increasing pressure on the administration.

The administration continues to weigh whether this disclosure requirement will be enshrined in a formal rulemaking process. It remains unclear if the idea is gaining traction among other officials within the Trump administration's leadership. The government is monitoring the spread of open-weight models compared to US versions like Meta's Muse Glimmer. Other American open-weight models mentioned include Nvidia's Nemotron and the Beam model created by the firm Reflection AI. The articles leave open whether the administration will eventually move toward more punitive actions against Chinese AI companies.

stories.Headline: Singapore launches AI initiatives to fight financial crime and improve small business financing
stories.Summary:
Singapore launched three national artificial intelligence initiatives on November 18, 2026, during the Singapore FinTech Festival held at the Singapore Expo. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced these missions to combat financial crime, improve small business financing, and enable safe AI payments. The government intends to bring together researchers, public agencies, technology companies, and financial institutions to build shared capabilities for the sector. These initiatives aim to create tools and testing environments that allow the financial industry to achieve more than any single institution. Singapore will test these promising solutions against global standards and best practices before moving the successful ones toward wider deployment.

The first mission uses AI to spot scam patterns, with the Monetary Authority of Singapore pooling data from five banks. A design study for the governance and operating model of this industry-wide scam detection system will begin in early 2027. The second mission improves financing for small and medium-sized enterprises and startups by using richer data and realistic synthetic data. The third mission enables AI agents to make transactions, with the government testing these in controlled environments to ensure safe payments. Additionally, Gan unveiled PayNow Generation 2 and a new SGQR+ switch to make QR payments simpler for residents and tourists.

Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who also chairs the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said the goal is a leading innovation centre. He stated that scams are not confined to one bank because a victim's money can pass through several institutions within minutes. Gan explained that AI can identify patterns that traditional approaches miss, giving lenders a fuller picture of a firm's creditworthiness. He noted that AI agents must operate within defined authority and limits, while institutions remain accountable for actions taken on their behalf. The Future of Finance Institute will support these missions by coordinating partnerships and developing guidelines and standards for the sector.

Small and medium-sized enterprises are affected because AI may lower borrowing costs and make financing more forward-looking and accessible. Lenders are affected as AI helps them make faster, better-informed decisions for businesses with limited financial records or assets. AI tech companies are affected because they will be invited to develop and test solutions using synthetic data for SMEs. Residents and tourists are affected by the new SGQR+ switch, which allows payments using any preferred QR application. Companies exporting advanced chips are affected by US rules, as Singapore will act against those who violate international export laws.

The background includes the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which was signed in Manila on November 14 by eleven member states. This agreement allows member states to agree on interoperability standards and provisions to help countries with varying levels of digital readiness. Singapore is exploring initiatives under this agreement as it prepares to serve as the ASEAN chair for the year 2027. The government is also focusing on the Kampong AI initiative to foster collaboration among local and international artificial intelligence talent. There is a stated need for continuous skills upgrading to ensure the workforce is ready for an AI-driven future.

Next, the government will examine safeguards for AI agents, including common approaches to identity, authority, accountability, and system interoperability. Singapore will continue discussions with ASEAN members to identify collaborative initiatives that can benefit all the member states involved. The Republic will also continue to monitor the diversion of advanced US AI chips to China to protect its reputation. The articles leave open the specific results of the synthetic data trials for SME financing and the final design study. It remains unclear which specific AI solutions will be selected for wider deployment after the initial testing phases are complete.

stories.Headline: Visa expands its Agentic Ready program in Asia Pacific to scale AI agent payments
stories.Summary:
Visa announced the expansion of its Agentic Ready program across Asia Pacific on November 18, 2026, in Singapore to scale AI commerce. This second phase of the program focuses on acceptance by working with payment gateways, acquirers, payment service providers, and selected regional merchants. The initiative aims to prepare the digital payment ecosystem for transactions that are initiated by AI agents acting on behalf of consumers. Visa is leading this effort to ensure that agentic commerce can scale securely while maintaining the trust and security consumers expect. The company is leveraging its global leadership in digital payments to facilitate these new types of automated commerce experiences across the region.

The program launches with over 50 participants, and Visa expects additional partners to join the initiative throughout the year of 2027. It builds on a first phase from April 2026 that saw over 100 issuers across 10 markets join for readiness. Acceptance partners include Adyen, Stripe, Airwallex, 2C2P by Antom, Allinpay Merchant Services, ALTEKGLOBAL by VNPAY, ASB Bank, AsiaPay, AXS, and Bank of China (Hong Kong). Other partners are CAKE DIGITAL BANK, Checkout.com, Cherri Tech, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Credit Saison Co., Ltd., Cuscal Limited, DBS Bank, DCS, and dLocal. The list continues with Eximbay, Fat Zebra, Fiserv, FOMO Pay, GMO Epsilon, Inc., GMO Payment Gateway, Inc., Hang Seng Bank, ICBC (Asia), and Infcurion, Inc.

Additional partners are Kasikorn Global Payment Co.,Ltd., KG Inicis, Maybank, Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS Co., Ltd., Mizuho Bank, Ltd., National Australia Bank, NETS, Nuvei, and OCBC. The group also includes OEN Tech, Pine Labs, Rakuten Card Co., Ltd., Razorpay, Retail Payment Solutions as a Coles Group company, SB Payment Service Corp., and Sumitomo Mitsui Card Company, Limited. Final partners are Toss Payments, UOB, UQPay, Windcave, Wpay, Xendit, YeahPay, and YeePay, who will test agent-initiated transactions in real-world environments. T.R. Ramachandran, Head of Products and Solutions for Asia Pacific at Visa, stated that AI transactions must be secure and reliable. He noted that merchants need a clear way to understand their readiness as AI agents increasingly shop and pay for consumers.

Merchants are affected because they must now determine how to recognize trusted agents and support them through checkout and post-purchase services. Visa is collaborating with Atlas Kitchen, CardInfoLink, Cleverbridge, Clink, Eats365 POS, FluxA, Juspay, [manif], Obenan, Pivota, Prava, and Reap Technologies Limited. They are also working with Set Sail AI, Shoplazza, and SHOPLINE to explore how agents discover products and build shopping carts for users. These partners help address practical questions regarding what an AI agent can access during the payment process in real-world commerce experiences. The goal is to provide transparency and control that businesses and consumers already expect from the existing digital payments landscape.

The program is based on Visa Intelligent Commerce, which is a portfolio of initiatives designed to enable secure agentic commerce experiences at scale. Visa uses its decades of experience in global technology and security to help partners embed intelligence into their specific commerce journeys. The Visa Acceptance Platform supports the payment lifecycle through credential management, fraud protection, dispute resolution, and acceptance across various digital channels. Additionally, Intelligence Commerce Connect enables these agentic experiences across different agents, commerce platforms, payment schemes, and various global networks. Visa currently facilitates transactions between government entities, financial institutions, sellers, and consumers across more than 200 countries and territories worldwide.

Next, acceptance partners will assess their existing systems and identify gaps while testing tokenized credentials, authentication, and transaction processing capabilities. They will specifically examine how to support agent-led discovery and post-purchase interactions to reflect the needs of different markets and payment ecosystems. Organizations that are interested in joining Agentic Ready or collaborating on agentic commerce are encouraged to contact their specific Visa representative. The articles leave open exactly how many more partners will join in 2027 and the specific results of the real-world testing. They also do not specify the exact timeline for when these AI agent payment capabilities will be fully available to all consumers.

stories.Headline: Nvidia stops shipping powerful AI chips to China
stories.Summary:
Nvidia Corp. announced it will stop shipping powerful AI chips to China on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Interim CEO Colette Kress revealed this decision during an earnings call with analysts on November 17. The company will remove licensed Hopper-based data center products from its future guidance. This move follows the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang on November 12, 2026. The board unanimously accepted his resignation as president, CEO, and director, effective immediately.

The company sold 2.4 billion dollars of licensed Hopper products to China in the third quarter. This follows US government licenses for H20 exports to Hong Kong, Macao, and mainland China in April 2025. Deliveries of H200 chips to China began in limited quantities in mid-July 2025. Nvidia previously sought permission to sell advanced Blackwell chips to China, but the Trump administration never acquiesced. The H200s are two generations behind the leading Rubin family of chips.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that future guidance excludes licensed Hopper data center products. She did not elaborate on why the shipments were ending during the earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones said the board recognizes that national security dynamics are changing the marketplace. Jones noted that the next CEO must navigate these waters very carefully. Nvidia also announced the formation of a board committee for national security and export controls.

The Trump administration increased scrutiny of processor exports to several countries on November 16. New rules limit sales when data center buyers provide Chinese companies remote access to AI servers. The People's Liberation Army is actively soliciting advanced chips to develop artificial intelligence military capabilities. Chinese companies like Huawei and Cambricon face a quality gap compared to Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission reported these findings in its 2026 annual report.

Jensen Huang was ousted following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. This woman worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed, which investigators eye for potential diversion of chips to China. Beijing denied that it attempted to spy on Huang, who expressed a desire to return as CEO. Fiscal third quarter revenue hit 115.8 billion dollars, while net income reached 65.3 billion dollars. Data-center revenue was 107.6 billion dollars, with supply-purchase commitments totaling 390 billion dollars.

The SEC is conducting a civil investigation into earlier disclosures, and Huang will appear before House panels December 1. An Nvidia lawyer is scheduled to testify on December 2 regarding these matters. The Commerce Department issued a rule to stop remote access to chips through third countries like Malaysia. This response followed criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and members of Congress. The articles leave open whether China can close chokepoints in logic fabrication, memory, and CUDA software.

stories.Headline: Nvidia expands supply chain partnerships to scale AI and high-performance computing infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Nvidia unveiled several high-performance computing developments at the Supercomputing 26 show in Chicago on November 18, 2026. The company is expanding its business beyond selling GPUs to supply complete AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. These announcements cover next-generation GPU and CPU platforms, networking, interconnect technology, and systems for large-scale AI workloads. Nvidia also announced expanded commitments with various supply chain partners on November 17, 2026, to support sustainable growth. These strategic agreements aim to align manufacturing capacity with the demand for accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms.

The Rubin HPC GPU, shipping in 2028, features over 50,000 CUDA cores and seventh-generation NVLink for scientific computing. A rack-scale Vera CPU platform combines 192 CPUs per rack with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking and SHARP in-network computing technology. Kinsus will expand ABF package substrate capacity at its Taoyuan, Taiwan, Youth campus by over 3.5x by 2028. Amkor is expanding packaging capacity in Arizona and South Korea through agreements totaling nearly 3 billion dollars since 2026. stories.Headline: IREN, CoreWeave and Nebius fall 63% to 79% from 2025 highs despite surging revenue
stories.Summary:
IREN, CoreWeave and Nebius have fallen 63% to 79% from their 2025 highs even as revenue and contracted backlogs surge, BigGo Finance reported on Nov. 18, 2026. Through Tuesday's close, IREN traded at $15.81, down 79% from its 2025 high of $76.41, while CoreWeave sat 74% below its peak and Nebius Group was 63% under its June high. The selloff accelerated since early October, when the Nasdaq set its latest record, with CoreWeave shares falling 45% since then and Nebius 57%, according to Reuters. The Motley Fool reported the same day that the neocloud industry had gotten bad headlines, with secondary effects harming CoreWeave and Nebius. Foreign Policy Journal reported on Nov. 16, 2026, that Democrats securing control of both chambers of Congress in November's midterm elections amplified investor anxiety over AI regulation, power consumption rules and restrictions on data center construction.

IREN's revenue rose 66% sequentially to $228 million in the September quarter, with AI cloud revenue nearly tripling to $200 million, and its contracted revenue backlog grew 22% to $20.3 billion, roughly two-thirds with investment-grade counterparties including Microsoft and Nvidia. CoreWeave's quarterly revenue jumped to $3.66 billion from $1.37 billion a year earlier, the company lifted its full-year outlook, and its backlog stands at about $132.5 billion. Nebius told investors customer prepayments on new contracts now cover more than 100% of the cost of bringing that capacity online, up from 50% to 60% in the second quarter. IREN had targeted more than $4 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026 but now expects that level in January or possibly as late as February, after a customer requested a design change and suppliers ran late. CoreWeave booked $207 million in operating income last quarter but paid $846 million in net interest expense, up from $310 million a year earlier, producing a net loss of $709 million.

Nvidia has been both shareholder and financier to the neoclouds, through a $6.3 billion order to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032 and a $2 billion investment in Nebius announced in March for an 8.3% stake. With Jensen Huang out as chief executive and former finance chief Colette Kress in the interim role, bond investors are questioning whether that support continues in the same form. Loren Moran, a fixed income portfolio manager at Wellington Management, said it is fair to say anyone who takes over will have a lower risk threshold than Jensen when it comes to Nvidia's balance sheet, and there may be a lot less credit availability toward weaker players. Tony Trzcinka, an investment-grade portfolio manager at Impax Asset Management, said existing contracts should survive the transition and it is all about whether Jensen's successor would want to be as adventurous in going into all these different arrangements. Miriam Wheeler, Goldman Sachs' global head of leveraged finance, said in the bank's "Top of Mind" note that the market had expected roughly $60 billion of AI-related high-yield issuance this fall, but supply has dried up since late September, with no new deals in the past month.

CoreWeave bonds issued in June at a 9.625% yield now yield close to 15%, and Nebius convertible notes sold in August at 4.5% traded at 70 cents on the dollar last Friday, pushing their yield above 12%. JPMorgan cut its IREN target to $55 from $65 on Nov. 9 while keeping an overweight rating, citing rising contract prices, and Jones upgraded IREN to buy on Nov. 6 with a $40 target. Goldman Sachs lowered its CoreWeave target to $101 from $106 and maintained a buy, and Citi named the company among its top software picks, pointing to signs of strong AI demand and nicer valuations. The consensus IREN price target of $56.50 across 11 analysts, eight of them at buy, implies roughly 257% upside from current levels. TeraWulf Inc. carries the highest short interest among the group at 24.34% of outstanding shares as of October 30, even though the stock remains fractionally positive for the year at 5.20%, and the company has shed nearly 40% of its value over the past six months.

The neocloud business is fairly new and was brought about by massive investments in AI infrastructure, as the biggest AI hyperscalers could not get enough computing capacity online fast enough, so other companies built their own AI data centers and rent them out. The Motley Fool reported that these upstarts do not generate ample cash flows to build data centers like other major cloud computing providers and must seek outside funding through issuing debt and selling shares. Nvidia became a major shareholder of both CoreWeave and Nebius as a result of seeing them as two of the best operators in this space. CoreWeave recently saw some of its debt get priced at distressed levels, which means there is a low likelihood of it repaying its commitments. The Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF lost nearly 4% in a single session and extended its six-month decline to more than 18%, while the NASDAQ 100 recorded its steepest one-day drop in 19 months, falling nearly 6% and trimming its year-to-date advance to just 5% after surging to a record peak of 30,800 on AI enthusiasm.

IREN still expects about $15 billion in capital spending for the remainder of its fiscal year, and $6 billion of that has not yet been arranged, while Nebius plans to spend $40 billion to $45 billion next year. Nebius also pushed back its targets, with management saying the revisions were just about timing, not demand, and its stock fell 17% on the day it reported. CoreWeave trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of about 1, Nebius around 3, and IREN at nearly six times estimated fiscal 2027 revenue on an enterprise-value basis, against 13.4 for Nebius and 6.9 for CoreWeave by that measure. Danny Zaid, a portfolio manager at TwentyFour Asset Management, said the uncertainty for the overall space means greater risk premiums expected by investors and expected dispersion to increase as investors evaluate credits on a case-by-case basis. BigGo Finance said the practical signal to watch is debt and deadlines rather than revenue growth, and that if IREN reaches its $4 billion run-rate target by February and CoreWeave keeps raising capital on acceptable terms, current prices may look cheap, while if delays keep accumulating the repricing may not be over.

stories.Headline: Unesco and UCL report AI models abandon climate facts when users challenge them
stories.Summary:
Unesco and University College London released a report on November 16, 2026, about artificial intelligence models and climate science. The study found that these AI models often abandon established climate facts when users challenge them during conversations. This research was presented at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, known as COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye. Accuracy for these models fell by 31 to 35 percentage points under sustained pressure from the users. Roughly eight in ten of these concessions occurred at the very first sign of a user disagreement.

Researchers tested up to 33 leading models across 13 languages, nine datasets, and 656 climate policy questions. They used En-ROADS, a simulator from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Climate Interactive, to check policy interaction accuracy. English accuracy averaged 88.6 per cent, while Bengali and Hindi were 83.6 per cent, Urdu 81.4 per cent, and Swahili 78.3 per cent. Performance in Spanish, French, and Portuguese was comparable to English, but the gap for Swahili reached over 16 percentage points. Policy interaction accuracy was only 33.8 per cent, which is barely above the 33.3 per cent expected by chance.

Ivana Drobnjak of UCL Computer Science stated that AI is not a dependable substitute for qualified experts or scientists. She noted that a conversational tone gives AI an air of authority despite its inability to perform complex reasoning. Senior author Dr. Maria Perez-Ortiz said AI is good at explaining knowledge but can give a false sense of capability. Lead author Leona Verdadero said it is concerning that models are incentivized to agree with users and deny facts. These experts warned that AI models should not be used by researchers or policymakers to develop actual climate policies.

The report affects policymakers, teachers, and journalists who use chatbots to explain climate science and inform public debate. It notes that speakers of languages like Swahili live in regions disproportionately affected by the impacts of climate change. Users who claim to be climate scientists, policy advisers, or sceptics can all cause AI models to concede facts. A single false claim from a supposed scientist could reduce the accuracy of a model by 12.9 percentage points. The findings highlight a significant gap between recalling simple facts and understanding how complex climate policies interact together.

The report was commissioned by Unesco as part of the Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change. This initiative was launched in November 2024 by the UN, Brazil, and Unesco to fight sophisticated climate disinformation campaigns. The research was a collaboration with the Unesco Chair in Artificial Intelligence at UCL, which was established in 2024. This Chair is hosted by the UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence and connects technical research with ethical and policy frameworks. The study is part of a series including reports on resource-efficient generative AI and gender bias in models.

The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change launched priorities for action on November 13 at COP31. It calls on AI companies to disclose environmental footprints and publish how their systems affect the reliability of information. Governments are urged to integrate information integrity into their national climate plans and their national AI strategies. Unesco recommends stronger testing against user pressure and independent checks before deploying AI in education or public services. The articles leave open how companies will respond to requests for transparency regarding their training data and performance.

stories.Summary:
VodafoneThree announced plans on November 18, 2026, to test Nokia's AI-RAN technology. The company will use Nvidia GPU-based hardware for these upcoming trials. These tests will occur in both lab and field environments in the UK. The operator intends to improve mobile network performance and efficiency through this. They also want to support new devices and services with this technology.

The trials use Nokia AI-native anyRAN software running on the Nvidia Aerial RAN computer. This architecture includes a Red Hat OpenShift cloud management layer and Nvidia compute. Vodafone Group opened a test center in Malaga, Spain, for broader studies. This facility evaluates Nokia, Nvidia GPUs, purpose-built ASICs, and Intel Granite Rapids processors. Nokia aims to double spectral efficiency by the year 2028 through these efforts.

Valeria Baiamonte is the director of network strategy and transformation at VodafoneThree. She stated that the UK trials will take place during the next year. Baiamonte said AI-RAN is extremely important for differentiated services like SuperMobile 5G slicing. She explained that AI helps predict and reconfigure resources quicker than was previously possible. She believes AI for RAN is the first monetization case for varied services.

Gabriel Brown is a senior principal analyst for mobile networks at Omdia. He said operators will get revenue uplifts from new AI-enabled devices and services. Affected devices include XR glasses, smartphones, cars, and Meta Charms connected to Muse AI. Brown noted that the industry must prepare for vast numbers of AI endpoints. These new AI endpoints will have a different connectivity profile than current devices.

Vodafone mainly uses Ericsson and Huawei for RAN equipment across its European footprint. It has deployed Nokia in Albania and recently awarded a deal for 7,000 UK sites. Only ten of those UK sites were activated as of April this year. VodafoneThree is also working with Ericsson on AI-RAN using custom silicon hardware. A new massive MIMO radio in London uses neural accelerators to increase inference.

BT plans to trial the Nvidia platform in the EE network next year. The first Nokia and Nvidia AI-RAN sites should be deployed in Birmingham. Deutsche Telekom, Elisa, and Orange are other European operators planning these field trials. T-Mobile recently completed the first voice call using Nokia software and Nvidia hardware. stories.Headline: General Assembly finds 52% of L&D leaders say AI use erodes worker soft skills
stories.Summary:
General Assembly published research on 19 November 2026 showing that many Learning and Development leaders believe AI is weakening employees' human skills, IT Brief Australia reported. The study surveyed 510 HR and Learning and Development leaders at large companies across six countries. More than half of respondents, 52%, said AI use is degrading skills such as communication, conflict resolution and collaboration. Another 41% said ensuring employees retain or develop critical thinking, communication and other soft skills despite using AI will be one of their biggest challenges in the coming year. The findings highlight a tension inside large organisations as companies expand AI training while trying to preserve workplace skills that are harder to automate.

At the same time, 83% of respondents said human skills are becoming more valued within their organisations, and 59% expect demand for soft skills training to rise. Nearly two-thirds, 64%, said their teams are under pressure to deliver AI upskilling across the workforce, and AI literacy was most often ranked as the top skill Learning and Development teams themselves will need. One-third of respondents, 33%, said closing the AI skills gap is a leading challenge, while 31% pointed to change management and employee fatigue around AI. The research found that 57% of leaders expect demand for role-specific AI training to grow, while 56% expect their organisations to expand personalised learning journeys, 55% expect more hands-on training and 52% expect more job-based or role-based training. Out-of-the-box third-party training was the option most likely to be deprioritised, with 15% of organisations expecting to place less emphasis on it.

Daniele Grassi, Chief Executive Officer of General Assembly, said employers are trying to balance technical training with broader workplace development. He said Learning and Development professionals are tasked with building role-specific AI skills while making sure the human skills that matter most do not erode in the process. He said companies are increasingly looking to integrate AI and soft skills training to prepare employees for the future of work. He said training is becoming more hands-on, with opportunities to practice critical thinking, judgement and collaboration alongside AI usage and get feedback in real time. Among respondents who said their learning strategy is fully linked to documented business priorities, 23% expect a significant budget increase, compared with 11% of other respondents.

More broadly, 73% said company leadership regularly asks for Learning and Development input on workforce capability, transformation or future skills decisions, while 63% said Learning and Development leaders help shape business strategy. Connecting learning initiatives to business outcomes or return on investment was the second most-cited challenge for the coming year, named by 35% of respondents. Less than half, 47%, said business outcomes such as revenue growth or profit are among their top three measures of success, while 36% still count course completions among their leading metrics and 26% said distinguishing AI course completions from actual competency is a major challenge. Half of respondents in dedicated Learning and Development roles said course completions are a top metric, compared with 32% of those in broader HR roles who also oversee training. Grassi said businesses are investing in AI upskilling but the big challenge for Learning and Development leaders is proving that what they are doing is working, which means going beyond counting how many people took a course and measuring behaviour changes, skills and competencies instead and linking those to real business outcomes.

Gartner found that 27% of Australian employees fear artificial intelligence will make their skills obsolete, rising to 46.2% among Gen Z workers, based on a survey of 589 employees in Australia. The survey also found that 18.6% of employees are frustrated by how AI has changed their role, while 29.8% worry the technology will make errors that harm their work, and among Gen Z employees those figures rise to 30.8% and 42.3% respectively. Nearly half of Australian employees, 46%, are already expected to use AI in their jobs, and among those workers 90% said their organisation provides AI tools, but only 60.9% said they receive clear guidance on AI use, 54.6% reported formal learning opportunities and 56.9% cited manager support. Jonathan Tabah, Director Analyst at Gartner, said the biggest risk is not the new skills that need to be built but some of the old ones that will disappear, and that unmanaged AI-driven skills atrophy can reduce performance while increasing business risk, yet few organizations have a plan to address it. Gartner said human resources leaders should work with business leaders to identify which declining skills would create the greatest operational, regulatory or performance risks if lost, and that some skills must be retained because they remain essential when technology fails or cannot provide an answer.

At the Fortune 500 Innovation Summit on Tuesday, Mary Culler, president of Ford Philanthropy, said nothing is future-proof but a lot of the skilled trades are jobs that are going to be required to have a human there. She said auto technicians, who are in short supply, could increasingly use AI to help diagnose vehicle problems but still need a human to do the actual manual labor. Carhartt CEO Linda Hubbard said AI-powered efficiency will change how skilled trades workers do their jobs but the industry's labor needs, fueled by the data center boom and broader infrastructure investments, will continue to outpace any productivity gains from the technology. Hubbard said on stage in an interview with Fortune's Kristin Stoller that no matter how good the industry gets at encouraging people, it will always be challenged to get the number of people needed into the trades to rebuild the infrastructure of the country. Employers are expected to fill approximately 1.7 million skilled trades openings annually between now and 2034, but roughly a quarter of the industry's existing 18 million workers are over 55 and nearing retirement.

Maria Flynn, CEO of Jobs for the Future, said there is pushback on the cost of college and on what jobs really require college degrees, and that decades of trade policies and other economic shifts have left some communities with fewer skilled trades opportunities than they once had. Flynn said the industry is having to rebuild trust and awareness and help parents, young people and school counselors understand what the 124 different skilled trades occupations offer and what the paths are into those roles. While 95% of counselors agree trade school is a valuable and credible post-high school option, just 54% say they often recommend vocational or trade school, and only 28% often recommend an apprenticeship, according to a report released earlier this year by the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades. Culler said the perception needs to change and guidance counselors need to start talking about the opportunities. The Alliance's September report found that among every 100 who start an apprenticeship, just 48 complete the program, and only 29 enter a skilled trade occupation within five years of leaving it, while of every 100 entrants to related postsecondary programs, 48 complete their programs and just 34 go on to work in a skilled trade.

Flynn described the problem as pipeline leakiness, which can often come down to a lack of support for workers navigating training programs, including barriers like transportation and childcare, and she said the industry really needs to be working on this together. The General Assembly research found that 57% of leaders expect demand for role-specific AI training to grow, while 56% expect their organisations to expand personalised learning journeys, 55% expect more hands-on training and 52% expect more job-based or role-based training. Gartner said not every fading skill requires intervention, but some must be retained because they remain essential when technology fails or cannot provide an answer. The articles leave open which specific skills organisations will decide can be allowed to atrophy and which they will deliberately safeguard. The articles also leave open how employers will close the gap between the 90% of AI-using Australian workers whose organisations provide tools and the 60.9% who receive clear guidance on AI use.

stories.Headline: Atlassian finds AI code share rises to 70 per cent as review bottlenecks grow
stories.Summary:
The Atlassian AI SDLC Index found that artificial intelligence is rapidly driving down the financial cost of generating software code, according to findings from over 500 organisations via DX. Atlassian released the index, which analysed engineering intelligence data from more than 500 organizations via DX. AI-generated code comprised 49 per cent of total merged code in April 2026, rising sharply to 70 per cent by October 2026, the index noted. By October, AI spend per unit of output dropped by nearly 27 per cent, while code survivorship rebounded by 9 percentage points to reach 68 per cent. The surge in automated code has displaced operational pressure onto human pull request review workflows, which expanded at their fastest month-over-month rate in October.

Engineers continue to spend approximately 58 per cent of their time building new features, a distribution ratio that has remained static for almost two years. An evaluation of 14 workplace dimensions against metrics of speed, quality, and delivery ease revealed that thorough planning processes and robust documentation correlate most strongly with high code quality. Only about 62 per cent of surveyed organisations rate their planning and documentation favourably, indicating upstream disciplines remain underserved. Incident handling earned the highest ratings among engineering teams, indicating that organizations remain far more proficient at reactive response than proactive planning. For several months, engineering departments had to deal with rising costs to generate code while seeing a decline in AI-generated code that is retained in subsequent commits.

Molly Sands, Head of Atlassian's Teamwork Lab, stated that time saved through automation does not automatically result in heightened innovation without deliberate shifts in incentivised activities. Sands emphasizes that time saved through automation does not automatically result in heightened innovation. Without deliberate shifts in the activities that organizations incentivize and reward, engineers naturally reallocate saved time toward processing existing task backlogs rather than pursuing creative breakthroughs. This persistent allocation of time highlights how corporate structures dictate developer focus, according to Sands. Final code quality relies heavily on thorough planning processes and robust documentation, which correlate most strongly with high code quality, according to the report.

Atlassian recommends tracking code survivorship over raw volume, investing in comprehensive specification briefs, enforcing documentation, and establishing structured team experimentation. Tech executives are urged to track code survivorship rather than raw volume output, invest heavily in comprehensive specification briefs, strictly enforce documentation, and establish structured opportunities for team experimentation. The index lays bare the reality that writing code is just one piece of the broader software development life cycle, and that it burdens engineers with greater need to validate code and ensure its quality and security. While these improvements demonstrate that organizations are refining their deployment of AI tools, severe operational bottlenecks persist outside the immediate scope of code generation. Generative AI tools have failed to alter how developers allocate their working hours.

Sessions at NEDCamp 2026 focused on managing AI costs and maintaining control over AI features in Drupal development. Developers should treat cost and control as design inputs from day one. Local models in Chrome can be used in Drupal for drafting, reducing paid service token costs. Atlassian plans to publish updates to the AI SDLC Index quarterly. Atlassian announced it will publish updates to the AI SDLC Index on a quarterly basis, establishing a recurring benchmark for software engineering adaptation. The index demonstrates that final code quality relies heavily on upstream factors within the development life cycle. To extract genuine value from AI investments, Atlassian outlines clear recommendations for enterprise leaders. The study also found weak upstream planning and documentation, rated favorably by only 62 percent of organizations, correlates with lower code quality.

stories.Headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he would return if the board asks
stories.Summary:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said on November 17 that he would return if the board asked him to. The company board dismissed Huang over an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. He resigned under a cloud on November 12, which was five days before his public statement. Huang had previously admitted to the affair and called himself a piece of shit before quitting. This message was his first public communication since leaving the company in Silicon Valley.

Returning as CEO would require the board to judge it as the best option for shareholders and employees. It would also need to be the best choice for the company and the United States. Alice Huang is the woman suspected of being a Chinese spy in this specific affair. The board is not discussing a return, according to reports from The Wall Street Journal. The Financial Times reported that Huang discussed return options with close associates on November 15.

Jensen Huang stated he received numerous requests to return from investors, business partners, customers, and Nvidia employees. He said he would gladly accept a request to return if the board deemed it necessary. The Nvidia board says it is not currently discussing bringing the former chief executive back. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a Fox News interview that Nvidia needs a sweeping overhaul. Bessent insisted that the board should look outside the company to hire a new chief executive.

Elon Musk, the chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, signed an online petition demanding that Huang return. This petition has drawn more than 180,000 signatures from people who want the former leader reinstated. President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he would not mind if Huang returned. Trump also said no one had proven Alice Huang is a spy and she might not be. Employees are affected by a culture where Nvidia has avoided layoffs since the year 1996.

Nvidia staff revere Huang because the company grants restricted stock units broadly to new and senior staff. Huang drove a culture of aggressive AI tool use to raise productivity for his engineers. He believed an engineer earning 500,000 dollars annually should spend 250,000 dollars on tokens. This approach contrasts with Meta and Microsoft, which cut 8,000 and 4,800 jobs respectively. Some staff testify that not a single colleague speaks ill of the chief executive behind his back.

Scott Bessent pressed the board for an answer within 10 days regarding chips smuggled to China. He questioned if Nvidia ignored warnings about a Singapore shell company used for these illegal shipments. A war room of Silicon Valley executives is reportedly being assembled to support a return. The articles leave open whether the board will ever reconsider its decision to dismiss the leader. They also leave the status of the Chinese spying intelligence assessments as an unresolved matter.

stories.Headline: Zoho adds AI agents to Zoho Desk to combine automated tasks with human judgment
stories.Summary:
Zoho launched Blended Agents in its Zoho Desk platform on November 16, 2026, for several global regions. Australia is among the first six regions where this new customer service tool is now available for use. The software allows AI agents to perform tasks across business applications before handing cases to human representatives for judgment. These AI agents differ from standard chatbots because they can execute actions instead of only answering customer questions. Handovers to humans include full conversation history and context so that customers do not have to repeat their information.

The tool is available in Australia, India, the US, the EU, Japan, and China, with Canada launching soon. Blended Agents are included in all paid Zoho Desk plans, including the Express edition, without an added software charge. Users pay for large language model usage, with Zoho hosted models providing up to 30 million free monthly tokens. Automation Studio is available from the Professional edition, while the Workstation tool is available for those using the Enterprise edition. Workstation offers six predefined styles, including Standard, Classic, Modern, Compact, Superior, and Advanced, or a custom drag and drop builder.

CEO Mani Vembu stated that good customer service begins with understanding people through patience, empathy, and understanding a customer's context. He said Blended Agents are a natural extension of the philosophy upon which the Zoho Desk platform was originally built. Vembu explained that AI taking on routine tasks allows human representatives to spend more time on situations requiring empathy. He believes this approach keeps customer service personal while providing teams with the necessary tools to work more efficiently. The company also introduced WhatsApp Co-Existence, in-chat payments, and support for incoming and outgoing WhatsApp calls within the platform.

The launch occurs as companies test how far AI can be used in service without harming overall customer satisfaction. A CHOICE Consumer Pulse survey cited by Zoho found that 51 percent of Australians say AI chatbots make experiences worse. Affected businesses can use the tool to retrieve order details, check stock, and update customer accounts using connected systems. Support staff can pause AI execution to review or approve steps, maintaining manual oversight of tasks affecting the customers. The system can also identify repeated issues to alert teams or flag scheduling conflicts, such as unavailable technicians.

Zoho Desk launched in 2016 and now serves more than 125,000 businesses across 155 countries with a high growth rate. Between 2017 and 2025, the platform recorded a compound annual growth rate of approximately 35.3 percent across its global markets. The largest revenue contributors are India, the US, Continental Europe, and the Middle East and Africa region. Zoho is a privately held company based in Chennai, India, and employs more than 19,000 people across the world. The broader company has more than 150 million users worldwide across hundreds of thousands of different businesses.

Next, businesses can publish knowledge-base articles and community content in Markdown and llms.txt formats for easier access by external AI. Zoho will continue to host data in its own local data centers and will not use it for training. The company maintains a privacy pledge and does not use an ad-revenue model for any of its business products. The articles leave open how many Australian businesses will adopt the tool given the negative views of chatbots. They do not state when the specific launch date for the Canadian market will be officially announced to users.

stories.Headline: US imposes AI chip export rules on five countries causing Singapore data centre stocks to slide
stories.Summary:
The United States imposed new rules on AI chip exports on November 16. These rules caused Singapore data centre REITs and related stocks to slide on November 17. Investors feared that the measures would lead to tighter licensing and weaker regional demand. The news followed the disclosure of an affair between Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. Alice Huang is a former Megaspeed executive suspected by the US of being a Chinese spy.

The rules aim to stop sensitive US technology from being accessed through remote computing in third countries. This adds Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand to a list of countries subject to export restrictions. Companies must now get licences from the US Commerce Department to ship to these five nations. US cloud hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services will receive exemptions from these rules. This creates a two-tier environment with strict licensing for local and non-US operators in Singapore.

The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Digital Development and Information are studying the measure. They are engaging affected companies to understand the potential business impact of the new rules. A Singtel spokesperson said the impact should be minimal because their sovereign AI platform serves Singapore only. Singtel will work with the Singapore Government to obtain necessary licences and clearances for its operations. ST Engineering stated that its existing operations are not impacted because it has the required infrastructure.

Analysts say the sector still has strong demand from cloud computing and artificial intelligence. Ritesh Ganeriwal noted that Singapore REITs own assets well beyond South-east Asia. Charu Chanana warned that operators dependent on Chinese AI customers face the biggest risks. Andy Wong said the direct impact is limited for landlords and infrastructure providers like Keppel DC REIT. Ben Chong noted that exemptions for US-headquartered end users should preserve a channel for investment.

Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia chief executive on November 12, while Alice Huang is believed to be in China. Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud computing provider. Singtel has a 6MW RE:AI platform, with 4MW installed and 2MW contracted. Singtel shares closed 2.5% higher at $4.10, but ST Engineering closed 1.9% down at $8.86. NTT DC REIT fell 0.5%, DigiCore REIT fell 2.2%, and Keppel DC REIT fell nearly 1%.

Authorities will continue to monitor the impact on customers and execute pipelines in a gated manner. Eric Xiao stated that Singapore remains well placed due to land, power, and policy support. The articles leave open how the rules apply to specific customers and their expansion plans. It remains unclear if the rules will lead to delays or cancellations of regional data centre projects. The long-term effect on earnings and the conversion of backlogs into revenue remains uncertain.

stories.Headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following national security concerns and boardroom crisis
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the founding CEO of Nvidia on November 13, 2026, following a boardroom crisis. His departure followed revelations of national security concerns and extramarital affairs involving a Chinese businesswoman. The company's board acted deliberately in the best interest of shareholders, employees, partners, and customers. Interim CEO Colette Kress and Chairman Harvey Jones spoke with investors on November 18, 2026. Huang stated he is willing to return as CEO, but the board does not intend to reinstate him.

The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent CEO suited for national security and semiconductor technologies. Nvidia established a committee to strengthen oversight of export control matters and engagement with United States government agencies. The company announced new supplier agreements with Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Spil, and Kinsus to address shortages of substrates, wafers, and packaging. Nvidia expects CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028 due to demand for the Vera CPU. This demand is driven by CoreWeave, OpenAI, Meta, and Nscale as agentic AI workloads increase.

Interim CEO Colette Kress said agentic AI is driving extraordinary demand for CPUs that far outstrips the available supply. She noted that weekly token volume on OpenRouter surged 35 times year-over-year and 3.5 times in three months. Chairman Harvey Jones stated the board acted in the best interest of the company during this unexpected transition. He declined to answer specific questions about the resignation but confirmed the board will seek a permanent leader. Kress also highlighted that Nvidia compute remains fully utilized across every neocloud and hyperscaler they serve.

Investor Gavin Baker warned that concentrating artificial intelligence within a few proprietary companies risks having only two or three value systems. He argued that a vibrant open-source ecosystem is necessary so companies can own their weights and their own destiny. House Democrats elected Representative Ted Lieu of California as caucus chairman on Wednesday to coordinate priorities for January. Lieu believes failing to regulate AI is freaking insane and is pushing for expanded federal oversight of the technology. This shift affects the ability of Americans to choose AI systems that reflect their own personal beliefs.

Nvidia's Nemotron models and partnerships with independent developers previously threatened to reduce business dependence on OpenAI and Anthropic. A 2015 study by Ronald Robertson and Robert Epstein showed biased search rankings can shift undecided voter preferences by 20 percent. A Media Research Center study found Apple News promoted 60 times more left-leaning stories than right-leaning ones over 12 months. Of 6,849 stories, 4,832 were from left-leaning outlets like The Guardian, The Atlantic, The New York Times, and The Washington Post. Only 81 stories, roughly 1 percent, came from right-leaning outlets such as The Telegraph and the New York Post.

Representative Ted Lieu and Republican Representative Nathaniel Moran of Texas introduced the AI Kill Switch Act to stop catastrophic harm. This bill would authorize the Department of Homeland Security to shut down or slow the operation of powerful AI platforms. Token prices have fallen nearly 60 percent since May, but B300 rental rates have increased by over 60 percent. Hopper GPUs have been recontracted at up to twice their original prices under various multiyear agreements for computing resources. The articles leave open whether AI will expand individual freedom or become a tool for unelected elites to manipulate.

stories.Summary:
Bas Wijne, the CEO of APO Group, released a report on November 16, 2026, regarding artificial intelligence research in African markets. He used data from Africa Newsroom to show what European and American research misses about AI assistants in Africa. On November 18, 2026, Cassava Technologies and Mauritius Telecom signed a memorandum of understanding at the Africa Tech Festival. This strategic partnership focuses on strengthening model access and compute for AI services and education across various African markets. The agreement also explores opportunities for the AI powered education platform called myt Learn in South Africa and elsewhere.

The partnership utilizes Cassava's NVIDIA powered AI Factory in Cape Town, which is the most powerful supercomputer on the continent. It combines Cassava's AI platforms and regional reach with the local language capabilities and operating experience of Mauritius Telecom. The companies will explore on demand computing capacity via the AI Factory and access to models through the CAIMEx platform. These services will complement the existing myt AI Cloud infrastructure in Mauritius and support expansion into other African markets. The partners will also assess myt Learn for South Africa's public and private education sectors before expanding further.

Bas Wijne stated that first impressions of companies often depend on which local websites AI assistants are allowed to read. Ziaad Suleman of Cassava Technologies said that realizing AI's promise requires infrastructure, technology, and proven expertise in Africa. Veemal Gungadin, the CEO of Mauritius Telecom, said the goal is to make trusted AI useful and accessible. He added that the partnership brings together developed products and infrastructure to take their current work much further. Gungadin also emphasized that those responsible for using the AI must retain meaningful control over the technology.

The Reuters Institute found that African markets are driving growth in AI use for news despite being ignored in research. BuzzStream reported that 79 percent of the biggest news sites in the UK and US block at least one crawler. In South Africa, the GIBS Media Leadership Think Tank found that 30 percent of 263 news sites block AI. Zyte found that only 12 to 14 percent of websites in Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, and Nigeria block these crawlers. Publishers who block AI do so because assistants use their journalism, which leads to fewer readers visiting primary sources.

APO Group is a communications consultancy founded in 2007 by Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard that operates across all 54 African markets. Its newswire, Africa Newsroom, reaches over 250 Africa focused news sites and connects with over 450,000 journalists and analysts. AI crawlers visit Africa Newsroom about 200,000 times daily, with Google AI drawing about 62,000 impressions every single month. Microsoft's AI services, including Copilot, name an Africa Newsroom page as a source approximately 16,000 times per month. The consultancy serves clients such as the African Development Bank Group, Africa CDC, Afreximbank, Nestlé, Emirates, Canon, and Western Union.

Bas Wijne will speak in Cape Town alongside Victoria Evdokimova of Yango and Shafee Khan of Microsoft at the festival. He will also join Strini Mudaly of Gold Fields and Sabine Dall’Omo of Siemens Sub-Saharan Africa for this discussion. The companies will continue to monitor how AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and DeepSeek cite their news announcements. They will advise clients on generative engine optimisation to ensure they are found and credited by AI assistants. The articles leave open who will write the content that AI assistants use to form impressions of new companies.
