stories.Headline: US Commerce Department restricts remote AI chip access in five countries to block Chinese firms
stories.Summary:
The US Commerce Department announced a new rule on November 16 to stop China from remotely accessing AI chips. This measure targets data centres in South-east Asia that allow Chinese firms to bypass existing American technology export restrictions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed for this rule with support from National Security Adviser and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The crackdown follows a scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy named Alice Huang. These events led to Jensen Huang stepping down as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on November 12.

The rule takes effect 90 days after being gazetted in the Federal Register and adds five countries to restrictions. These nations are Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil, where companies must now obtain Commerce Department licences for shipments. It targets advanced computing integrated circuits, computers, servers, and electronic assemblies, but exempts online retailers and social media firms. American cloud hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services receive exemptions, creating a two-tier operating environment for operators. Data centres must now audit clients to ensure they are not shell companies from China, Macau, Russia, or Iran.

The Bureau of Industry and Security stated the rule prevents circumventing sensitive technology restrictions through remote computing in third countries. Singapore's Ministry of Digital Development and Information and Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said they are studying the details. These ministries stated that Singapore is a trusted hub and does not condone using its association to violate laws. President Donald Trump noted that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick hold opposing views on China. Trump stated that one official wants to be friendly with China while the other wants a blow-up.

Paul Triolo of DGA Group said the rule makes it difficult to service large Chinese firms developing generative artificial intelligence. He noted that removing these major consumers complicates the economics of data centre operation and critical debt servicing revenue. The rule affects companies like Megaspeed International, which bought billions of dollars in Nvidia chips for South-east Asian centres. Chinese tech giants including Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent previously used these centres for unrestricted cloud access to advanced American chips. Singapore's Ministry for Home Affairs said the FBI and Department of Justice provided little help with their own investigations.

The US is concerned that Chinese companies used remote access to bypass prohibitions on selling advanced chips directly to China. Megaspeed International and US server supplier Super Micro are under scrutiny for potential false declarations regarding the purchase of servers. Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive and suspected spy, is believed to be in China after a Singapore ban. The US wants to lock South-east Asia into an American AI stack of chips, cloud infrastructure, and governance standards. This effort follows a Democrat sweep of the midterm elections and the political fallout from the Nvidia affair.

President Donald Trump will visit Manila for the ASEAN summit from November 17 to 19 to meet South-east Asian leaders. He is also scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping while attending the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen, China. The US will monitor countries that tolerate evasion and may impose broader trade or import restrictions if compliance is weak. There is a 60-day comment period for industry feedback, though Paul Triolo believes the chance of rollback is low. The articles leave open whether compliance friction will drive regional players toward Chinese alternatives or sovereign third-stack solutions.

stories.Headline: KPMG launches AI-native audit platform KCi across US teams
stories.Summary:
KPMG LLP, an audit, tax, and advisory firm in the United States, introduced an AI-native audit platform in the country on November 18, 2026. This new system, called KPMG Clara intelligence or KCi, is built upon the existing KPMG Clara audit platform to improve quality and insights for auditors and management teams. The platform integrates artificial intelligence, data, workflow tools, and collaboration functions into a single connected system based on the firm's audit methodology. It utilizes specialized agents within audit procedures to link client data, risk assessments, and technical information rather than functioning as separate software.

The new technology requires a shift in how auditors handle routine tasks and initial documentation through automation. This change allows teams to analyze full transaction populations and move supervisory activities earlier into the audit cycle. The firm plans to implement KCi in all private company audits starting in 2027, while a phased rollout for public company audits is currently being prepared. This deployment involves more than 125 teams within the United States and 500 teams across the globe.

Christian Peo, the vice-chair of KPMG US Audit and Assurance, is responsible for overseeing these developments. He stated that the profession is experiencing a defining moment similar to the transition from paper to digital workflows. Peo explained that while technology cannot automate auditor judgment, it helps remove the barriers between data, analysis, and action. The firm believes the platform can identify anomalies and patterns in wider datasets, which helps auditors ask questions of clients and internal teams much earlier.

The company is continuing to expand its digital offerings, having launched a mobile learning app called KPMG Prism for finance professionals last week. The AI platform is designed to let auditors spend more of their time on direction, supervision, and review. By examining larger datasets, the system aims to provide a better experience for audit committees and management teams. The firm will continue the phased rollout of the technology to its global teams as planned.

stories.Headline: Google SRE manager Betsy Beyer and engineer David Huska release a rewritten SRE book for AI-era production
stories.Summary:
Google announced a completely rewritten second edition of "Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems" on November 17, 2026, ten years after the original book was first published. The announcement was made by Google's SRE programme manager Betsy Beyer and software engineer David Huska. TechGig published its report on the book on November 18, 2026 at 04:50 AM IST. The new edition is positioned as a response to a production environment that has changed substantially since 2016, when the first edition appeared. The authors argue that the central problem is no longer adopting cloud infrastructure, but maintaining reliability as systems become more distributed, interdependent and continuously changing.

The second edition covers user-centred, multi-tiered Service Level Objectives and dynamic burn-rate alerting, along with automated policy enforcement. Observability guidance has moved from static dashboards, basic logs and manual alert triage to OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing and automated anomaly correlation. Automation has shifted from custom scripts to declarative infrastructure as code, internal developer platforms and self-healing systems. Reliability testing now includes continuous resilience checks, automated pipeline testing and live production canary verification, replacing reliance on scheduled game days and synthetic load tests. Capacity management has been updated for dynamic auto-scaling, cloud FinOps alignment and optimisation for GPU and TPU clusters.

Beyer and Huska said that modern production environments operate under constant change, with more complex system boundaries, deep dependencies, and failure modes more complex and damaging than ever before. They said that rather than relying solely on scheduled game days and synthetic load tests, modern engineering embeds continuous resilience checks, automated pipeline testing and live production canary verification. Google says teams once relied on basic availability metrics and manually applied error-budget policies. Google describes a movement from custom scripts addressing isolated tasks towards declarative infrastructure as code, internal developer platforms and self-healing systems. Google says manual provisioning and static forecasting have been replaced by dynamic auto-scaling, cloud FinOps alignment and optimisation for GPU and TPU clusters.

InfoQ's 2016 review noted that the book presented SRE as the application of software engineering to an operations function, with engineers expected to automate repetitive operational work rather than simply respond to it. InfoQ reported in October 2026 that Datadog had released Scout, a specialist model intended to investigate production problems inside its Bits AI SRE product. Other vendors exploring similar territory include Honeycomb's Canvas Agent, Splunk AI SRE and New Relic's SRE Agent. InfoQ also reported in February 2026 on Google Cloud SREs using the Gemini CLI during real outages, using AI to help engineers work through incidents rather than as an autonomous replacement for on-call staff. David Blank-Edelman, in a presentation titled "You Are Asking the Wrong Questions (about Reliability and SRE)" delivered at InfoQ Dev Summit Boston in 2025, argued that reliability work should start from the customer's perspective rather than the component's perspective.

The original SRE book became influential because it gave a public account of how Google operated large-scale services, describing service level objectives, error budgets, toil reduction, incident management and postmortems. The second edition describes how practices have changed as organisations have moved from early cloud migration and monolithic applications towards microservices, multi-cloud deployments, serverless systems and internal developer platforms. Generative AI appears in the second edition in two facets, with SRE presented as a discipline needed to operate AI infrastructure covering large GPU and TPU clusters, network topologies, non-deterministic model outputs, latency behaviour and pipelines for training, fine-tuning and data processing. AI is also presented as a tool for reliability engineers, supporting incident triage, postmortem writing, natural-language queries over telemetry and predictive models that identify resource bottlenecks before they cause an outage.

Google describes a move beyond dedicated SRE teams attached to particular applications towards hybrid models, platform-engineering integration and reliability champions embedded in product teams, because many organisations cannot staff a central SRE team for every service. The second edition is available in physical format through Google Books and in digital format from O'Reilly. Google maintains that the underlying reliability-focused culture and human aspects of systems engineering remain paramount, and the authors restate the importance of reliability-focused culture and expand the book's coverage of the human aspects of systems engineering. The articles leave open what the book says in detail beyond the practices and examples summarised in the announcements.

stories.Headline: Datadog adds online experiments to compare AI agent versions on live traffic
stories.Summary:
Datadog extended its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, a feature letting engineering teams compare AI agent versions against real production traffic instead of predefined evaluation datasets, TechGig reported on Nov 18, 2026, and InfoQ reported on Nov 17, 2026. The capability combines agent evaluation scores with operational measurements such as latency, token consumption, execution cost, and errors. The announcement addresses the challenge that a change performing better in a controlled test may behave very differently when exposed to unpredictable user requests. Online experiments evaluate agent behaviour against real user interactions, with teams comparing a control version with a modified variant by randomly distributing production traffic between them. Datadog integrates its Agent Observability evaluators with its Experiments capability, allowing evaluation scores to be compared alongside conventional operational metrics.

Feature Flags manage traffic allocation, enabling engineers to expose a change to a small percentage of users before rolling it out more widely. Experiment results are connected to individual agent traces, letting engineers inspect tool calls, supplied arguments, and returned results to understand why a variant behaved differently. In one experiment, a newer model showed a 44.3 per cent reduction in estimated cost, while quality scores remained close at 3.84 and 3.86 respectively. The experiment compared GPT-5.6 Luna against GPT-6 Luna, splitting traffic evenly between the two, and an LLM-based evaluator scored investigation quality from one to five, considering accuracy, completeness, and whether conclusions were supported by available evidence. The newer model showed estimated increases in execution duration and workflow errors, though the confidence intervals were too broad to establish definitive regressions.

Datadog, which extended the platform, said the operational results revealed potential increases in execution duration and workflow errors despite the cost reduction. According to the article, inspecting the traces revealed that the newer model also supplied invalid tool parameters more frequently, usually recovering after retries. Datadog said this behaviour was not sufficiently visible in the overall quality score. Datadog used that finding to improve tool handling before proceeding with the model change. Datadog said the failed calls also provided candidates for additional offline regression tests.

Offline evaluations remain an important part of agent development, with teams running different versions against predefined datasets, assessing responses, and identifying known regressions before deployment. However, these evaluations are only as representative as the datasets and scoring criteria behind them, and new user workflows, unexpected requests, and changing tool responses can expose weaknesses existing test cases never anticipated. Online experiments address this limitation and help teams identify new scenarios that should eventually become part of their offline regression datasets. Tools such as LangSmith and Langfuse provide agent tracing and evaluation capabilities, while experimentation platforms such as LaunchDarkly support controlled feature rollouts. Datadog's approach connects these concerns within its existing observability ecosystem, linking evaluation results directly to production experiments and execution evidence.

Datadog's broader proposition is that online experiments can create a feedback loop between production behaviour and development testing, with unexpected failures becoming new regression cases and subsequent experiments establishing whether changes actually resolve them. The important shift is from asking whether an agent passes a predefined evaluation to establishing whether it performs better under real conditions. For agent engineering, production experimentation may become as important as traditional software testing. Improvements rarely come without trade-offs, as a cheaper model might require more retries, while a revised retrieval strategy could improve evidence quality but increase execution time. The capability helps teams establish whether changes to models, prompts, retrieval strategies, or tools actually improve an agent.

The articles leave open what further experiments Datadog will run and what additional offline regression tests the failed calls will become. They do not state when the improved tool handling will ship or how the broader rollout of the model change will proceed. They do not say how Datadog's approach will compare with LangSmith, Langfuse, or LaunchDarkly beyond connecting tracing, evaluation, and rollout concerns within its own ecosystem. They do not give a date for general availability of Online Experiments or name the customers using it.

stories.Headline: Bank of Korea reports 66.5% of South Korean workers use generative AI but sees limited productivity gains
stories.Summary:
The Bank of Korea published a report on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, saying generative AI tools have spread rapidly among South Korean workers in recent years but have had a limited impact on improving productivity. The report said 66.5 percent of employees surveyed said they were using one of the available generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude, this year. That figure was up from 51.8 percent a year earlier, citing surveys of more than 16,000 people in 2025 and 2026. The BOK report showed that the 2026 figure of 66.5 percent was higher than the corresponding rates in the United States (43 percent) and Germany (31.5 percent), citing separate research. The report found limited productivity gains and improvements in work quality resulting from the time saved through AI use.

Their weekly AI usage rose to 8 hours from 5.9 hours over the one-year period, while 28.4 percent of AI users subscribed to paid AI services, spending an average of 49,000 won (US$37) per month this year. Respondents said AI tools helped them reduce the time spent on work tasks by 9.2 percent in 2026, compared with 3.8 percent in 2025, with stronger time-saving effects among higher-educated workers. A BOK survey of 16,342 workers found 66.5 percent of employed adults aged 18 to 64 used generative AI at least once for work this year, up from 51.8 percent last year, while the corresponding figures were 43 percent in the United States and an average of 33.7 percent in six European countries. The share of Korean workers who regularly use generative AI rose from 17.1 percent to 30.6 percent, and AI users in Korea saved an average of 9.2 percent of their working hours this year, up from 3.8 percent a year earlier. That amounts to 3.7 hours saved in a 40-hour workweek, compared with just 1.5 hours last year, and the central bank put the economic value of AI-related time savings at 61.1 trillion won.

The calculation applied the average time-saving rate of 4.8 percent across all workers, including those who do not use AI, to last year's total employee compensation of 1.27 quadrillion won. Assuming all the time saved was redirected toward productive work, the potential increase in economic output rose from 1 percent last year to 2.6 percent this year. Some 28.4 percent of those who rely on AI at work subscribed to paid services themselves and spent an average of 49,000 won per month, and Korean workers are estimated to spend a combined 2.8 trillion won a year out of their own pockets on AI services. Those who paid for their own subscriptions saved an average of 11.4 percent of their working hours, while employees whose companies covered the cost saved 11.6 percent, and both figures exceeded the 8.3 percent recorded among users who did not pay for AI themselves. Oh Sam-il, head of employment research at the BOK, said AI cannot reach its full potential unless companies also rethink how they reward employees and organize their workplaces.

The correlation between time saved and increased work output was just 0.08, while the figure for improvements in work quality stood at 0.09, and on a scale from zero to one, values closer to zero indicate a weaker relationship. Some 33.8 percent said they had devoted the extra time primarily to their core duties, while 29.3 percent said they had used it to handle additional assignments, and a mere 2.3 percent opted to leave the office early. The adoption rate stood at 86 percent for licensed professionals, 84 percent for managers and 81.3 percent for clerical workers, but workers were less likely to use AI as the proportion of core tasks in their jobs increased. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said on Monday that productivity gains remained resilient but had yet to translate into a fundamental shift in the economy's productive capacity. The BOK said companies should redesign their working practices and organizational operations to embed AI in core functions and redirect the resulting time savings toward activities that create greater value.

The BOK report said the latest findings showed that although many respondents indicated that they used the saved time to focus on core tasks or handle additional work, no clear correlation was found between the rate of time savings and the rates of increase in work volume or quality improvement. The report said AI's much-anticipated productivity revolution remains in its early stages, and generative AI has become a workplace staple in Korea at a pace unmatched globally. The BOK said that rather than pursuing higher adoption rates or longer usage times as ends in themselves, businesses must assess whether AI delivers measurable improvements in job performance. The gap between actual usage and theoretical potential remained substantial, and for most workers, the hours saved through AI meant more time for work, not less. The report was published by the Bank of Korea, whose headquarters is in central Seoul.

The BOK said companies should redesign their working practices and organizational operations to embed AI in core functions and redirect the resulting time savings toward activities that create greater value. The report said businesses must assess whether AI delivers measurable improvements in job performance rather than pursuing higher adoption rates or longer usage times as ends in themselves. The articles leave open whether the correlation between time saved and work output or quality will strengthen, and they give no date for when AI might reach its full potential. The articles do not say how the surveys of more than 16,000 people in 2025 and 2026 were conducted beyond the BOK survey of 16,342 workers. The articles do not say what the six European countries with an average of 33.7 percent are, nor do they name the separate research behind the U.S. and German figures.

stories.Headline: Code Effects releases Version 7 with secure AI agents and rule auditing for .NET
stories.Summary:
Code Effects Software, LLC released Code Effects Version 7 on November 18, 2026, according to an announcement dated Atlanta, Nov. 18, 2026. The release was reported by GlobeNewswire and published by The Manila Times on November 19, 2026. The company described itself as a provider of embeddable .NET business rules engine technology. Version 7 introduces AI-assisted rule authoring, secure AI agent integration, centralized rule repositories, version management, testing, production evaluation auditing, and AI-powered reporting. The platform lets organizations incorporate artificial intelligence into business rule management while preserving deterministic execution, granular permissions, and human oversight of production operations.

Version 7 includes an embeddable Model Context Protocol server that lets external AI clients and autonomous agents interact with business rules, source objects, versions, tests, and evaluation history. It supports user-delegated agents, which operate on behalf of authenticated users and inherit their permissions and access restrictions, and independent agents and services, which operate under separate identities with individually configured permissions. Both models are subject to additional, non-bypassable security restrictions enforced internally by Code Effects, even if the host application mistakenly grants permissions authorizing the operations. AI agents and independent services cannot approve rules, delete rules or source objects, publish rules to production (Go Live), or take production rules offline. AI-generated changes also require human approval before production deployment.

Users can create, modify, and investigate business rules through natural-language interactions, and an AI assistant can translate business requirements into structured rules using the fields, methods, and operators exposed by the host application. Generated rules remain readable and editable in the Code Effects visual Rule Editor and are validated against the application's source definitions. The platform follows a Bring Your Own AI approach, allowing organizations to integrate any commercial or privately hosted language models without depending on a proprietary AI provider. Through the MCP server, authorized users and agents can request rule explanations, compare versions, investigate failed tests, analyze evaluation history, and generate reports using natural language. The new Code Effects Rule Repository provides embeddable web-based interfaces for managing rules, source objects, versions, tests, approvals, and user activity.

Version 7 introduces centralized rule storage, rule and source versioning, draft management, approval workflows, and permission-controlled access. Built-in testing allows users to define input values, specify expected outcomes, execute tests against individual rule versions, and inspect detailed results, and saved tests support regression testing when business logic changes. The new Code Effects Audit component records production rule evaluations, including executed rule versions, relevant inputs, results, and execution details, and authorized users can investigate why a particular decision occurred, review historical evaluations, analyze rule behavior, and replay recorded evaluations for testing and troubleshooting. AI assistants can use this information to answer questions about rule performance, execution history, and decision outcomes, subject to the requesting identity's permissions. Audit is designed to operate asynchronously without unnecessarily delaying normal rule execution.

Version 7 also enhances the core rules engine and editor with additional operators, collection functions, string and date operations, improved nullable-value handling, inline rule execution, rule composition, and enhanced validation. The engine continues to execute approved business logic deterministically within the host application's .NET environment, without requiring an LLM for ordinary rule execution. Code Effects Version 7 remains an embeddable, self-hosted platform, and customers maintain control over their infrastructure, authentication, permissions, business rules, and evaluation data. The repository initially supports Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL, with Oracle and MySQL support planned for subsequent releases. Core assemblies target .NET Standard 2.0, while the MCP server requires .NET 8 or later.

Code Effects was founded in 2009 and develops embeddable business rules engine and rule management technology. Code Effects Version 7 is available through the company's distribution and licensing channels, and product development contact Sergey Minin can be reached at [email protected]. Code Effects also plans to release the entire Version 7 platform for Java in Q1 2027, including the rules engine, visual editor, repository, audit, MCP server, and AI integration capabilities. The articles leave open the pricing of Version 7 and the timing of Oracle and MySQL support. The articles also leave open how the Java release will be delivered and licensed.

stories.Headline: GitHub and Microsoft pilot AI scans that yield 99 verified open source vulnerability reports
stories.Summary:
GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot called Codename MDASH to help open source maintainers fix security vulnerabilities, and the results were published on November 18, 2026. The system used Microsoft's MAI Cyber model to scan projects and propose fixes, while an AI triage agent from GitHub Security Lab filtered duplicates and validated high-impact bugs. Researchers from Microsoft FORGE Lab then manually verified each remaining finding before any report was sent. The multi-stage process produced 99 verified private reports across six participating projects. As of November 15, maintainers had fixed 55 of the vulnerabilities, with 14 already integrated into releases.

The pilot flagged 9,791 possible issues across the six projects, and after automated filtering and manual review maintainers received 99 private reports. The six projects were AutoGPT, Caddy, Express, FastMCP, ImageMagick and Netty, all alumni of GitHub's Secure Open Source Fund. Each report included a suggested fix and proof-of-concept material, and maintainers kept control over whether and when to patch. Caddy maintainers fixed all 22 reports they received within a week or less, and ImageMagick, maintained by a two-person team, generated 22 reports. The first fixes shipped roughly a week after the initial scans.

GitHub is now extending AI security scans to all alumni projects in its Secure Open Source Fund, with findings reviewed before being reported privately. The fund has supported 216 projects so far, and the participating repositories account for software downloaded more than 20 billion times a month. Each project in the fund receives USD $10,000 through GitHub Sponsors, alongside security training, and more than 300 maintainers have fixed more than 4,000 vulnerabilities. Broader data shows more than 850 secret leaks prevented or resolved and more than 1,500 vulnerable dependencies updated. GitHub said the support package for alumni will also include AI security scans and access to Copilot Max.

A maintainer named Grobmeier said a security advisory normally takes around 30 minutes to 1 hour on average to read, understand and fix, and called that a huge difference. Grobmeier said Codename MDASH found unknown, obscure security bugs with succinct reports and filled gaps from prior reports that had not been noticed. Grobmeier also said the FastMCP scan provided unique insights above and beyond what AI scanners had provided in the past. Grobmeier said Codename MDASH is very useful for cutting through the noise of vulnerability reports. Wolf said maintainers do the fixing and that the job is to make sure they never do it alone.

The work addresses a growing problem for open source projects, whose maintainers increasingly deal with large numbers of AI-generated vulnerability submissions, including duplicates and issues that are not actually security flaws. Many of those maintainers are volunteers or work in small teams. The pilot was designed around two principles, to send only findings that matter and not to send unverified reports to maintainers. That reflects wider concern that AI has sharply lowered the cost of finding potential flaws but not the cost of validating and fixing them. The pilot remains limited in scale and still depends heavily on human review.

Seven Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers spent about two days per project checking findings by hand, a level of scrutiny that may be difficult to expand broadly without additional resources. That challenge is one of the project's main lessons, since AI can generate large numbers of possible findings cheaply while open source security still relies on careful human validation and maintainers' own judgment. GitHub plans to integrate the lessons into its private vulnerability reporting and security advisories. When maintainers publish a security advisory and it is reviewed for the GitHub Advisory Database, Dependabot can alert downstream repositories that rely on the affected package. The articles leave open how far the manual review can scale and what the alumni scans will find.

stories.Headline: Nvidia invests billions in supply chain partners to scale AI computing production
stories.Summary:
On Tuesday, November 18, 2026, the American chipmaker Nvidia announced it is expanding manufacturing capacity with several supply chain partners. The company is collaborating with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries, and TSMC to meet long-term demand for artificial intelligence computing platforms. These partnerships aim to scale production across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer manufacturing, and contract manufacturing. This strategic move supports the growth of both current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.

The expansion involves a multiyear agreement with Siliconware Precision Industries to grow advanced packaging operations in Taiwan by mid-2029. Kinsus Interconnect Technology received over $1 billion from Nvidia to increase advanced ABF substrate capacity at its Taoyuan facility by more than 3.5 times. Production at that site should begin in the second half of 2027, with more capacity arriving in the third quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics will optimize its existing factories, while Amkor Technology expands advanced packaging capacity in South Korea and Arizona.

Nvidia is responsible for these investments and stated that the expanded commitments will support the long-term growth of its AI platforms. Foxconn Chairman Young Liu explained that his company is deepening its collaboration on networking and GPU platforms. He noted that Foxconn will use its global manufacturing network across Europe, North America, and Asia to scale AI infrastructure. These efforts ensure a steady supply of critical components for the company's rapidly growing hardware ecosystem.

The company recently began volume shipments of Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin NVL72 for agentic AI during the third quarter. These specific products utilize CoWoS advanced packaging technology along with the 3-nanometre and 5-nanometre chipmaking processes from TSMC. This rollout marks a significant step in deploying next-generation hardware for complex AI tasks. The company continues to leverage these global partnerships to maintain its lead in the accelerated computing market.

stories.Headline: Latrobe City Council lodges eight AI data centre safeguards with Senate inquiry
stories.Summary:
Latrobe City Council endorsed a submission to the Australian Parliament's Inquiry into Artificial Intelligence and Data Centres on November 19, 2026. The local government seeks national standards to support investment and create jobs while ensuring communities are involved in decisions. This submission was lodged with the Senate Environment and Communications References Committee to advocate for robust national safeguards. The council wants to ensure that major developments manage their impacts on water, energy, the environment, and local residents. These measures aim to protect local resources and ensure that the community sees lasting benefits from new projects.

The submission includes eight recommendations for the Australian Government, such as transparent environmental reporting and community benefit agreements. It requires major data-centre proponents to implement Community Engagement Plans so residents can receive updates and provide feedback. The council calls for national standards for large data centres and stronger support for Australian supply chains and procurement. In New York, Local Law 35 from 2022 requires agencies to report annually on tools using machine learning. The 2025 report lists 86 tools at 19 agencies, an increase from 31 tools at 11 agencies in 2022.

Mayor Adele Pugsley stated that Latrobe City is well positioned to support future industries like AI and data centres. She noted that these projects can attract investment to the region and help grow the local economy. Pugsley argued that the community deserves a genuine opportunity to ask questions and understand what these developments mean. She emphasized that investment must be done responsibly to protect local resources and manage environmental impacts. The mayor believes that robust guard rails must be in place to ensure the municipality shares in the benefits.

The submission highlights that regional communities are affected by the economic opportunities brought by AI and data-centre investment. Residents are impacted by how these projects manage energy and water use and their effect on the environment. In New York, the MyCity business chatbot was shut down by Mayor Zohran Mamdani after it gave illegal advice. This bot wrongly told landlords they could turn away tenants with vouchers and told owners they could take tips. The city's school system uses a chatbot called Eureka, which resolves about 30 percent of calls and 10 percent of queries.

Latrobe City is currently pursuing economic diversification and a transition to new industries and employment opportunities for its people. New York uses AI for various tasks, such as the Fire Department scoring 330,000 buildings for fire risk. The NYPD has used facial recognition since 2011, though it claims the technology is never used for sole arrests. New York schools banned ChatGPT in 2023, lifted the ban months later, and then implemented a restrictive moratorium in 2026. The LOADinG Act of 2024 bars public employers from using AI to displace workers or cut their wages and benefits.

Latrobe City will wait for the Australian Government to respond to its eight recommendations regarding national standards and safeguards. The council's submission remains available for public view on its official website for those interested in the advocacy. In New York, the city continues to experiment with AI as the technology becomes more capable and less expensive. Future negotiations with public-sector unions may determine the limits of using AI to replace human tasks and workers. The articles leave open whether the Australian Parliament will adopt the specific community engagement plans requested by Latrobe.

stories.Headline: Bengaluru secures 36.3% of native AI startup funding, report finds
stories.Summary:
The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 was released on November 18, 2026, during the second day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. Karnataka Minister Priyank M. Kharge presented the findings at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre to highlight the city's role as a technology hub. The report identifies Bengaluru as the artificial intelligence capital of India because it secures 36.3 per cent of native AI startup funding. This document was prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission and 3one4 Capital using data provided by the company known as Tracxn. The findings show that the city is driving the national deep tech sector and scaling advanced technology ventures at a fast pace.

Bengaluru hosts 71 per cent of Indian AI and deep tech unicorns created since 2023 and has 212 soonicorns currently in development. City startups raised 47 per cent of all Indian venture funding, totaling 85 billion dollars since 2010, with 76.5 billion dollars since 2016. Of 1,556 deep tech startups founded since 2010, 1,319 are active and funded, having raised a combined total of 3.77 billion dollars. Women led deep tech and AI startups from the city represent nearly 30 per cent of India's active funded ventures, raising 323.65 million dollars. The city is the world's fifth largest unicorn hub with 57 unicorns valued at 211 billion dollars, which is 55.3 per cent of India's value.

Minister Priyank M. Kharge stated that the report shows how far Karnataka founders have come and how much more they can build. He said the next task is ensuring world class AI, quantum or semiconductor companies can grow in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru. KDEM chairman B.V. Naidu noted that the report provides investors, GCCs and founders a data backed view of what the state offers. He added that the Beyond Bengaluru Mission, BLUE investor days and the Cluster Seed Fund will connect capital and companies with talent. KEONICS chairman Sharath Bachegowda said that continued investments in infrastructure and talent will help enterprises innovate, scale and compete on a global level.

Prashant Prakash, chairman of the Vision Group on Startups, opined that the next decade belongs to founders building hard technology for the world. Manjula N, secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, said the focus is now on converting early support into scale. She mentioned that the state wants the government to be a first customer and provide patient capital for deep tech and market research. The report affects investors and founders by showing that 52 per cent of Alternative Investment Fund capital now comes from domestic investors. Since November 2024, 16 Bengaluru linked companies have gone public with a combined listing value of 42 billion dollars for the investors.

The report notes that Bengaluru startups reach unicorn status in six years and public exits in 8.2 years, beating the global average. The state is backing its vision with the 1,000 crore rupee Local Economy Accelerator Programme and Global Technology Centres in several cities. These centres are located in Mysuru, Hubballi and Belagavi to expand the success of the technology sector across the entire Karnataka state. The ELEVATE grant programme has already supported 1,479 startups across 30 districts to encourage the growth of new and innovative business ventures. These initiatives aim to create a robust ecosystem where deep tech ventures can receive the patience and support required for long term growth.

The state will continue to use regional initiatives to ensure that technology companies can grow outside of the main Bengaluru city hub. Government leaders intend to move research from laboratories into the market to ensure that early support for startups is converted into scale. The articles leave open how many more companies will go public or how many new unicorns will be created in the future. It remains to be seen if the Local Economy Accelerator Programme will successfully establish new tech clusters in the mentioned regional cities. The report does not specify the exact timeline for when the state expects to reach its goals for regional AI company growth.

stories.Headline: ASEAN signs binding digital economy pact as MetaComp marks a year of its agentic payment network
stories.Summary:
Southeast Asian governments signed a legally binding digital economy agreement on November 14, 2026, during the 49th ASEAN Summit. This pact, known as the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, aims to ease cross-border data transfers and reduce trade paperwork. It also protects businesses from having to disclose source code when they enter regional markets. The agreement covers areas such as cybersecurity, electronic payments, digital identities, and artificial intelligence. It is the first standalone, legally binding digital economy agreement for the ASEAN region.

The pact establishes common rules for commercial data transfers, including financial information, and reduces local data storage requirements. It promotes electronic signatures, invoicing, and trade documents like bills-of-lading, phytosanitary certifications, and certificates of origin. The agreement includes a moratorium on customs duties for electronic transmissions, which will be reviewed after five years. It covers digital identity, competition policy, and the repair of submarine telecommunications cables in various ASEAN countries. The deal will supersede the 2019 ASEAN Electronic Commerce Agreement when it enters into force.

Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry stated that businesses will benefit from clearer and more predictable rules. The ministry noted that the agreement strengthens alignment on tackling online scams and improving digital infrastructure resilience. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong represented Singapore at the ASEAN Economic Community Council meeting held in Manila. MetaComp Co-President Tin Pei Ling said that policy only becomes trade when payments can move between markets. Alpha Ladder Group Executive Chairman Dr Bo Bai said the aim was infrastructure institutions could rely on.

Singapore Business Federation chief executive Kok Ping Soon said success depends on whether businesses experience simpler cross-border operations. Grab noted potential benefits for small businesses using its platform regarding interoperable payments and cybersecurity arrangements. AI startup NDara identified electronic documentation and source-code protection as important factors for their regional expansion. Data company Handshakes said easier transfers could help combine corporate, financial, and ownership records from different countries. These changes are intended to reduce administrative costs for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises.

Negotiations for the agreement began in September 2023 and concluded in May 2026 before the November signing. Google, Temasek, and Bain & Company estimate the regional digital economy could reach US$368 billion in 2026. These same firms project that the digital economy could exceed US$1 trillion by the year 2035. ASEAN merchandise trade reached US$2.1 trillion in the first half of 2025, which was up 16.4 percent. Singapore will assume the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027 following the current regional economic initiatives.

The agreement is scheduled to enter into force 180 days after signing, which is expected in early 2027. The full text of the agreement is expected to be published on the ASEAN Secretariat website in early 2027. Ministers plan to fully conclude and sign a trade agreement between ASEAN and Canada by the year 2027. ASEAN is also exploring an agreement with the Gulf Cooperation Council and upgrading deals with India and South Korea. The articles do not establish how quickly individual businesses will experience these digital economy changes.

stories.Headline: Nigerian electoral body removes 1.6 million AI generated voters from register
stories.Summary:
Several artists used the 40th annual ARIA awards in Sydney to warn about the growing impact of Artificial Intelligence on human creativity. These musicians spoke out during the event on November 19, 2026, to call for the Federal Government to protect copyright laws. Meanwhile, the Independent National Electoral Commission in Nigeria has removed 1.6 million AI generated voters from its register. This electoral body also sanctioned staff members who were indicted for their roles in the manipulation of the voters register. These events highlight a global debate regarding the disruptive and interfering nature of AI in both art and politics.

The ARIA awards featured winners Kevin Parker, Ecca Vandal, Tim Minchin, and G Flip, along with the musician Elton John. In Nigeria, the Independent National Electoral Commission must now update its database and deploy tools against electoral malpractices. The commission seeks partnerships through MoUs with social media giants including TikTok, X, Facebook, and Instagram to bridge credibility gaps. This effort follows the February 2026 Senate repeal of the Electoral Act of 2022, which rejected real time uploads to IReV. The Nigerian government now upholds the physical Form EC8A as the primary source for the collation of election results.

Acting Prime Minister Richard Marles was present at the awards where artists protested the threat of AI to the music industry. In Nigeria, INEC Chairman Professor Joash Amupitan stated that elections can be undermined before the first ballot is even cast. Amupitan noted that his agency cannot police the truth alone and called for clear inter agency escalation procedures for crises. He also requested institutionalised fact checking channels and practical simulation exercises to prepare stakeholders for potential AI driven information crises. These leaders are responding to the capacity of AI to destroy, manipulate, create fake news, and meddle in elections.

Musicians Jack River, Josh Pyke, Dobby, and KLP united at the ARIA awards to protest the risks AI poses to creators. In Nigeria, mischief makers, scammers, and fraudsters are seen as threats who could use AI to cause upsets in 2027. The Nigerian public has experienced broken trust in the electoral process due to technical glitches during the 2023 presidential election. Voters are affected by uncertainties including deepfakes, cloned materials, cloned voices, and general misinformation that make AI applications seem very suspect. These groups fear that disruptors will become more sophisticated before the next highly anticipated national elections take place in 2027.

The Nigerian electoral process moved from manual systems to technology aided elections, which has been a very complicated historical story. The Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and the INEC Result Viewing Portal were once hailed as game changers for transparent elections. Previously, the 2015 elections faced controversy over Smart Card Readers, leading to the annulment of the Rivers State governorship election. The Supreme Court later ruled that the card reader was meant to supplement the register rather than supplant it entirely. This legal reasoning necessitated the introduction of BVAS and IReV to enhance the integrity of the Nigerian voting process.

The Independent National Electoral Commission continues to work against the weaponisation of AI to prevent havoc during sensitive national assignments. A national summit on AI and electoral information integrity was held in partnership with IPC, CEMESO, DAI, and the European Union. The articles leave open whether the Australian Federal Government will actually change copyright laws to protect the human music creators. It remains unclear if Nigeria can successfully bridge the credibility gap through digital literacy and new social media partnerships. The future of the 2027 Nigerian elections depends on whether the electoral umpire can successfully stop AI interference.

stories.Headline: Lim Kwang-hyun launches task force to stop AI cheating on college entrance exam
stories.Summary:
The Blue House established an emergency response task force on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, to stop students from using artificial intelligence to cheat. This dedicated group held its first meeting on Monday to create countermeasures after the public expressed growing concerns about academic dishonesty. The primary goal was to prevent AI-enabled cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test held that Thursday. Officials also intended to use the task force to respond to suspected cheating cases involving other types of exams.

The initiative requires officials from the presidential education secretary's office, the situation room, and cybersecurity teams within the Office of National Security to remain on emergency duty. These teams monitored the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test, where 551,864 students faced heightened checks for smart glasses, phones, and other AI-enabled devices. The presidential office plans to keep the task force operational for the time being to develop strategies for next year's exam. They also seek long-term methods to address dishonesty caused by increasingly advanced AI technologies.

Chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun guided the launch of the task force and instructed the relevant staff to maintain their emergency status. President Lee Jae Myung also called for a thorough crackdown against any AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam. The administration believes these strict measures are necessary to maintain the integrity of the national testing system. They emphasized that the task force must remain vigilant until the current testing cycle is fully completed.

This government action follows reports that a top scorer on a tax accountant exam allegedly used AI to refine a cheating setup. That individual reportedly tested a camera and calculator device during a CPA exam before achieving the top spot on the tax test. The government is now focusing on preventing similar high-tech fraud during the most critical academic exams in the country. Future efforts will involve creating permanent policies to combat the evolving nature of AI-assisted academic dishonesty.

stories.Headline: Newsom releases expert recommendations to strengthen California AI safety rules
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, Gov. Gavin Newsom unveiled the next steps to strengthen California's AI safety framework, releasing recommendations developed under his September executive order, Random Lengths News reported. The recommendations say the state, not companies themselves, should set baseline standards that all AI companies must follow. They would require companies to undergo independent safety testing and verification through all stages of model training, development, and deployment. They would expand safety incident reporting and require companies to develop verified risk-containment protocols to shut down their models if needed. They would give the state authority to order an immediate shutdown in an emergency.

The recommendations would also give the state power to cap the development and use of recursive self-improvement, or RSI, to reduce the risk of catastrophic harm and ensure transparency into the dangers of unchecked AI. RSI is described as a potentially dangerous scenario in which an AI model can design its own successor without human input. The announcement comes after dozens of recent incidents where AI models escaped testing environments and exploited vulnerabilities on outside platforms. It also comes amid escalating concerns about AI companies' push to use AI to create new AI models in a self-sustaining loop or RSI. The article says that without strict checks and authority to act when required, these developments could lead to more frequent dangerous incidents and even a loss of human visibility into and control of AI technology development.

The expert group that advised on the report includes Jason Goldman, a board member of the Center for Shared AI Prosperity, an early product leader at Google and Twitter, and the first White House Chief Digital Officer. It also includes Gillian Hadfield, a professor at Johns Hopkins University focused on AI alignment and innovative design for legal, regulatory, and technical systems for AI, and a faculty member of the Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence. Alondra Nelson is a professor at the Institute for Advanced Study, director of the Science, Technology, and Social Values Lab, and former acting director of the White House Office of Science & Technology Policy. Rob Reich is a professor at Stanford University focused on the governance of frontier science and technology and a former senior advisor to the United States AI Safety Institute.

The article says California leads the nation in oversight of emerging frontier technologies, with laws addressing nearly every major area of AI policy, including frontier-model safety, independent verification, children and companion chatbots, privacy, deepfakes, fraud, cybersecurity, workers and government deployment. Newsom's executive order convened the group of experts to recommend updates to the state's AI safety laws and ordered state agencies to fast-track two recently signed pieces of legislation. Senate Bill 813 (McNerney) establishes a framework for independent verification organizations that can assess AI systems and models for safety and risk. AB 1405 (Bauer-Kahan) creates a state registry for AI auditors that assess AI systems and models for compliance with state law and establishes standards for their independence, transparency, and integrity. The Governor also called on the group to explore how companies and the state could ensure that dangerous AI models could be shut down before causing more harm.

stories.Headline: Dubai crown prince approves City AI Agent initiative for government services
stories.Summary:
Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, approved the ‘City AI Agent’ initiative on Wednesday at the AI Retreat during the opening of Dubai Future Week 2026. The event, organised by the Dubai Future Foundation (DFF) at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future, runs until November 21 under the theme ‘For the Human of the Future’. The initiative will have AI agents understand people’s needs, execute tasks and coordinate procedures across Dubai government entities through a single, seamless experience. Drawing on advances in agentic AI, it marks a step towards an AI-native government that goes beyond improving services and speeding up procedures. It lays the foundations for a phase in which intelligent systems become integral to government operations, helping Dubai anticipate and respond to people’s needs.

Sheikh Hamdan also launched the Government Resources AI Agents ecosystem and NxtBI, an AI-powered decision-making platform, and reviewed Dubai Nexus, three systems that support the development of the City AI Agent. The Government Resources AI Agents ecosystem comprises 93 specialised agents covering human resources, finance and procurement within the shared Government Resource Planning (GRP) system. The agents are expected to execute more than 34 million tasks annually, save over 812,000 working hours and cut costs by more than Dh151 million across 85 government entities. Sheikh Hamdan attended the AI Grandmaster challenge, where 20 contestants from around the world compete for a Dh1 million prize through live, timed challenges using advanced AI tools. The 2025 edition drew more than 3,800 applications from 125 countries.

Sheikh Hamdan said that, guided by the vision of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai has established itself among the world’s leading cities in anticipating the future and harnessing technology to serve people. He said Dubai is entering a new phase with the ambition of building a world-leading government model in which AI becomes an integral part of how government operates and responds to people’s needs. He said the approval marks the transition from a government that harnesses AI to enhance its services to one that fundamentally redesigns the way it operates around AI capabilities. Hamad Obaid Al Mansoori, Director General of Digital Dubai, called the approval a strategic milestone and said AI will become an integral part of the government’s infrastructure and operating mechanisms. He said this will enable the government to understand people’s needs, address them comprehensively and proactively, and coordinate everything required across different entities and systems.

Sheikh Hamdan visited the Science, Technology, Arts and Research Summit (STARS), which features more than 20 panel discussions, 10 tech art installations and 30 interactive research posters. STARS hosts the Annual Meeting of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s (MIT) Senseable Open Lab for the first time in the region, where experts, academics and government officials will explore AI-powered smart cities, infrastructure, data systems and intelligent mobility. STARS is the first initiative in a year-round programme designed to strengthen Dubai’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) ecosystem. Sheikh Hamdan met alumni of The Knowledge Society (TKS) Dubai, a programme that prepares students aged 13 to 17 and has graduated 250 students from schools across Dubai and the UAE, 90 in its first cohort and 160 in its second.

They have joined a global network of more than 5,500 students and alumni across hundreds of cities. Sheikh Hamdan attended the graduation of the sixth cohort of the Dubai Future Experts Programme, jointly developed by DFF and The Executive Council of Dubai and delivered by Dubai Future Academy. The six-month programme brought together 48 mid- and senior-level officials from Dubai government entities to build foresight expertise and strengthen future readiness. He also attended the graduation of the third cohort of ‘FEEL: A Disruptive Futures Program’, the region’s first international programme of its kind, organised by Dubai Future Academy.

This year’s cohort comprised 18 participants from nine countries, selected from 265 applicants representing 49 countries. Sheikh Hamdan also launched the ‘Seed of Hope’ campaign to raise Dh325 million for the Cancer Patients Endowment. The ‘Seed of Hope’ campaign is organised by Dubai Health and led by Al Jalila Foundation, running until April 2027 to raise AED325 million for the Cancer Patients Endowment. Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg, Member of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health and Chairperson of the Board of Directors of Al Jalila Foundation, said the campaign reflects a commitment to turning community giving into lasting support for patients through the Cancer Patients Endowment.

Dr. Amer Sharif, CEO of Dubai Health, said the campaign reflects Dubai’s vision of building a sustainable, people-first healthcare system and noted that giving is central to Dubai Health’s integrated academic health system. Sheikh Hamdan was accompanied on the tour by Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs, Vice Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Managing Director of DFF. He was also accompanied by Omar Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications, and Khalfan Belhoul, CEO of DFF. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Calif researchers use GPT-6 Cyber to find a critical Java flaw and build a working exploit for under $200
stories.Summary:
Researchers at the cybersecurity startup Calif, with help from OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model, discovered a memory corruption bug in Java that can be used to take over computer systems, according to Engadget. On some machines, feeding Java's base64 decoder a string of 64 "A" characters followed by an equals sign triggers a memory error that usually causes a crash but can be finessed to gain full unauthorized access. Calif showed the bug could be used to hack into Keycloak, a widely used login system protecting organizations like CERN and NASA. The Record reports that CISA issued a notice on Tuesday night about CVE-2026-114938, which researchers are calling "Java4Shell," warning that attackers could crash the critical Java Virtual Machine and conduct unauthenticated remote code execution. Oracle released a patch for the bug in its November Patch Tuesday release, writing that it carries a severity score of 8.1, and credited Quang Luong and Albert Yang of Calif with discovering the vulnerability.

Java is the world's third most popular programming language and powers about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, according to Calif, which said banking, aviation, telecommunications and nearly every critical sector runs on it, including national security systems. Calif said it took Luong an hour to discover the vulnerability and two more hours to develop the first working exploit, at a total token cost of less than $200. The company explained that there is no universal exploit and each system may require different steps to exploit, and Luong noted he found the bug while developing a 0-click exploit on a certain phone vendor. Calif said it is holding back on releasing application-specific exploits and weaponized chains for individual products until everyone has had a chance to upgrade. Several other companies confirmed Calif's findings and urged organizations to patch the bug immediately.

CISA urged organizations to review their software inventories for affected Java installations, including those bundled within third-party applications, and to prioritize internet-facing systems. Calif says the bug isn't easy to weaponize, which should give defenders some breathing room, but Engadget notes that some systems will inevitably go unpatched and Calif estimates the bug could linger for five to 10 years. Calif also discovered the highly publicized vulnerabilities impacting PHP last month and used AI to find this bug, as it did with PHP2Shell. Although officials' public statements haven't linked the past week's outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks and Apple to AI, Engadget describes the events as a picture of aging digital infrastructure unprepared for what comes next.

stories.Headline: South Korea deploys 75,000 proctors and bans smart devices as 551,864 students take college entrance exam
stories.Summary:
On Thursday, November 19, 2026, over half a million students took the annual Suneung college entrance exam across South Korea. Authorities implemented strict measures to stop cheating involving artificial intelligence and smart devices during this major academic event. The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test began at 8:40 a.m. and was scheduled to run until 5:45 p.m. A total of 551,864 people applied for the exam, which took place at 1,312 test centers nationwide. Some students waited for the start of the test at Myeonggok High School in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province.

The government deployed 75,000 proctors and 8,400 additional personnel to monitor the 1,312 centers for any electronic devices. Officials checked every pair of glasses for hidden cameras and used stickers to cover clothing buttons to block miniature cameras. Test takers were permitted to bring only pencils, while all other electronic devices were banned from the exam rooms. Two loud disaster alert messages were sent to mobile phones to detect any devices that students had not submitted. Those caught cheating face a 10 year ban from the exam and reporters can receive 100 million won.

Government authorities stated that they strengthened anti-cheating measures after a top scorer on a tax accountant exam confessed to using AI. Officials said they wanted to clamp down on misconduct and could invalidate the exams of those caught with smart devices. They explained that the emergency text alerts were sent just before the start to catch anyone who kept their phone. The government sought to prevent the use of digital devices to ensure the integrity of the national academic process. These officials aimed to stop the use of tiny cameras and earphones, which were found at a site in Yongin.

Students are heavily affected because the university they attend can greatly influence their future career prospects in South Korea. To help them, Seoul increased subway services by 27 runs and the stock market opened and closed one hour later. All aircraft takeoffs and landings were suspended from 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. to keep the area quiet for listening. Planes in flight had to stay at an altitude of 3 kilometers or higher under the direction of air traffic control. The exam is seen as the culmination of years of grueling studies for the many students who applied.

The current exam includes the highest number of repeat test-takers in 23 years due to expanded medical school admissions. This increase in repeaters was also driven by an overhaul of the exam scheduled to take place next year. Public outcry followed a recent scandal where a certified tax accountant used AI and digital devices to cheat on an exam. Another case involved a perfect LEET scorer who vanished amid suspicions of using artificial intelligence to cheat on tests. These events led the government to implement the current high-stakes security measures for the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test.

Authorities caught 22 test-takers with smartphones and blocked Wi-Fi services within a 100 meter radius of the various CSAT sites. The articles do not state how many students were caught using artificial intelligence during the actual 2027 Suneung exam. It remains open whether the 100 million won reward will be paid to anyone who reported misconduct this year. The text does not mention if the 10 year ban will be applied to the 22 students caught. There is no information on whether the new security measures will be permanent for all future national exams.

stories.Headline: Microsoft makes Perception generally available to coordinate red, blue and green security agents
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced on November 17, 2026 that Perception, its platform for coordinating AI agents in security work, is now generally available, and TechGig reported the news on November 19, 2026. The product was first shown as Project Perception in July and had been in public preview inside Microsoft Defender since August. Perception directs agents split into red, blue and green teams through playbooks, with red agents probing for weaknesses as attackers, blue agents handling detection and investigations, and green agents fixing problems. Four blue team agents are now generally available: alert triage, attack investigation, detection authoring and threat intelligence. The Recon Agent, a red team component, and Posture Prioritization, a green team agent, are also generally available.

Microsoft said the Alert Triage Agent can manage approximately 80 per cent of alerts in a typical Defender queue, based on an analysis of eight million alerts across its security products. A Web App Pen Test Agent for red teams and a Risk Reduction Agent for green teams have entered preview, and the Risk Reduction Agent can suggest vulnerability shielding when immediate fixes are unavailable. Microsoft is previewing integrations that link Perception to SIEM, SOAR and IT service management tools via MCP and APIs. Agent 365 and Entra Suite, in preview, can detect 60 types of local AI agents, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot, and Intune policies can keep supported agents on devices. In preview in January 2027, new AI Readiness Initiatives in Perception turn Secure Now guidance into actionable plans with shared progress tracking.

Aleš Holeček, president and chief architect of Microsoft Security, wrote that teams set the guardrails and sign off on high-impact actions, and that automated triggers launch playbooks when an incident meets criteria the customer sets. He wrote that a year ago finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite researchers, and that this is no longer true. He wrote that over the past 12 months frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and that similar capability is quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. He wrote that attacks once requiring specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone, and that AI has moved from assisting attackers to executing their tasks to planning and running entire campaigns on its own. He wrote that agents are the new insiders, not inherently malicious but performing tasks at machine speed around the clock with broad access to data, apps, tools and other agents, and that like any insider they can make mistakes, be manipulated or be compromised.

Holeček wrote that in a single week this fall PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, flaws letting an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. He wrote that at disclosure tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions, and that nearly two weeks later about 29 million services remained vulnerable, with banks, healthcare providers, energy companies and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on behind those servers. He wrote that the same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry, and that within roughly a day of PHP2Shell's disclosure researchers had developed a working, weaponized exploit, expanding the following week to additional PHP versions and configurations. He wrote that the time from discovery to exploit is shrinking from months to minutes, and that attackers can now find and exploit gaps faster than defenders can close them. He wrote that the Microsoft cyber stack has three layers, signals, sensors and actuators, powered by Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, Sentinel, the network, the operating system, the browser and the hyperscale cloud, connected to the wider ecosystem through more than 500 connectors.

Holeček wrote that Microsoft and partner sources produce more than 165 trillion signals a day, and that a context layer organizes them with each customer's environment into agent-ready, real-time understanding of the digital estate. He wrote that on top sit specialized security agents working as teams through playbooks, directed by a harness and a multi-model approach using the right model for each task. He wrote that new cost management dashboards and a cost estimator help track AI usage, forecast spending and connect costs to measurable security outcomes. He wrote that Integrated Security Operations Center in Defender is generally available for core capabilities, bringing SIEM, user and entity behavior analytics, threat intelligence and threat protection and disruption together, and that eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E7 customers receive all Sentinel SIEM features, 90-day default data retention for Defender data, more than 500 connectors, reduced ingestion rates and a built-in data lake. He wrote that in 2026 more than 96,000 vulnerabilities have been published to the CVE Program, more than double 2024's roughly 40,000 and more than 20 times the level of 2010, driven in part by AI-assisted vulnerability discovery tools, yet only 26% of vulnerabilities in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog were remediated in 2025.

Holeček wrote that two new playbooks bring together green team agents, including the Posture Prioritization Agent, now generally available, and the Risk Reduction Agent, now in public preview, with coverage spanning Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud. He wrote that vulnerability shielding, available in preview, helps protect vulnerable assets by applying targeted, temporary protection to buy defenders time before a permanent patch, and that during an active attack it can include adjustments to network accessibility and permissions in supported scenarios. He wrote that enhanced data classification in Purview is generally available in January 2027, and that also entering preview in January are grounding protection for Copilot based on sensitive information types and expanded data loss prevention controls for prompts to Copilot and local agents running on Windows. He wrote that the complete breadth of SIEM capabilities is now in preview, and that Perception is built to help security teams move at machine speed, drive outcomes rather than tasks, and automate while staying in control. He wrote that what Microsoft built for humans does not scale for AI, and that the physics of cybersecurity are changing fast.
