stories.Summary:
A class action lawsuit over memory price manipulation will proceed after Judge Noel Wise of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California dismissed the joint motion to dismiss filed by Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron on November 14. The ruling, a 20-page document, rejected the three manufacturers' attempt to end the case. The lawsuit was first filed on June 25 this year. Mark Garciagire, an ordinary consumer living in Pasadena, California, joined 16 other plaintiffs and entrusted the boutique law firm Bathaee Dunne to sue the three major memory manufacturers in federal court. The 17 plaintiffs include ordinary consumers who buy RAM modules from Amazon and Micro Center, as well as small distributors such as PC assembly stores in Florida.

The three parties must submit an official response before December 7 and are required to hand over internal production capacity schedules, executive correspondence and meeting minutes during the subsequent discovery phase. The plaintiffs accuse the three giants of colluding to control production since October 2022, leading to a 697% surge in the price of regular DRAM contracts within 18 months. They presented shopping receipts in the 118-page indictment. The three companies together hold over 91% of the global DRAM market share. This is the first time in DRAM history that a class action lawsuit over price hikes during the AI cycle has crossed the motion to dismiss stage and entered the evidence discovery phase.

Judge Wise became a federal prosecutor through the U.S. Department of Justice's Honors Program in her early years and later spent ten years presiding over complex civil litigation trials in California courts. In response to the claim that the old case would repeat itself, she only replied: "This court does not think so." Facing the defense lawyers' "eagles watching each other" theory, Judge Wise refuted along the same metaphor: in nature, eagles may watch each other when hunting, but they will never fly together in a neat formation. She dismissed the motion to dismiss because the plaintiff presented "additional factors" sufficient to meet the threshold at this stage. The plaintiff's lawyer Brian Dunne's team was also prepared early.

The defense lawyers referred to the period from the end of 2022 to the beginning of 2023 as the "DRAM Winter". In the first quarter of 2023, Samsung's semiconductor division suffered a huge loss of 3.51 billion U.S. dollars, SK Hynix lost 2.61 billion U.S. dollars, and Micron posted a net loss of 5.833 billion U.S. dollars for the entire 2023 fiscal year. The lawyers argued that production cuts were for self-rescue, and shifting production to HBM was to chase the AI trend. They cited the Chicago School's "oligopoly interdependence theory", which successfully convinced judges in a similar lawsuit back in 2018. The plaintiff pointed out that on October 26, 2022, SK Hynix took the lead in cutting DRAM production capacity, and only three weeks later, Micron followed suit immediately.

In January 2023, Samsung executives even publicly stated that "we will never artificially reduce production of memory chips", but on April 7, 2023, Samsung suddenly made a 180-degree turn and joined the production cut camp. According to TrendForce's calculation, by the first quarter of 2026, the output value of a single wafer for DDR5 64GB RDIMM has surpassed that of HBM, and its profit margin is also higher than HBM. In the third quarter of this year, the global total DRAM revenue soared to nearly 200 billion U.S. dollars, a year-on-year surge of 369%, but the actual total shipment capacity of the entire industry only increased by 4%. The lawsuit revealed that Samsung and SK Hynix forcibly raised the price of server memory sold to Google and Microsoft by 60% to 70% within one quarter, and refused to sign long-term multi-year contracts. By the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, Micron's single-quarter revenue surged to 54.23 billion U.S. dollars, and its Non-GAAP gross profit margin soared to 87%, surpassing NVIDIA in one go; its full fiscal year net profit reached 84.97 billion U.S. dollars.

In the second quarter of 2025, the three parties all shut down or significantly cut the production lines of low-cost DDR4 for regular PCs; Samsung and Hynix also simultaneously stopped selling old DRAM manufacturing equipment to the second-hand market. On December 3, 2025, when consumer-grade memory prices hit a record high, Micron suddenly announced the shutdown of Crucial, its well-known consumer brand that had been in operation for 29 years. By January 2026, the three parties launched almost identical "customer review mechanisms" in the same month, using nearly copy-pasted questionnaires to interrogate distributors and OEMs. Apple CEO Tim Cook publicly complai More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia outlines AI-defined model for chip fabrication using simulation and digital twins
stories.Summary:
Nvidia outlined what it calls an AI-defined model for semiconductor fabrication on 17 November 2026, combining accelerated computing, physics-based AI, AI agents and digital twins. The company said the approach focuses on using AI tools to shorten engineering analysis in chip manufacturing, where assessing process changes, materials interactions and defects can take days. It noted that physical experiments on production lines are costly, and that manufacturers face rising demand for advanced chips and increasingly complex processes. Nvidia said even small errors in yield or process quality can have significant commercial consequences in that environment.

The model relies on faster simulation so engineers can test more alternatives before deciding which changes to try in physical production. Software provider COMSOL is using Nvidia's cuDSS library to speed up semiconductor manufacturing simulations by up to 10 times, and Applied Materials is working with Nvidia on atomic-scale materials discovery and process development. Nvidia said Applied's Ginestra platform runs up to 10 times faster than CPU-only approaches with cuDSS, while its ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35 times faster with Nvidia PhysicsNeMo. Siemens is integrating Nvidia cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, which Nvidia said delivers up to 17 times acceleration on key simulation workloads.

Nvidia also cited Lam Research, which it said has shown that the PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behaviour in milliseconds compared with days for a full simulation. Nvidia said engineers still make the decisions in semiconductor production, but many intermediate steps can consume hours, and it highlighted AI agents as a way to automate sequences of tasks traditionally handled manually. It said Advantest is using Nvidia NeMo Switchyard AI agents to automate the selection of which AI model to apply to a particular task, cutting response times from hours to minutes. Applied Materials uses Nvidia Omniverse libraries to build physically accurate digital twins of entire fabrication plants, according to Nvidia, and those models simulate material movement, identify bottlenecks and assess layouts, throughput, cost and process control.

Nvidia argued that these technologies become more useful when linked in a closed engineering loop, where production data informs simulations and AI models that are then used to test alternatives before engineers decide on the factory floor. Nvidia presented the closed loop as a way to shorten feedback cycles across semiconductor manufacturing, helping engineers identify problems earlier, evaluate more options and act on production insights sooner. The push comes as chipmakers and their suppliers look for ways to manage greater process complexity without relying solely on slower, more expensive physical trials. Nvidia said the aim is to extend simulation beyond individual manufacturing steps to the operation of the factory as a whole, which it said is increasingly relevant as fabrication plants become more complex and the cost of unsuccessful process changes rises.

stories.Headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion Series C to advance its AI drug design engine
stories.Summary:
Isomorphic Labs, the UK-based AI drug research company founded by Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis, announced on November 17, 2026 that it had completed a $5 billion Series C financing round, equivalent to about 33.3 billion yuan, which was oversubscribed. The round was jointly led by Greenoaks and HSG (Sequoia Capital), with participation from a16z and multiple new investors, while Alphabet continued to make large-scale investments. All existing investors also took part, including Thrive Capital, MGX, GV, CapitalG, Temasek and the UK Sovereign AI Fund. According to the article, the round refreshed the company's previous single-round financing record and may set a new global record for single-round financing in the AI pharmaceutical sector. The financing brings Isomorphic Labs' total publicly disclosed funding to $7.7 billion, about 51.3 billion yuan, after a $600 million first external round in March 2025 and a $2.1 billion Series B in May of that year.

The company, founded in 2021 and headquartered in London, plans to use the new funds to upgrade its proprietary drug design engine IsoDDE, expand its self-developed and partnered drug candidate pipelines, and build a globally AI-driven bioengineering infrastructure. It said positive preclinical results have been achieved in its internal oncology and immunology projects and in cooperative projects, and that preparations are underway to advance them into clinical trials. The article adds that the use of the financing has extended from model research to drug pipelines, translational research and clinical development infrastructure. Hassabis, who is founder and CEO of Isomorphic Labs, co-founder and Chairman of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, and who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for protein structure prediction work with AlphaFold, said the team believed at founding that biology could be understood and modeled at the most fundamental molecular level and that AI could significantly accelerate this process. He said the company's drug design engine is generating molecules with higher precision and speed, and that the financing will help the team build fundamental biological models, deepen understanding of disease mechanisms and push the first batch of therapeutic projects to clinical trials.

Max Jaderberg, the company's President since January 2026, who holds a doctorate from the University of Oxford and previously led the DeepMind Open Learning Research Team and served as Chief AI Officer, said the team achieves reproducible scientific progress with models every week and converts it into better molecular properties. Isomorphic Labs was incubated by Google DeepMind and operates independently under Alphabet for external financing, and its core technology is the IsoDDE engine, which integrates fundamental simulated AI models covering multiple therapeutic areas and drug types and is described as exploring the vast chemical space to help design, optimize and screen molecules with ideal druggable properties. The company has also developed proprietary Agents for exploring complex biological systems and conducting reasoning, and says the combination of its models and Agents has driven progress across multiple candidate drug pipelines. After this round, the company will continue to improve IsoDDE, explore new biological fields with more advanced models, build a partner ecosystem and construct a scalable, AI-centered translational research and clinical development system. The article notes that most of the company's major achievements remain in the preclinical stage, and that as the first projects advance to clinical trials, the safety, effectiveness and development progress of its candidate drugs will become an important basis for verifying AI drug design capabilities.

stories.Headline: China fines AI virtual human operator for fabricating product usage experiences
stories.Summary:
The Market Regulation Bureau of Panyu District in Guangzhou issued a penalty on November 13, 2026. This agency fined Guangzhou Wode Film and Television Media Co., Ltd. over 68,200 yuan for illegal medical advertisements. The penalty was publicly disclosed on November 16, 2026, targeting the operator of the virtual character Fang Taozi. This case marks the first penalty in China for AI virtual humans fabricating product usage experiences. The fine targets a 60-second ad for Nuts Power cosmetic contact lenses, which are Class III medical devices.

The AI character claimed the lenses were comfortable for a whole day and did not shift when blinking. Regulations require such ads to be reviewed and clearly mark that users should read manuals or seek medical guidance. Additionally, the law prohibits using advertising spokespersons for recommendation or certification of these specific medical devices. The Market Regulation Bureau classified the act as the illegal publishing of medical advertisements and false advertising. Officials stated the penalty targets the fabricated content and publishing procedure rather than the identity of the on-camera presence.

They argued that while AI is not a legal spokesperson, it cannot bypass the bottom line of authenticity. The core issue is the fabrication of fictitious personal product usage experiences by a digital image. Netizens questioned how a digital image with no eyeballs or corneas could know if lenses were comfortable. Viewers in the comment section realized that the AI had no eyes to experience the product. This case affects the AI digital human track, specifically those providing realistic human-like experience product recommendations.

High-risk categories like medical devices and pharmaceuticals now face a greatly compressed commercial order space. Fang Taozi gained 400,000 followers in one month after the June 12, 2026, launch of the series The Laid-off Girl. The operator, established in September 2019, registered 192 art work copyrights including Fang Taozi and Zhou Yiheng since July. The account's short video quotations started from 168,000 yuan, which is more expensive than many bloggers with millions of followers.

The industry will now divide into brand image broadcasting and realistic human-like experience product recommendation. AI can still broadcast parameters and read brand propositions, but it cannot output first-person physical experience testimony. Future boundaries include five prohibited actions: wearing, eating, applying, using, and smelling. The articles leave open how beauty, food, and home furnishing categories will adapt to these rules.

stories.Headline: Nvidia reports record quarterly revenue of 115.8 billion dollars under interim CEO Colette Kress
stories.Summary:
Nvidia released its third quarter fiscal year 2027 financial results in the early hours of November 18, Beijing time. Interim CEO Colette Kress led the company during this period following the sudden departure of founder Jensen Huang. The company reported record quarterly revenue of 115.8 billion US dollars, which is a 103 percent year-on-year increase. Net profit reached an all-time high of 65.3 billion US dollars, representing a 105 percent year-on-year increase. Data center business revenue hit 107.6 billion US dollars, accounting for 93 percent of the total revenue.

Revenue from Hong Kong and mainland China reached 11.05 billion US dollars, which is a 272 percent year-on-year increase. Nvidia does not include Chinese data center computing revenue in its financial guidance for the next quarter. The board of directors established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to manage global trade risk. On November 16, the US Department of Commerce issued regulations supervising remote access to AI chips in third countries. These rules extend restrictions on Chinese computing power from physical chip exports to overseas computing services.

Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones stated the board has no intention of restoring Jensen Huang to his position as CEO. He also refused to accept questions from analysts regarding the return of the former chief executive officer. Jensen Huang publicly stated he is willing to return to lead the company if the board invites him. The company is moving from personal mediation by Huang to an institutionalized board level oversight structure. This change follows the dismantling of the previous relationship model between Washington and global customers.

Cloud vendors and AI enterprises in China are now accelerating the adaptation of domestic GPUs to ensure supply. Some small and medium model companies are contacting Southeast Asian computing power lessors to lock in resources. A cloud vendor salesperson noted that computing power shortages make business easier for those holding existing stock. Other industry insiders believe that some local subsidy projects now require domestic GPU proportions to exceed 80 percent. US cloud service providers and chip manufacturing enterprises tied to Nvidia saw their stock prices drop sharply.

Nvidia built a huge industrial network spanning cloud computing, chip manufacturing, and AI model companies over several years. The company recently took stakes in Marvell, Synopsys, and Intel while investing billions of dollars in optical communications. In February, Zhipu GLM-5 adapted to Moore Threads, Cambricon, and Huawei Ascend chips to expand the software ecosystem. By September, Huawei Ascend entered the official PyTorch support system to move beyond single model adaptation. These shifts occur as the market reprices for a post Jensen Huang era.

Nvidia stock rose about 4 percent in after-hours trading before settling at a rise of about 3.4 percent. Market value evaporated by 800 billion US dollars in five days, which is 3.5 times Alibaba's market value. Supporters of Jensen Huang created a war room and an online petition with over 180,000 signatures. The articles leave open whether the White House will support the return of the former CEO. It remains uncertain if Chinese enterprises will face increased difficulty obtaining high-end GPUs under new management.

stories.Headline: Tencent updates LightVela AI Agent to function as a personal assistant with long term memory
stories.Summary:
Tencent updated its cloud based AI Agent product called LightVela in late 2026. This product evolved into a personal assistant with long term memory and autonomous task execution. The company launched the public beta in April and opened it to all users in September. Recent upgrades occurred over the past two months to make the tool more like a personal agent. These changes aim to integrate AI into the daily work and life of users.

The system requires a web page interface but supports WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, and QQ. It includes a cloud computer added in October and a My Workbench Beta feature. New users receive one month of free experience and 4500 AI points. Six connectors exist for Tencent Meeting, Feishu, DingTalk, Tencent Docs, Tencent Securities, and ima. Users can create multiple assistants with independent personas, skills, and persistent memory.

Lei Tech conducted a real world test and found the product far from perfect. The tester stated that the interactive design for delivering files is not intuitive enough. They noted that the AI sometimes provides sources that are not applicable to domestic users. The tester observed that the AI failed to complete a simple browser screenshot task. They concluded that the product is not as polished as WorkBuddy or Muse.

Ordinary users are affected by the need to understand environment failures and technical requirements. The researcher Bot spent 1 minute and 18 seconds to sort out three specific updates. A personal display website took over 17 minutes to develop but failed to launch. The AI encountered a display service conflict when attempting to use the cloud browser. Users must switch between Daily and Explore pages to arrange work or adjust assistants.

LightVela originally migrated the open source Hermes Agent to the cloud for easier deployment. It now uses SkillHub to share most existing AI skills for its assistants. The persona page allows users to extract personality cards or take a persona test. The product is positioned as a cloud personal assistant for business, finance, and housekeeping. It provides templates for data dashboards, operation activity, and personal display benches.

The AI will continue to develop as a partner for development and business operations. Users can still customize Agent Bots based on existing recommended templates. The articles leave open whether ordinary users can smoothly find the functions they need. It remains unclear if the cloud computer can operate software independently like a human. The final product quality compared to mature office agents is not yet determined.

stories.Headline: AWS adds full fine-tuning to SageMaker AI serverless model customization
stories.Summary:
Amazon Web Services announced that SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning on November 19, 2026. This new feature allows businesses to train pretrained large language models on their own specific company data. The process helps models adapt to a particular style, task, or domain instead of using general knowledge. Full Fine-Tuning updates all model parameters simultaneously to better absorb complex domain knowledge. This method overcomes the representation power limits found in parameter efficient fine tuning methods.

The service requires no GPU provisioning, cluster setup, or distributed training configuration from the user. Experiments used a Qwen3-4B base model and the Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K dataset containing 110,000 coding instruction pairs. The data was split into 99,000 training records, 5,500 validation records, and 5,500 test records. Other supported base models include DeepSeek-R1-1.5B, Nemotron-30B, and Gemma-4-26B. Users can set hyperparameters like a learning rate of 2e-5 and a global batch size of 8.

AWS stated that this serverless approach lets engineers focus on tuning without managing infrastructure. They explained that Full Fine-Tuning modifies the weight matrix uniformly to use the full representational capacity. The company noted that this results in stronger model convergence and better activation alignment across layers. They claimed that the quality advantage of this method grows as the dataset scale increases. AWS mentioned that the service handles compute allocation and checkpoint management automatically.

The articles state that LoRA methods can hit an accuracy plateau on complex tasks. This limitation affects businesses that need to capture complex patterns for diverse and scaling datasets. Using a frontier model called Amazon Nova Pro, the LLM-as-Judge metric showed FFT reached 90.0 percent correctness. The PRIMECODE scorer measured code fidelity using BLEU, F1, and ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L metrics. MMLU was used as a guardrail to detect if the model forgot general knowledge.

Fine tuning is used to increase accuracy on domain work while reducing per token inference costs. LoRA reduces trainable parameters by freezing weights and injecting small low rank replacement matrices. However, the low rank nature of these updates can limit the power of the model. Full Fine-Tuning is more effective for complex domains where large, high quality datasets are available. This method avoids the localized distortions that are characteristic of low rank fine tuning methods.

Users can now launch jobs using the SageMaker Python SDK by setting the training type to full. The articles leave open how effective values for hyperparameters will vary across different specific tasks. They note that Full Fine-Tuning is not universally superior to LoRA in every single scenario. The effectiveness of the process is described as being extremely sensitive to the chosen hyperparameter settings. The text ends before completing the final comparison between the two different tuning methods.

stories.Headline: Henna Virkkunen hosts Brussels Apply AI Summit and presents first startup award
stories.Summary:
Nearly 1,000 high-level policymakers, start-ups, industry leaders and researchers will take part in the Apply AI Summit in Brussels on 17 November 2026, the European Commission has announced. They will discuss how artificial intelligence can boost Europe’s competitiveness across 10 strategic sectors and the public sector, according to the press release. The summit will also showcase concrete AI applications, European success stories and innovative projects. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will host the summit and present the first Apply AI Startup Award to three European start-ups. The award recognises innovative European startups and scaleups developing AI solutions in the strategic sectors, the Commission said.

Alongside the in-person event, an online conference platform will run from 16 to 20 November, allowing an additional 2,500 participants to join part of the summit. The Apply AI Summit marks one year since the adoption of the Apply AI Strategy, which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. It concludes the first European AI Innovation Month, running from 14 October to 17 November 2026, organised by the European Commission in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union. Virkkunen, as Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, is responsible for hosting the summit and presenting the first Apply AI Startup Award to the three winning European start-ups. The Commission organised the European AI Innovation Month in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

The press release does not say what the three start-ups said or name them. The articles give no further statements from the hosts or participants. The summit is tied to the Apply AI Strategy, which the Commission adopted one year before the event and which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. The articles do not say what happens after the summit beyond the online platform running until 20 November. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Atturra forum speakers urge schools to set clear AI boundaries and limit data exposure
stories.Summary:
Atturra hosted an education forum in Sydney on the use of technology in schools, and speakers said schools need to adopt digital tools carefully as AI and cyber risks reshape teaching, administration and parent engagement. The forum focused on how schools are managing rising expectations from teachers, students and families while under pressure to improve efficiency and protect sensitive data. Discussion covered AI in classrooms, cybersecurity, administrative systems and the challenge of ensuring smaller schools can keep pace with change. Brett Auton, Director of Scholarion at Atturra, said schools were being forced to think more strategically about technology decisions across teaching, risk management and communication. The forum was reported by IT Brief Australia on 18 November 2026.

Speakers said institutions should not treat AI as a neutral tool and must set clear boundaries around its role in learning. Dr Joseph Sweeney, Adviser at IBRS, said some schools may increasingly consider replacing large external technology platforms with sovereign AI tools built for their own environments, although he suggested that option would be more realistic for better-resourced institutions. According to the Australian Education Technology Industry Association, K-12 schools spent an estimated AUD $3.2 billion on education technology products and services in 2025, up 28 per cent since 2023. Barrett said Microsoft's data shows more than 15,000 emails containing malicious QR codes are aimed at the education sector every day. Auton said schools needed to examine what information they hold, who can access it, how long it is retained, and their exposure to third-party providers.

Auton said school leaders need to understand the strategic implications, teachers need to understand how technology will support their work, and students and parents need confidence that information is being handled appropriately. Sweeney said schools must keep teachers firmly in charge rather than letting software act as a moral authority or companion, and must safeguard kids against manipulative, addictive algorithms. Sweeney said AI should prompt students to think rather than simply hand over answers, and that if ungoverned it has the potential to be even more damaging to children's cognitive development and learning than social media has been. Lee Barrett, AI Education and Advocacy Lead at Catholic Education Network, said teachers are entitled to ask for the evidence and parents are entitled to understand what their children are using and why.

Vivek Puthucode, General Manager of Microsoft Elevate Asia, said the question is no longer whether students should learn to use AI but how we equip them to use it wisely, safely and creatively. Barrett said schools are working incredibly hard but are up against a lot, and that education is consistently among the most targeted sectors. Puthucode said success in the age of AI won't be measured by how much technology we put into classrooms but by how much more time educators have to teach and how well we protect the trust that students, families and communities place in schools. Auton said knowing and limiting your exposure is becoming the main game in town, which means understanding what information you hold, reducing unnecessary duplication, reviewing who has access to it, challenging how long you retain it, and being much more deliberate about the systems and providers you use.

Auton said simplifying admissions, improving communication with families, removing duplicate data entry and making student information easier to access can deliver significant value across a school. Barrett said when a new staff member logs in on day one and everything they need is already connected, that is back-office technology doing its job well, and when a teacher in a remote school gets the same reliable network and tools as one in the city, that is equity. Auton said strong core platforms, reliable data, cybersecurity, integration capabilities and the skills needed to use technology effectively are the foundations that allow schools to take advantage of new capabilities as they emerge. Puthucode said the real value of AI in education isn't simply about saving time but about how we reinvest that time, and that by reducing administrative burdens we can help educators focus more of their energy on improving learning, supporting student wellbeing, and helping young people thrive.

Speakers warned that smaller schools may struggle to keep up with emerging technology because of cost and limited internal expertise. Sweeney said pooling resources lets schools access sovereign AI platforms, negotiate better vendor terms and share specialist teachers remotely across campuses so students don't miss out. Auton said schools shouldn't need to become technology companies to operate effectively, and that standardised platforms, cloud-based services, shared capabilities and repeatable implementation approaches can all help reduce the cost and complexity of adopting modern technology. More to follow.

stories.Headline: UNESCO finds AI models answer climate science questions well but average 33.8% on policy interactions
stories.Summary:
UNESCO released a report titled Can We Trust AI on Climate Information?, developed with the UNESCO Chair in Artificial Intelligence at University College London, on 17 November 2026, testing how reliably AI models handle climate-related questions. The number of models varied by test, with up to 33 assessed overall, five in the multilingual assessment and 15 in the conversational-pressure assessment. Leading models answered 88% to 96% of established climate-science questions correctly, and the best scores on tasks asking whether a source supported a claim were 71% to 77%. The best score for judging the direction of a single policy's effect was 94.5%, but across models accuracy on how two policies interact averaged 33.8%, close to the 33.3% chance baseline.

The multilingual assessment tested five models in 13 languages, and average accuracy was 88.6% in English, 83.6% in Hindi and Bengali, and 81.4% in Urdu, with only about half of the tested questions receiving identical answers across all 13 languages. In staged conversations, sustained pushback reduced the accuracy of initially correct answers by about 31 to 35 percentage points across 15 models, with many concessions occurring at the first expression of disagreement. For the policy test, researchers compared model answers with En-ROADS, a climate-policy simulator, asking whether the combined temperature effect of two policies would be greater than, less than or equal to the sum of their separate effects. The report says this measures agreement with the simulator on a defined task rather than the real-world success of any particular climate policy.

The report distinguishes two uses of AI that call for different standards of validation, namely public climate information, where services in Indian languages need language-specific testing including whether answers stay consistent and withstand misleading follow-up prompts, and policy analysis, where assessments of interacting measures need checks against validated modelling tools and scientific expertise. It says strong performance on factual questions is insufficient evidence for the policy use. The report's direct India-relevant evidence is the measured performance in Hindi, Bengali and Urdu, and its wider implication is to test a model for the specific task, language and conversational setting in which it will be used. The article names the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and the report notes that poorer performance in a language is not inevitable, since differences varied by model.

stories.Headline: European Commission sets HR rules for high-risk AI with deadlines from 2026 to 2028
stories.Summary:
The European Commission established the EU AI Act to regulate artificial intelligence, including specific rules for human resources. These regulations target high-risk AI used for recruitment, selection, and employment management, such as tools for filtering applications or monitoring worker performance. Certain transparency provisions under Article 50 became effective on August 2, 2026, while the broader high-risk rules under Annex III will apply starting December 2, 2027. Other deadlines include December 2, 2026, for specific marking obligations and August 2, 2028, for AI embedded in regulated products.

Compliance requires employers to classify their systems based on intended use and influence on decisions rather than administrative labels. Systems that profile natural persons remain high-risk, though an exception under Article 6(3) exists for narrow procedural tasks that pose no significant risk of harm. Under Article 26, employers deploying high-risk AI must ensure human oversight by competent staff and maintain relevant input data. They must also inform affected workers and representatives, keep automatically generated logs for at least six months, and report serious incidents to authorities.

The European Commission is responsible for these mandates and the associated enforcement timeline. The Commission stated that classification depends on how a system fits into a decision and its intended purpose. They clarified that the Article 6(3) exception requires both a qualifying task and a lack of significant harm to be valid. Furthermore, the Commission requires that employers suspend any high-risk system if they believe it creates a risk and notify the provider or market-surveillance authority.

stories.Headline: Exa raises embedding throughput about 50% on AWS Inferentia2 chips to index billions of documents
stories.Summary:
Exa boosted embedding throughput by about 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips, the company said in a post published on the AWS blog on November 18, 2026. Exa said it is building one of the few true web indexes by aggregating and serving knowledge from across the web, along with private and synthetic sources. Exa said it optimizes the index for semantic search, grounding agents and humans in true, high-quality data. Exa said it uses multi-tower semantic machine learning models to embed web data and query data into the same vector space. Exa said the keystone technology behind this is an in-house vector database.

Exa said the database must ingest as much high-quality web data as possible and embed all of it. Exa said the unit economics of embedding therefore underlie everything it does. Exa said that at the scale of tens or hundreds of billions of documents, finding hardware that delivers the best performance per dollar is not a tuning detail. Exa said any per-document cost improvement compounds into a significant number. Exa said inference runs on an asynchronous pipeline that must be high-volume and fast to serve recent data quickly and shrink the time between discovery and serving.

Exa said every structured web document it ranks as high enough quality must be embedded before it can be served. Exa said raw web data moves from crawlers into an asynchronous pipeline of parse, moderate and filter, then embed, with the result served from a vector database. Exa said its experience with the Neuron hardware family began with a backfill. Exa said moving to a superior document model meant re-embedding its existing corpus, and it selected 30 billion high-priority documents for re-embedding. Exa said a migration like this temporarily doubles the embedding load, which made it exactly the right moment to re-evaluate its hardware choices.

Exa said the doubling was a clear trigger to reconsider its hardware and optimization choices. Exa said AWS Inferentia2 figures refer to performance on the smallest instance type, an Inferentia2 xlarge instance (inf2.xlarge), with one chip and two NeuronCores. Exa said its workload runs on a single NeuronCore, so it runs Kubernetes pods that pack onto larger instances without leaving any cores idle, giving container homogeneity across the embedding fleet. Exa said the same process runs on a Trainium2 NeuronCore and scales the same way through data parallelism. Exa said its initial Inferentia2 implementation was a straightforward data-parallel, FP16 representation of the model.

Exa said that from that baseline it became a march to push throughput as high as possible, using the Neuron SDK and support from the AWS Trainium team. Exa said a progressive series of optimizations ultimately delivered roughly a 1.5× throughput improvement from the naive compile. Exa said the first was weight layout optimization, which eliminates unnecessary transposes by aligning the weight layout with the scheduling and layout of the broader model. Exa said it also enabled autocast, letting the compiler downcast matrix multiplications to lower precision while preserving dynamic range. Exa said the downcast outputs met its correctness gate of 0.999 cosine similarity against the reference, so the accuracy impact was within its acceptance threshold.

Exa said the Neuron Kernel Interface library provides optimized kernels for common model layers and operations. Exa said these pre-built kernels deliver immediate gains on common features, and it used them to quickly remove the most straightforward sources of inefficiency. Exa said a drop-in attention kernel gave it the next bump in performance. Exa said profiles from the Neuron Explorer consistently showed large amounts of spill and reload from high-bandwidth memory, which kept the Tensor Engine from being fully utilized through the forward pass. Exa said it wrote a custom weight-stationary fused SwiGLU MLP kernel that eliminated the HBM stalls, using the higher-level NKI language for layout operations, loops and memory operations and dropping into the lower-level NKI ISA only for specific tensor operations.

Exa said keeping most of the kernel in the higher-level language makes it more understandable for engineers and easier to debug. Exa said per-accelerator throughput measured with the other on-chip core idle was significantly higher than what it saw with both cores running simultaneously. Exa said that gap meant its theoretical data-parallel throughput should have been well above its realized aggregate performance, which pointed to contention between the cores. Exa said profiling and experimentation showed its workload was not yet saturating the Tensor Engine, and the remaining headroom was its to claim by making the computation leaner. Exa said it rewrote the attention kernel around the exact shapes in its model to cut FLOPS spent on padding.

Exa said generic kernels are built to handle any shape, so they cannot take advantage of the specific shapes in a given architecture. Exa said it also folded attention operations into single matmuls where the generic kernel used multiple instruction steps. Exa said that cut the inner-loop operations needed to compute the same values, which reduced HBM round trips and produced the final significant speedup. Exa said its final version was a 47% improvement in performance and cost per 1 million documents embedded, against its initial baseline. Exa said agents developed all of these optimizations inside a simple three part harness that lets them verify correctness, measure performance and profile the workload to find the next direction.

Exa said that using Flyte, an ML ops workflow platform, each agent runs its own workflow. Exa said the workflow compiles a NEFF Neuron executable and checks a forward pass against a baseline dataset, which must reach 0.999 cosine similarity to the canonical model. Exa said it then profiles one forward pass and runs a 30 minute saturation benchmark on real hardware. Exa said the harness supports agents at different costs, with lightweight models handling tedious work like grid searching compiler parameters and correctness checks preventing drift. Exa said reasoning agents test complex hypotheses and find bottlenecks, while the strongest code generators write custom kernels to fix them.

Exa said matching each agent to its task keeps costs in check, and validation keeps capable agents from drifting. Exa said that because many agents do not know the latest features and syntax, neuron agentic development skills also helped. Exa said it has so far optimized Inferentia2 for the US West (Oregon) Region (us-west-2), but tuning one hardware family in one Region has hard limits. Exa said spot and on demand availability vary by Region, and organizations with many consumers compete with themselves. Exa said locking into one Region or instance type almost guarantees a compute shortage, and possibly degraded service.

Exa said it schedules compute across multiple Regions from one Kubernetes control plane. Exa said its scheduler compares performance per dollar across instance types and packs pods onto the cheapest nodes, rescheduling as embedding demand shifts. Exa said each hardware type it optimizes for brings it closer to the global optimum, which is why its Inferentia2 work carried over directly to Trainium2. Exa said shifting hardware profiles lets it free up nodes other teams need or absorb their unused reserved compute. Exa said that for a long lived model, optimizing across hardware pays off enormously.

Exa said that at the scale it operates, extracting maximum cost-performance from a flexible pool of hardware is what matters. Exa said adding Neuron hardware to that pool and optimizing it with NKI has proven to be a major source of long-term cost savings. Exa said the post was published on the AWS blog on November 18, 2026. Exa said the post details how it optimized its embedding infrastructure for cheaper, more flexible inference workloads on AWS Neuron hardware, AWS Inferentia2 and AWS Trainium2. Exa said an agentic development workflow drove the optimization.

stories.Headline: Commonwealth Bank releases CodeCheck, an open-source AI tool for finding software vulnerabilities
stories.Summary:
Commonwealth Bank of Australia released CodeCheck, an open-source AI cybersecurity tool, on November 19, 2026, according to TechGig. The tool is designed to help businesses identify potential software vulnerabilities earlier in their development processes. Security engineers at the bank developed CodeCheck based on an internal AI capability already used in the bank's own software development. The public version lets other businesses apply a similar approach when reviewing their code. The tool works with OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code to analyse software, investigate potential security weaknesses, and provide evidence for engineers to review.

CodeCheck uses an AI harness that guides coding agents through a structured security review of individual code changes, files, or entire codebases. Businesses can supply extra context about what their applications are meant to do, which helps the AI judge vulnerabilities based on the software's design. According to the bank's GitHub documentation, the tool reviews security in four stages, examining entry points, data flows, and potential weaknesses before assigning agents to investigate using the Common Weakness Enumeration framework. It then combines duplicate findings and assigns independent AI agents to challenge the initial results before generating a report. Findings include how untrusted input reaches affected code, an independent reviewer's assessment, and a severity score based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System 4.0, and they follow the Security Analysis Results Interchange Format data standard. The tool supports diff-aware reviews of commits, branches, and pull requests, and organisations can customise it with CWE-based security playbooks.

CommBank Chief Security Officer Nicola Nicol said the bank built the capability to strengthen its internal defences before making it publicly available. CodeCheck is a free download from GitHub for businesses using Codex or Claude Code, though organisations remain responsible for costs tied to their AI coding agents and underlying models. The bank recommends running the tool in an isolated environment, mounting reviewed code with read-only permissions, restricting network access, and preventing AI agents from accessing credentials, warning that prompt-based restrictions are not deterministic. CBA also notes that CodeCheck sends reviewed code to the selected model provider, making that provider's data-handling and security policies relevant, and that token consumption and processing costs rise as the codebase grows, so it recommends spending limits or timeouts for unattended reviews. Some providers restrict cybersecurity-related requests, which can interrupt authorised reviews or end responses early, and the final report might not always show when part of an assessment was interrupted.

CBA has released CodeCheck as a one-time open-source project and does not plan to actively maintain, update, or provide ongoing support for the public repository. Organisations that adopt the tool will be responsible for maintaining their own versions and evaluating any modifications they make.

stories.Headline: Zheng Yuanjie uses AI to animate fairy tales as other users steal actors' faces for traffic
stories.Summary:
Zheng Yuanjie announced a career shift on November 17 to revive his fairy tales using AI. He is creating short videos from his past writings for a Douyin account. These animated works are released for all readers to watch for free. Other AI users have misappropriated actors' faces without any authorization agreements. This theft occurred to harvest online traffic through unauthorized short dramas.

The Douyin account Zheng Yuanjie's Fairy Tale World began updating on October 24. It features Good Habit Stories and Chinese Zodiac Fairy Tales with episodes of 4 to 5 minutes. The 1987 A Dream of Red Mansions actors were used in Dreaming Back to the Red Chamber. This drama includes Daiyu's Rebirth and Revenge and features Chen Xiaoxu, Zhang Li, Deng Jie, and Li Ting. The 1987 series cost 6.9 million yuan for 36 episodes across 219 scenic spots.

Zheng Yuanjie, the 71-year-old King of Fairy Tales, says he will keep working hard. He believes imagination is the one thing that AI cannot do for humans. Director Jia Zhangke says AI and live-action films are complementary rather than mutually substitutive. He believes the most touching movie moments come from human judgment and physical sensations. Director Zhang Yimou says AI is a good tool that puts the industry under pressure.

Actor Zhang Li stated she never authorized any institution to use her portrait for AI synthesis. She reserves the right to pursue legal responsibility for the unauthorized use of her image. Some netizens say the style of Zheng's AI animations is rough and not exquisite enough. Ordinary people are affected as AI short dramas compete for attention at zero cost. The entire film industry faces survival anxiety due to these low-cost AI productions.

The 1987 series used 2,700 hand-made costumes and music written by Wang Liping over 21 months. Modern S+ costume dramas now cost between 300 million and 800 million yuan in total. A 41-second AI celebrity video can be customized for a deposit of 40 yuan. Digital human images cost 1,500 to 2,000 yuan, while compliant face authorization is 100 to 500 yuan. Lawyer Li Haiquan notes that performers can claim portrait and performer rights.

AI images may reach a level of authenticity that passes for real in three to five years. This shift could allow ordinary people to replace professional screenwriters and directors. The industry still lacks rules on whether film festivals or theaters should accept AI works. It remains open what standards the evaluation system should use for these new films. The protection of personal portrait and voice rights faces unprecedented and severe challenges.

stories.Headline: AI finds software flaws and firms rush patches, raising outage risk, experts say
stories.Summary:
Recent tech outages at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab disrupted businesses and consumers, and a temporary ground stop at US airports also caused chaos, though Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy cited aging air traffic control infrastructure for that one. Politicians and tech executives, including Armadin CEO Kevin Mandia, suggest organisations are using AI to discover software vulnerabilities in their systems. That has led to a mad rush to apply patches quickly, according to Senator Mark Warner, vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee. Mandia stated that updating at speed may prevent testing all potential outcomes of an update. Nicole Perlroth, a former cybersecurity reporter, noted that pressure to patch faster increases the likelihood of breaking things in unexpected, cascading ways, in a post on X.

The article, published by TechGig on November 19, 2026, says organisations are rolling out a higher volume of fixes, potentially overwhelming systems. Fast updates may hinder full testing, leading to system disruptions, experts say, and more tech outages are expected as firms accelerate patching in the AI era. Last month, AI discovered significant flaws in a programming language used by up to 70 per cent of websites, contributing to the increased patching activity. The report ties the recent outages at the banks, Microsoft and the FAA to the rush to fix cybersecurity flaws discovered by AI.

Mandia added that while nobody wants an outage, organisations will become operationally better at updating in the AI age, and he anticipates near-term cybersecurity pain will lead to long-term gains. Warner, the senator who described the mad rush to patch, and Mandia are among those pointing to AI vulnerability discovery as the driver of the faster patching. Perlroth's warning focused on the risk that speed creates, with pressure to patch faster raising the chance of unexpected, cascading breakage. The article does not say what the organisations themselves said about the outages.

The context given is that organisations use AI to find software vulnerabilities, which prompts quick fixes, and that the fast updates may skip full testing. The report says more tech outages are expected as firms accelerate patching in the AI era, and it notes the near-term pain may give way to long-term gains as organisations get better at updating. No further steps, timelines or responses from Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab or the FAA are given in the article.

stories.Headline: NTT Data CTO Vikram Bharwani argues banks must control data and decisions to use AI
stories.Summary:
Vikram Bharwani, CTO for Banking and Financial Services at NTT DATA in the UK and Ireland, published an article on November 13, 2026, arguing that every major bank will need sovereign AI. He defined sovereign AI not as a bank-owned frontier model or a warehouse full of GPUs, but as the ability to use powerful AI while retaining control of knowledge, actions and decisions. The article appeared on nttdata.com at 06:00:00Z on 2026-11-13, and a second version appeared on 2026-11-14 at 06:00:00Z. Bharwani wrote that banking has spent half a century digitalizing how money moves and how financial services operate. He said AI is now beginning to digitalize something far more complex, namely the judgment behind banking decisions.

Bharwani cited a 2024 survey by the Bank of England and the UK's Financial Conduct Authority, which found that 75% of responding firms were using AI, up from 58% in 2022. He described the reverse information paradox as framed by Satya Nadella, who said that in the AI age the buyer risks giving away knowledge just to use what they bought. Bharwani said a bank's knowledge includes the credit officer's correction, the fraud analyst's rejected lead and the exception an experienced underwriter accepted, with the reasons for those decisions. He said the knowledge layer is more valuable than the model itself, and that a bank can use external models while owning its private evaluations, approved knowledge, feedback and orchestration. He said data residency is important, but a model can run in a bank's own building and still leave the bank unable to explain a decision or switch suppliers.

Bharwani said sovereignty comes down to whether a bank controls its data, can explain decisions, retains what the system learns and can keep operating when something fails. He said an agent's permissions, network access and spending limits need to sit outside the model, and critical actions need approval and an effective way to stop them without it. He said these controls can exist in a public cloud and can also be missing from a private deployment. He said the FCA expects firms to apply existing duties and governance to AI, including consumer outcomes and senior accountability. He said a decision passport should capture inputs, permissions, policy and model versions, tool actions, human interventions and the final explanation, and a bank must recreate that record after changing models.

Bharwani said a mortgage application from someone with irregular income shows what the architecture must do, with AI reconciling payslips and bank statements, finding policy, flagging conflicting evidence and preparing an affordability recommendation. He said the underwriter should see conflicts and assumptions rather than a confident paragraph that hides them, and a declined customer deserves a clear reason and a way to correct the record or seek review. He said an upheld appeal may expose a faulty interpretation, arrears may show whether affordability assumptions reflected risk, and a complaint may reveal that the explanation failed the customer. He said learning should stay in a sandbox, tested against unseen cases, before release under control, and historical lending data can reflect past exclusions while declined applicants create gaps in outcome data. He said the same principle applies to fraud, customer service and operational resilience, and the test is fewer avoidable referrals, lower false positives, faster resolution, sounder decisions and better customer experiences.

Bharwani said banks do not need to own every part of the AI stack but must control their data, knowledge and evaluations, with freedom to change models without losing context. He said banks need clear controls over what agents can do, decision records that survive each technology change and, for critical services, a tested fallback. He said some tasks warrant private inference while others are better served by a smaller model or a clear deterministic rule. He said a bank should start with one material process, establish what a good decision costs today, how long it takes, where it goes wrong and what customers experience, then measure whether AI improves those outcomes. He said cost per token means little if the result is a faster, cheaper mistake.

Bharwani said banks should consider what happens to human judgment as work is automated, asking how junior underwriters learn to challenge AI in five years if it builds every first-pass credit pack. He said they should be given supervised exceptions, simulated cases and access to model traces, and human oversight is meaningless if a person clicks approve without the chance to investigate the evidence. He said powerful AI will be available to everyone, and the real difference will be whether banks turn it into a governed extension of institutional judgment without giving up control. He said a bank can rent a model but cannot rent accountability, and he expects sovereign AI to become part of core banking infrastructure. The articles leave open which specific process a bank should choose first and what the IDC InfoBrief sponsored by NTT DATA concludes.

stories.Headline: Doubao Work reaches 2 billion yuan in annual recurring revenue within three months of launch
stories.Summary:
Doubao Work reached an annual recurring revenue of 2 billion yuan by November 18, 2026. The AI office application was launched only three months before hitting this financial milestone. Its daily active users have now exceeded 8 million people. Many enterprises integrated the tool into production line management and quality audits. These companies also used the AI for equipment operation and maintenance.

The system combines with Feishu collaboration to turn implicit knowledge into reusable organizational assets. In Changzhou, Ninebot uses the tool to automate 16 daily forms for attendance and overtime. This automation saves two clerks between 20 and 30 minutes of work every day. The tool also manages standard working hours and manpower data for different models. It now includes a memory function to reduce redundant data entry for line leaders.

He Yuchong, a production management specialist, used Doubao Work to polish functions based on site pain points. He described specific operation paths and expected effects to the AI to modify the system. He first troubleshot errors himself before telling the AI the phenomenon and repair logic. He then asked actual clerks and line leaders to test each updated version for convenience. He aimed to let AI take over repetitive tasks to free energy for high-value work.

Front-line engineers in Wuhan and Changzhou, and across a national supplier network, use these tools. Line leaders previously complained about redundant actions, such as selecting the same product model ten times daily. Managers formerly had to scroll through dozens of chat records or nested folders to find data. Now, managers use mobile terminals to check real-time output and efficiency while patrolling lines. Bosch China engineers also use the system to reduce time spent moving information.

TSMC faced high costs when building a wafer fab in Phoenix, Arizona, on December 6, 2022. The US plant cost 4 to 5 times more than plants in Taiwan, China. Compliance with 18,000 rules cost 35 million US dollars, and gross profit margins were only 8 percent. TSMC sent 500 engineers from Taiwan and trained 600 Arizona hires in Taiwan, China. These challenges delayed the 4-nanometer production line originally scheduled for mass production in 2024.

The AI tool now runs dashboards on large screens at the head of each production line. It automatically sends messages to responsible persons to remind them of stand-up meeting problems. The articles do not state the specific future revenue targets for Doubao Work. They leave open how other manufacturing sectors will integrate these specific AI organizational processes. The text does not detail the final results of the Bosch China implementation.

stories.Headline: Letitia James launches ASSET unit to enforce New York AI safety law from January
stories.Summary:
New York Attorney General Letitia James launched a specialized unit on November 17, 2026, to enforce artificial intelligence regulations. This new office is designed to oversee compliance before a state law takes effect in January. The initiative focuses on the safety and transparency requirements that will soon apply to frontier model developers. This agency represents the first effort of its kind in the United States dedicated to AI laws. The new organization is called the AI Safety, Standards, Enforcement, and Transparency Unit, or ASSET for short.

It will require developers of frontier models to meet specific safety and transparency standards starting in January. These legal requirements aim to ensure that powerful artificial intelligence systems are developed and deployed responsibly. The unit will monitor these developers to ensure they follow the impending state safety laws. Letitia James is the official responsible for the creation and leadership of this novel regulatory unit.

Her office stated that this is the first unit in the country dedicated to enforcing AI laws. The Attorney General intends to use this group to hold technology developers accountable under the new state framework. By establishing ASSET now, the office aims to be ready for the upcoming regulatory changes. More to follow.

stories.Headline: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill pushes for state-led AI and privacy rules
stories.Summary:
Governor Mikie Sherrill pushed for state-led AI and privacy rules during a recent interview. She argues that states must lead because federal regulation has stalled. Sherrill is a first-term Democrat elected in the 2025 off-year cycle. She has been in her job for roughly one year. The governor believes states are filling a power vacuum left by Washington.

Sherrill signed a data center plan in May 2026 and build-out bills in August 2026. These require water transparency, community benefits agreements, and bring-your-own-power to avoid resident rate increases. New Jersey levied over $1 million in fines on a southern New Jersey facility. The state also received $525 million from a Meta settlement. Sherrill supports the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact to replace the Electoral College.

Sherrill says government must protect people from the downside risks of AI. She claims that power moves into vacuums, pushing authority down to governors and state legislatures. The governor stated that states are now laboratories for tech regulation without federal statutes. She believes that parental controls are a full-time job that still fails. Sherrill says she will not use profanity online to seem tough.

Sherrill notes that teens spend 35 hours a week online, impacting their mental health. She claims that Republican politicians are trapped in a bubble created by Elon Musk. The governor mentions that Zohran Mamdani, Rob Sand, and Amy Acton are authentic video natives. She says that graduates who cannot find jobs may lose interest in MAGA rallies. Residents demanded Flock license plate readers after a wave of car thefts.

The articles state that New Jersey warned ports that importing Russian diesel is illegal. This action turned away a couple of ships by using existing federal statutes. New Jersey established the first national research center on child online safety for parents. The governor restructured her office to include a chief operating officer for better coordination. She froze energy rate hikes on her first day to stop double digit increases.

Sherrill expects to litigate against YouTube CEO Neal Mohan over settlement terms. The governor is waiting to see if TikTok accepts the same terms as Meta. It remains open whether data center moratoriums will spread beyond the state of New Jersey. The articles leave open if the popular vote compact will reach its required threshold. It is unclear if other states will converge on New Jersey's data center pillars.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandal and allegations of chip diversion to China
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive and board member on November 12. He stepped down following an infidelity scandal and allegations of diverting AI chips. These accusations involve relationships with Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang, a suspected spy. Alice Huang allegedly used the former leader to send chips to China. The diversion involved at least 7.5 billion dollars worth of Nvidia technology.

Interim CEO Colette Kress now leads the company and its financial operations. She previously lowered an OpenAI data center guarantee in Ohio to 105 billion dollars. On August 10, Nvidia signed a 500 billion dollar memorandum with six firms. These partners include BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR, and Apollo Global. The company's market value fell to 3.7629 trillion dollars, placing it third overall.

Colette Kress is responsible for management and is known as a finance executive. She has previously stopped several large transactions from moving forward at the company. Elon Musk stated that Huang led supply chain management brilliantly through verbal agreements. Musk warned that the company will lose key contracts without Huang's personal trust. Sam Altman called Huang his hero but noted that heroes have flaws.

Shareholders Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker sent a formal letter requesting Huang's reinstatement. A petition titled Stand With Jensen gathered about 160,000 signatures from employees and investors. Many startups may struggle because Nvidia participated in 129 venture capital investments this year. UBS warned that 50 billion dollars could leave the market if funding scales back. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia should look outside the company for leadership.

Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 after mapping it out at a San Jose Denny's. He previously worked as a dishwasher at that restaurant while living in Oregon. He married Lori Huang in 1985 after meeting at Oregon State University. His daughter, Madison Huang, served as a chief of staff and pushed marketing. Biographer Stephen Witt described Huang as an arrogant man who could not tolerate dissent.

The Nvidia board is not currently discussing bringing Jensen Huang back to power. A war room of executives is reportedly lobbying the White House for his return. Denny's will reinstall a plaque marking the birthplace of the trillion dollar company. Bitdeer plans to open an AI data center in southern Malaysia next year. The articles leave open whether the 500 billion dollar financing project will collapse.

stories.Headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress oversees a cautious shift in AI funding strategy
stories.Summary:
Nvidia is likely to recalibrate its aggressive financing strategy following a change in leadership. Former CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, leading to this shift. Colette Kress has served as interim CEO since the resignation of Huang. The company is now expected to take a more cautious investment approach. Financial partners continue to discuss funding arrangements for various artificial intelligence companies.

The $500 billion initiative announced August 10 involves Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR. Nvidia may backstop 25 percent of transactions, which equals 125 billion dollars. An OpenAI data center in Ohio saw guarantees reduced from 250 billion to 105 billion dollars. Apple data center guarantees were cut from 500 billion to under 250 billion dollars. These specific guarantees are separate from the broader third-party capital initiative.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has overseen finances since 2013 and maintains a cautious stance. Former CEO Jensen Huang stated that the days of acting as a blank check are over. Huang told partners in Berlin they must build structures to raise their own funding. He suggested that companies seeking GPUs should collect upfront payments from their own customers. This approach aims to reduce the industry's total dependence on Nvidia's financial support.

UBS estimates that over 50 billion dollars in liquidity could disappear from the market. AI startups and neocloud companies with limited financial resources are directly impacted by this shift. These companies rely on guarantees to secure data centers and AI chips upfront. Low profitability and rising interest rates could make it harder for them to operate.

Morgan Stanley expects future capital to concentrate on large customers with stronger credit profiles. PitchBook reports Nvidia made 129 global investments this year, compared to 49 in 2023. This activity accounted for 27 percent of all global venture investment activity this year. The company projected 70 percent revenue growth for fiscal 2028 during a presentation in August.

Previous adjusted gross margins were 75 percent, with third quarter guidance set at 74 percent. Wall Street expects third quarter revenue of 109.1 billion dollars and earnings per share of 2.47. Nvidia will release fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on November 17 and hold an earnings call. Investors will watch the rollout of the Vera Rubin platform and its revenue contribution.

The company will provide written commentary on results at 6:20 a.m. Korea time, November 18. A $3 billion investment in Perplexity and talks with other startups remain under consideration. The articles leave open how rising memory prices will impact the company's gross margins.

stories.Headline: Google ties school search access to its AI tools as districts weigh alternatives
stories.Summary:
Google announced earlier this month that it plans to turn off search engine access as soon as next year for K-12 schools that toggle off its AI tools. The company claimed the decision was necessary based on the technologies' recent fusion. Educators were not satisfied by that. A growing number of schools across the country are looking for search engine alternatives in lieu of Google's AI ultimatum. Some of the country's largest school districts, including in Los Angeles, New York, and Chicago, are considering doing away with Google altogether.

Potential options include DuckDuckGo and Microsoft's Bing, both of which offer users the option to disable AI-generated answers. Google has only offered school districts more ways to interact with AI, such as AI Mode and AI Overview, which provides users with chatbot search functions and summarized results, reported The New York Times. Google disclosed that the company would turn off its Gemini AI program and search engine for schools "until schools decide which services to enable." A January report by the Brookings Institution's Center for Universal Education found that AI can "undermine children's foundational development," and that "the damages it has already caused are daunting." New skill development and problem-solving abilities are among the chief concerns when it comes to early-age AI dependence.

Kamar H. Samuels, the chancellor of New York City schools, said in a statement that if Google doesn't reconsider their position, they will explore other search options. He said they refuse to accept the false binary Google has laid out. Google told the Times in a statement Wednesday that it is actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure its products support students and teachers. Rebecca Winthrop, one of the report's authors, told NPR in January that when kids use generative AI that tells them what the answer is, they are not thinking for themselves. She said they are not learning to parse truth from fiction, not learning to understand what makes a good argument, and not learning about different perspectives in the world because they are actually not engaging in the material.

Children can easily fall into a catch-22 in which they continually offload their work onto the AI, diminishing their self-confidence and self-reliance in the process, according to the Brookings Institution report. After school on October 20, 2025, 16-year-old Taki Allen was waiting with three friends outside Kenwood High School in Baltimore County, Maryland, for a ride home from football practice. Allen was eating a bag of Doritos. At least six Baltimore County Police Department vehicles arrived at the scene, and officers leapt out, guns drawn, forcing the boys to the ground and searching them. Omnilert Gun Detect, an artificial intelligence weapon-detection system that scans security footage for firearms, had used the school cameras to misidentify Allen's bag of chips as a gun.

Allen and his classmates Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III are all Black. The Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law filed a lawsuit on their behalf Tuesday against the police department, the Baltimore County board of school, school administrators, and several individual officers. The lawsuit says the encounter was terrifying and life-threatening, and that with armed police encircling them for no apparent reason, each student feared for his life and the lives of his friends. After failing to find anything in the search, one police officer reportedly told the students, "AI is not the best," and another said, "Fucking Omnilerts." As the officers were leaving, another said, "Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem."

The lawsuit showed that the principal texted school staff and administrators after the police left to laugh about the incident. The lawsuit also points out that the Omnilert Gun Detect system was patented in 2022, "barely a year" before it was implemented in Baltimore County schools. After it identified Allen's doritos as a firearm, it sent a text message to a group of school administrators and police, who reviewed the alert and canceled it. But 10 minutes later, the school principal sent a screenshot of the footage in the security alert to a co-worker, who sent it to the police department, who then responded at the scene. The Omnilert Gun Detect parent company, Omnilert LLC, has claimed that the AI system "distinguishes guns from inert objects such as cell phones, hand tools, common office objects and more" in order to "diminish false positives."

Maryland's Office of the Inspector General for Education found that 99 percent of alerts in Baltimore County schools have been false positives. Damon Hewitt, president and executive director of the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, said these students were failed not only by a technology that is prone to false alerts, but also by the very adults meant to keep them safe when we send them to school. He said that instead of this protection, they were met with guns and traumatized, and that it could have been even worse. Texas Supreme Court Justice James P. Sullivan refused to acknowledge the parameters of the Twenty-Second Amendment during his confirmation hearing in the Senate Judiciary Committee Wednesday, even after Delaware Senator Chris Coons spelled it out for him. Trump has repeatedly said he was "not joking" about pursuing a third term in office, first using that phrasing in March 2025 during a phone call with NBC News's Kristin Welker.

In an April 22 interview with Time magazine, the president said there are some loopholes that have been discussed that are well known for keeping him in power. Senator Ted Cruz got into it with outgoing Republican Senator John Cornyn Tuesday, and the two yelled back and forth about the judicial nomination from the mostly empty Senate floor. Cornyn told Cruz, "I don't find you credible. I'm mad at you!" loud enough that people could hear him up in the press gallery.

Cornyn ultimately said, "Oh, that's bullshit," and stormed away toward the Democratic side of the aisle, according to The Washington Sun. At the time of the fight, Cornyn was refusing to return the "blue slip" for T. Elliot Gaiser, assistant attorney general for the Office of Legal Counsel, who was nominated for a Dallas-area federal judgeship earlier this month. Cornyn said on Wednesday to the Associated Press that Gaiser is not from Texas, has not been vetted, and that this is a lifetime job with better qualified people to hold it. Cruz said on Wednesday that Gaiser was the only option for the seat, lest it be relinquished to the Democrats. Cruz said that if the Senate Judiciary Committee does not move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay the price because it will effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity.

Cruz said that would be a tragedy. Cruz's political consulting firm, Axiom Strategies, helped Ken Paxton beat Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary earlier this year, and Paxton ultimately lost the seat to Democrat James Talarico. Cornyn said he does not know why a Texas senator would agree to a nomination of somebody from Ohio for one of the most important district benches in the state, in Dallas. After Vice President JD Vance stuck a shiv in Trump's back with a lengthy X post the morning after the Republican Party was decimated from Mississippi to Maine, Trump has suddenly lost interest in his right-hand man. The president said at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, where the secretary of state is playing a prominent role, "How hot is Marco, right?"

and "Is Marco doing a great job? He's been fantastic." Vance, the erstwhile crown prince to the MAGA throne, wasn't mentioned. The president has also been praising Rubio behind closed doors and suggesting that he could be a good presidential candidate, according to sources who spoke with The New York Times. More to follow.
