stories.Headline: Tencent profits drop as company increases AI infrastructure spending sixfold
stories.Summary:
Tencent Holdings experienced a decline in adjusted net income during the third quarter ending September 30, 2026. The Chinese technology giant saw its profits drop by 6 per cent year on year to 66.5 billion yuan, which equals 10 billion US dollars. This financial dip occurred because the company significantly increased its spending on computing power to remain competitive in the artificial intelligence race. While revenue grew by 8 per cent to 207.3 billion yuan, this figure failed to meet the market expectation of 210.5 billion yuan.

The company expanded its computing capacity by increasing capital expenditure to 81.4 billion yuan, representing a 527 per cent jump from the previous year. This spending increase was 54 per cent higher than the amount spent during the second quarter and exceeded 12 billion US dollars. Such massive infrastructure outlays pushed the firm into a negative free cash flow of 69.1 billion yuan. These investments required the company to sacrifice its profit margins to build the necessary hardware for AI development.

The company is responsible for these financial shifts as it prioritizes long term technological growth over short term gains. By ramping up spending more than sixfold, the firm aims to catch up in a cutthroat domestic market for artificial intelligence. Analysts polled by Bloomberg had predicted the adjusted net income figure, though the overall revenue missed their targets. The company continues to pour money into infrastructure to ensure it possesses the computing power required for future AI competition.

Articles.Title: Tencent profit dips on sixfold increase in AI infrastructure spending

stories.Headline: Wall Street analysts see 160% upside for Sandisk and 130% for CoreWeave amid the AI sell-off
stories.Summary:
Wall Street analysts identified two AI stocks with high upside on November 18, 2026. This analysis followed a market correction that hit the Nasdaq Composite earlier that month. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 24,328.38 during this period of AI boom concerns. Sandisk and CoreWeave are the two companies highlighted for potential growth. These stocks are seen as buying opportunities despite the current market sell-off.

Sandisk shares are 809 dollars with a median target price of 2,100 dollars. CoreWeave shares are 50 dollars with a median target price of 115 dollars. Sandisk will split its stock 8-for-1 on November 19. CoreWeave reported a contracted revenue backlog of 132 billion dollars. Sandisk reported 11 billion dollars in revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

Sandisk CEO David Goeckeler said NAND flash is the only economically viable solution for real-time inference. He stated that product differentiation is strongest as the critical nature of the technology is understood. Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis called CoreWeave the benchmark for AI cloud performance. He praised the company for technical execution and operational maturity in managing large-scale solutions. These leaders highlighted the technical strengths of their respective AI infrastructure companies.

SemiAnalysis recognized CoreWeave as the best AI cloud for the third consecutive time in September. Investors are affected by the cyclical nature of the memory industry and rising interest rates. Sandisk faces competition from Samsung and SK Hynix in the storage device market. CoreWeave competes with general-purpose clouds operated by Microsoft and Amazon. The Nasdaq Composite has historically returned 21 percent in the year after a correction.

Sandisk focuses on consumer products like SD cards, USB flash drives, and portable solid-state drives. It uses a joint venture with Kioxia to purchase NAND flash memory wafers at cost. CoreWeave rents large clusters of GPUs for training and running artificial intelligence models. Sandisk reported triple-digit sales growth in its edge segment and quadruple-digit growth in data centers. CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of 3.6 billion dollars, which rose 168 percent.

Sandisk earnings are forecast to grow at 40 percent annually over the next three years. CoreWeave revenue is expected to increase at 96 percent annually through 2028. A memory supply glut could develop by 2029 and drive profits lower. CoreWeave must still prove its debt-fueled expansion can generate sustainable profits. The articles leave open the timing and severity of the next industry downturn.

stories.Headline: Civil servants pitch AI and data ideas for £50,000 prize by 10 December
stories.Summary:
The fifth Civil Service AI & Data Challenge opened for entries on 18 November 2026, inviting civil servants of any role or grade to pitch ideas for using AI and data in public services by 10 December, with £50,000 of investment and senior support going to the winner. Global Government Forum reported the launch on 17 November. Entries can be written in plain English and no technical background is needed. Senior digital and data officials shortlist the best ideas, and each shortlisted entry is worked up by a volunteer team drawn from different departments and disciplines. Those teams pitch at a semi-final in a Dragons' Den-style format, after which four go through to a further development stage and a final.

The competition is run jointly by Global Government Forum, the Cabinet Office, DCMS and the IT services company NTT DATA. Past winning ideas include a service to support peatland restoration and a project to improve how the NHS and the Department for Work and Pensions share data after a death, to spare bereaved families some paperwork. The organisers say departments and agencies are progressing at least seven of last year's entries. Last year's winner, DWP verification assurance officer Marlon Woodley, is now working on his idea to improve the tools benefits caseworkers use, aimed at fewer errors and faster decisions.

Digital government minister Stephanie Peacock said civil servants see first-hand where technology could make a real difference. Government chief data officer Aimee Smith described the challenge as a way for staff at every grade to put good ideas in front of people who can deliver them. The article's own view is that the scheme's value lies in its pipeline more than its prize, and that at least seven ideas in progress from a single round is a useful signal that bottom-up suggestions can reach delivery. It says the test for this round is whether winners move from pilot to service at a pace that keeps frontline staff entering.

stories.Headline: Payhawk raises US$280m in Goldman Sachs-led Series C at a US$2bn valuation
stories.Summary:
Payhawk announced on November 18, 2026 that it raised US$280m in Series C funding led by Growth Equity of Goldman Sachs Alternatives, bringing its valuation to US$2bn and its total funding to more than US$515m. The AI-native spend management platform was founded in 2018 and now operates across 33 countries and 12 offices. Payhawk reported positive cashflow in Q3 2026 and said 70% of the capital raised in its 2022 Series B round is still held. Co-Founder and CEO Hristo Borisov told FinTech Magazine that the money will help the company scale globally.

Payhawk said the capital will be used to build what it calls the global Finance Operating System for the AI era, built around three interconnected layers. These are AI agents that perform financial work, payments infrastructure that lets agents safely interact with money, and enterprise controls that give finance teams governance over what agents can do and when human help is needed. Borisov said fintech represents only a small percentage of the global payments market, which he and the investors see as an incredible growth opportunity. He said the company aims to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payments infrastructure and enterprise controls.

Borisov said Europe does not need to build local versions of categories invented somewhere else, and that Europeans should build categories the rest of the world follows. He said being born in Europe exposed Payhawk to complexity from day one, and that the window to define the category is open now. James Hayward, Managing Director within Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, said Payhawk's growth reflects the strength of its engineering DNA, global footprint and clear vision for modern spend management. He said payments, AI and enterprise software are increasingly converging, and that Goldman is excited to partner with the team as it scales globally. Hayward is set to join Payhawk's Board of Directors following the round.

Payhawk said its independence will let it scale its predictable subscription pricing model and develop its AI-native finance suite beyond its own cards. Visa is Payhawk's card network, with Payhawk operating as a Visa principal member under EU and UK electronic money institution licences. Oracle NetSuite integrates with Payhawk through a native connector, and Payhawk reports that 99.7% of transactions sync with zero manual intervention and that customers close their books 50% faster. Sage Intacct lists Payhawk as a recommended solution following an integration launched on 10 September 2024.

stories.Headline: ECB warns AI debt boom echoes subprime bubble risks in November review
stories.Summary:
The European Central Bank released its November Financial Stability Review on November 18, 2026, to warn about the current artificial intelligence borrowing boom. The bank stated that the rapid shift toward debt finance resembles the mechanics of the dotcom and subprime bubbles. This trend could lead to financial spillovers that threaten the stability of the euro area. The report highlights that the way these projects are funded creates risks for lenders and investors.

The review estimates that big tech firms held more than $4 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments by the second quarter of 2026. Major US technology companies are projected to reach $5.5 trillion in cumulative capital spending by 2030. European insurers hold approximately €211 billion in private credit, which represents 2.3 percent of their total assets. Looser capital rules could potentially increase demand for securitized debt by another €10 billion to €20 billion.

Vice-President Boris Vujcic stated that the financing needs across the AI supply chain are unprecedented. He noted that heavy borrowing by private firms creates competition for capital with governments that already carry high debt. President Christine Lagarde elevated these warnings to a political signal during a G7 summit in Évian. The bank cautioned that a market reassessment could trigger abrupt repricing and significant valuation losses for investment funds.

The bank is specifically concerned about circular financing and opaque private markets where risk is repackaged and spread. These structures make it difficult to trace who owns the debt if a data center developer fails. The ECB is not predicting an immediate crash but has placed the debt-fueled buildout on its stability watchlist. The next Financial Stability Review is scheduled for publication on May 26, 2027.

Articles.Title: ECB says the AI borrowing boom has echoes of the subprime bubble

stories.headline_source: ECB says the AI borrowing boom has echoes of the subprime bubble

stories.Headline: Ukraine’s chief AI officer says war accelerates the country’s AI rollout and offers lessons for Europe
stories.Summary:
Roman Kyslyi, Ukraine’s chief AI officer, told Euronews in an interview published on 18 November 2026 that Russia’s war is accelerating the country’s rollout of artificial intelligence, because the need to keep essential public services running has driven rapid technological innovation. Ukraine has become a testing ground for AI-powered military technologies, including self-guided drones, while also pioneering the use of artificial intelligence in public administration, according to the article. Kyslyi said Ukraine is among the first countries to start an AI assistant for citizens, referring to the digital government app Diia, which offers advice and access to public services. The country is also developing its own national AI language model, drawing on locally gathered data that includes cultural and scientific material, while partnering with the US technology giant Nvidia to build its sovereign AI infrastructure.

Kyslyi said Europe could learn from Ukraine’s experience of deploying technology rapidly while maintaining services under extraordinary pressure, and he explained the speed by saying the country has no other choice. He said Ukraine has to continue to provide the services because they are essential for its citizens, according to the interview with Euronews. Ukrainians can even get married or divorced through the app, he said, highlighting its importance for soldiers on the front lines and for the millions of Ukrainians living abroad. The article was published by Leo Cendrowicz on 18 November 2026 at 9:29 GMT+1, and it describes the wartime push as offering lessons for Europe.

The article does not name any other officials, does not give figures for the rollout, and does not say when the AI assistant or the national language model was first launched. It also does not describe the terms of the partnership with Nvidia or say how far the sovereign AI infrastructure has been built. The context it gives is Russia’s war in Ukraine, which it says has made the country a testing ground for AI-powered military technologies such as self-guided drones. The article does not say what happens next beyond describing the work already under way and the lessons Kyslyi says Europe could draw from it.

stories.Headline: AMD executive warns against using data center GPUs in radio access networks
stories.Summary:
Piotr Weglicki of AMD warned against using data center GPUs in radio access networks on November 18, 2026. He spoke during a recent AI-RAN symposium organized by the company Omdia. Weglicki promoted AMD CPUs as a power efficient answer for telcos. He predicted a big backlash against using power hungry GPUs in these networks. This position follows three years of Nvidia promoting a GPU based RAN vision.

AMD suggests using general purpose CPUs instead of GPUs or custom silicon for the RAN. The company is based in Santa Clara and rivals Intel in x86 architecture CPUs. AMD offers a model with 84 cores, which exceeds the 72 cores in Intel's Granite Rapids. This approach avoids the T2 Telco Accelerator Card and Xilinx FPGAs acquired in early 2022. It targets the L1, L2, and L3 categories of the RAN function stack.

Piotr Weglicki said that general purpose compute is now absorbing the RAN acceleration. He claimed that CPUs provide telcos with data center economics and faster development cycles. Weglicki stated that software based forward error correction on general purpose cores has huge consequences. He argued that operators can then decide how to allocate compute between different workloads. This flexibility allows for better distribution between network tasks and edge applications.

Alok Shah of Samsung Networks said his company has done work with the AMD platform. He noted that the 84 core platform can support meaningful multicell capacity for operators. Nokia is currently using Nvidia GPUs to develop its future 5G and 6G products. Ericsson remains heavily invested in custom silicon, though it has some hardware independent products. Most networks today use custom silicon because it is as energy efficient as possible.

Nvidia helped set up the AI-RAN Alliance nearly three years ago to promote GPU based networks. Intel integrates a hardware accelerator for forward error correction, which AMD called vendor lock-in. AMD previously tried using separate FPGA cards, but telco executives found them too power hungry. Custom silicon is expensive to develop and cannot be sold outside the RAN sector. This makes the return on investment for custom silicon less attractive than CPUs.

AMD needs big RAN vendors to adopt its CPU strategy to make visible progress. Samsung is currently the most likely avenue to market for these AMD processors. Other vendors must develop software only forward error correction to allow a wider rollout. The industry still seems to look at Nvidia for any GPU based RAN needs. It remains open if AMD will develop a lightweight GPU for mobile energy constraints.

Articles.Title: AMD telco chief says GPU 'backlash' is coming in AI-RAN

stories.Headline: Samsung executive Kim says neoclouds hold about 8% of the AI market and pose no major threat to growth
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics, the world’s top maker of memory chips, on Wednesday downplayed concerns that highly leveraged neocloud providers could fuel a broader AI bubble, saying they account for only a small share of the overall market. Kim Yong-kwan, president and head of corporate management, strategy and operation at Samsung’s component business division, spoke at a Morgan Stanley conference in Singapore. The story was refiled to correct an image, with no changes to text, and was reported by Miyoung Kim in Singapore on Nov 18. Shares of neocloud firms including CoreWeave, which rents out computing capacity to tech firms, have been hit by concerns that their debt-fuelled data center expansions could backfire if AI demand slows. The departure of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia this month could also tighten funding for smaller, highly leveraged neocloud companies that have helped fuel the industry’s rapid expansion, analysts and investors have said.

Kim said neoclouds represent a relatively smaller and limited portion of the overall market, approximately 8%. He said Samsung does not expect these concerns to pose a significant threat to the broader AI growth trajectory. Kim said the current AI investment boom was structural rather than cyclical, with long-term contracts between chipmakers and customers providing greater visibility over demand and supply. He said the current boom differed from previous cycles in which speculative investment ultimately led to overcapacity. Kim said today’s investment is not a result of speculation, but actual tangible demand.

Kim also reiterated Samsung’s previous statement that it would carry out its remaining shareholder returns through a mix of cash dividends and a substantial share repurchase and cancellation program. He said the company had a number of factors to consider, including capital expenditures, before announcing details on its shareholder return package in January. Samsung Electronics shares were up 2.31%, and CoreWeave shares were up 0.02%. The conference was a Morgan Stanley event held in Singapore. Kim is president and head of corporate management, strategy and operation at Samsung’s component business division.

stories.Headline: Supergate signs MOU with FPT Semiconductor to cooperate on AI chips and packaging in Vietnam
stories.Summary:
South Korean fabless semiconductor company Supergate signed a memorandum of understanding with Vietnam's FPT Semiconductor on November 18 to cooperate in the artificial intelligence semiconductor business. This partnership was established in connection with the Vietnam, Korea AI and Semiconductor Summit 2026, which took place in Hanoi on November 12. The two companies intend to explore various cooperation opportunities involving semiconductor testing and packaging, cloud services, and vision AI solutions. They will initially focus on handling the testing and packaging of Supergate products within Vietnam.

The agreement requires the companies to jointly explore the local development and commercialization of Supergate's AI system-on-module products. These embedded computing modules integrate processors, memory, and power management onto a single compact circuit board. The partners will also discuss engineering cooperation regarding software integration and AI chip design at the Offshore Development Center of FPT. Furthermore, they will evaluate the technical feasibility of deploying the Tess C100 data center chip developed by Supergate into the cloud infrastructure of FPT.

Employees from both Supergate and FPT will work together at the same location to facilitate this collaboration. The companies will conduct joint testing of AI chips, cloud platforms, and system-on-modules while verifying interoperability and API integration. They also plan to consider joint sales, customer acquisition, and cross-marketing efforts to expand their respective markets. Specific implementation terms and business areas will be determined through separate agreements and subsequent discussions between the two parties.

stories.Headline: Baidu CEO Yanhong Li urges AI industry to prioritize applications to ensure financial returns
stories.Summary:
Yanhong Li, the co-founder and CEO of the Chinese technology giant Baidu, shared his assessment of the artificial intelligence industry on November 18, 2026. He spoke during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, where 2,000 delegates from 21 member states gathered as Presidents Trump and Xi prepared to meet. Li expressed optimism that AI is an inevitable trend, but he warned that the industry faces an urgent situation because the return on investment for use cases has fallen short of expectations. He cautioned that if companies do not see higher revenues or increased profits after adopting the technology, the concern that AI is a bubble could become a reality.

To avoid this outcome, Li argues that the industry must shift its emphasis toward applications, which he considers the most critical of the four AI tiers alongside GPU chips, cloud infrastructure, and large language models. He believes that without practical applications, the other components of the AI ecosystem are useless because long-term competitiveness depends on delivering measurable productivity gains and meaningful business outcomes. Baidu has implemented an application-driven approach by creating a portfolio that includes the general work agent DuMate, the digital human agent Yijing, the self-evolving agent Famou, and the content creation platform KuKu. The company has also integrated internal tools like the AI coding assistant Comate, the workplace agent Dodo, and the vibe coding platform Miaoda to help users complete complex tasks.

Li stated that users are willing to pay for products that consistently save time and solve problems, which creates a significant monetization upside as applications handle higher-value work. He pointed to DuMate as a success story, noting that its monthly active users increased more than 30-fold quarter-over-quarter in September without large-scale marketing campaigns. Regarding the Yijing digital human agent, Li claimed the technology matches or exceeds human hosts in e-commerce live-streaming while reducing production costs by approximately 80 percent. He noted that production time has also decreased by more than an order of magnitude, making these digital humans more scalable for customers.

This push for application-driven value comes as Baidu reports its sixth consecutive quarterly revenue drop amid a global struggle for AI domination between the United States and China. The company continues to optimize specialized agents like KuKu, which was rebranded from GenFlow and utilizes resources from Baidu Drive and Baidu Wenku to help users create high-quality artifacts. By focusing on real-world use cases, Baidu aims to prove that AI can generate actual financial value for enterprises and individual users alike. The company expects that as AI agents take on more complex scenarios, the adoption rate and willingness to pay will continue to grow.

stories.Headline: Paul Bainsfair says agencies must make AI deliver real business value
stories.Summary:
IPA Director General Paul Bainsfair addressed the evolving challenges of artificial intelligence in the November 2026 edition of the IPA AI Magazine. He explained that the industry has moved past the initial stages of experimentation and building capability over the last two years. The current focus must shift toward ensuring that these technological tools provide meaningful value for businesses, clients, and agencies. AI is already being used to optimize media buying, generate research, and support account management teams.

This transition requires agencies to resolve practical issues regarding costs, measurement, and commercial return. The latest magazine examines how AI affects talent, workload, and mental health while analyzing the limitations of synthetic audiences. It also explores the economics of deployment and how AI-mediated customer journeys change the way consumers discover products. These changes force a reevaluation of daily workflows and the overall accountability of agency operations.

Paul Bainsfair stated that putting AI to work is now the easy part of the process. He argued that the real challenge lies in making the technology work for the business. According to Bainsfair, the next phase of adoption depends on how technological promises meet the realities of budgets and data. He noted that AI is no longer on the edges of operations but is actively influencing brand interactions.

The industry is now looking toward how conversational AI and digital sales agents might reshape the entire role of advertising. The IPA AI Magazine intends to provide expert guidance and real-world insight to help leaders create sustainable business value. Future efforts will focus on turning these technological opportunities into practical tools for long-term growth. Agency leaders must now navigate the intersection of innovation and commercial reality.

Articles.Title: IPA Director General Paul Bainsfair Outlines Pressing AI Challenge for Agencies — LBB - LBB

stories.Headline: Fitch Ratings says AI-driven bond issuance will intensify market concentration and raise volatility for exposed issuers
stories.Summary:
Fitch Ratings said on November 18, 2026 that the growth of AI-related bond issuance is likely to boost bond market volatility as the market becomes increasingly tied to the fortunes of hyperscalers. Through the first 10 months of 2026, investment-grade corporate bond issuance in the U.S. reached US$940 billion for non-financial sector companies, which was up 33% from the same period a year ago, driven largely by AI-related issuance. The rating agency said it expects new issues of AI-linked investment-grade corporate debt to continue in the year ahead. Fitch said it does not expect the increase in regulatory uncertainty around data centre development in the U.S. to lead to a major pullback in capex in 2027.

As a result, the bond market's concentration around the AI boom will likely continue to intensify, potentially tightening funding conditions and raising volatility for AI-exposed issuers, Fitch said. It said increased volatility could lead to tighter funding conditions for some issuers, especially if Treasury yields remain elevated and hyperscaler credit profiles or equity valuations weaken, causing spreads to widen. In turn, increased market volatility and tighter funding conditions will raise the risk profile of the overall market, the agency noted. Fitch said issuers in sectors such as health care, technology and utilities that have significant upcoming maturities could face tougher financing conditions, due to higher borrowing costs and the need to time issuance opportunistically when refinancing this debt.

James Langton, a senior reporter with Investment Executive, wrote the article, which was published by Investment Executive on November 18, 2026. The article attributes the outlook and the warnings about funding conditions and volatility to Fitch Ratings, which it describes as a rating agency. The article does not say what Fitch or any other party plans to do next beyond expecting AI-linked investment-grade corporate debt issues to continue in the year ahead. It also does not give any further dates or figures beyond the US$940 billion and 33% figures for the first 10 months of 2026.

stories.Headline: Generali raises its 2027 AI earnings target above €350 million and expects to beat all plan targets
stories.Summary:
Generali raised its artificial intelligence earnings target at its investor day in London on 18 November 2026, confirming it expects to exceed all financial targets from its current strategic plan. The group's current FY2027 AI ambition stands at more than €350 million on its operating result, up from an initial target of approximately €300 million when the plan launched. Generali said it already expects to exceed €200 million on a cumulative run-rate basis by the end of 2026, ahead of that ceiling. The revised 2027 figure came at the FY2025 earnings call in March 2026, when group CEO Philippe Donnet said execution was running ahead of original assumptions, according to a conference call transcript published by Generali. The 16 AI use cases the group is scaling span pricing, underwriting, claims and operations.

Generali's global corporate and commercial business, which serves brokers and medium-to-large corporate clients across more than 180 countries, has already deployed AI in cyber underwriting submissions and multinational programme governance. Its AGORA platform, built in partnership with Capgemini, reduced pre-bind underwriting activity completion time by 80% across 25 countries, according to Capgemini. Faster submissions processing and reduced back-and-forth on multinational programmes are the practical outputs of that investment for the brokers placing business with Generali GC&C. On the underwriting side, Generali said it expects P&C gross written premium growth at a compound annual rate of 6.6% for the first two years of the plan, with the P&C operating result growing at 12% over the same period. In its third-quarter results, Generali absorbed €1.1 billion more in nat cat and large man-made losses than a year before and still kept the P&C combined ratio at 92.8%, while the P&C operating result grew 4.5% to €2.86 billion over the same period.

The life segment's operating result is projected to grow at a 5% compound annual rate between 2024 and 2026, with the new business margin expected to reach approximately 5.9% at year-end. Net inflows reached €25.2 billion cumulated in the period from FY2025 to the first nine months of 2026. Adjusted earnings per share growth is expected to exceed 14% year-on-year by the end of 2026, well above the original 8% to 10% target range. Cumulative net holding cash flow is projected to surpass €7.6 billion for the first two years of the plan, putting the group on track to exceed its more than €11 billion target by the end of 2027.

The investor day sits against the backdrop of a structural shift that takes effect from January 2027, when Generali is consolidating its global insurance markets into five regional clusters, folding its GC&C book under Italy governance and reducing a layer of senior management. The changes were framed as preparation for the final year of the current plan and the cycle that follows. That combination of target-beating financial performance and a leaner operating structure gives Donnet room to set more ambitious targets in the next plan. It also positions Generali to press harder in multinational and commercial lines, where it has been building broker relationships and underwriting capability for the past several years.

Articles.Title: Generali raises AI target as group expects to beat all plan targets

stories.Headline: Nicolas Bouliane says AI Overviews cost All About Berlin 70 to 75 percent of its traffic
stories.Summary:
Nicolas Bouliane, who has run the website All About Berlin since 2017 and has lived from it since 2020, wrote on November 18, 2026 that artificial intelligence is killing his site. After seven years of growth, the website has lost 70 to 75 percent of its traffic to Google AI Overviews, according to his post. When people used to search Google, they got a link to his website, but now they get a page of ads, then an AI-generated answer trained on his content, and only then a link to his site. He described the impact on his traffic as devastating and said it is hard to fund his work with only a quarter of his audience remaining. The change means Bouliane will soon need another way to pay his rent, and he already spends his days preparing for that future instead of writing new guides.

He said he has poured eight years of his life into making something good and useful, and that strangers' faces light up when they learn he runs the site. Local and federal government offices refer people to his guides, the Berlin immigration office uses his data about itself, and his work inspired two government portals and a few similar websites in other cities. If his work just gets mixed into an AI-generated answer, he said, he loses his voice and his audience, his carefully chosen words lose their meaning, and no one shakes his hand, buys him a beer, or tells him how their citizenship application went. Bouliane said this is not an isolated case, because many website owners have reached out in private to commiserate with him. Some of them have paywalled their work, while others have given up and moved on, keeping their websites online but no longer updating them because it is just not worth it.

He said it will get worse, noting that Google made two announcements last week: AI-generated answers will replace search results entirely, and they have ads in them. He called that the future of the internet, with no websites, just a chat box with ads, and said he does not know where All About Berlin fits in that future. The post said the situation was also discussed on Mastodon, Hacker News, LinkedIn and Twitter, and it invited affected people to reach out and let him know how they are doing, because they are not going through this alone. The article listed mentions in The Telegraph, Forbes, The Indicator by NPR, Deutschlandfunk, The Ringer, OMR, PPC Land, Handpicked Berlin, NDTV, Stockhouse, Clarin, Press.pl, H7O magazine, Root.cz, Adevarul and Pineberry. It also linked to similar stories about StackOverflow's traffic being down 99 percent from its peak, about how Google and AI are killing travel blogs, and about what is happening with Liliputing, and it cited Techcrunch as a source.

Articles.Title: AI is killing All About Berlin

stories.Headline: Gallup and Boston Children’s survey finds over a third of young people use AI for companionship
stories.Summary:
Researchers from the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital and Gallup conducted a survey between May and August. They sampled 15,925 people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries to examine how Gen Z forms connections. The findings reveal that more than 33 percent of these young people rely on artificial intelligence for companionship. This figure rises to 50 percent among those who use AI daily and reaches 42 percent for those with online-only friends.

The report indicates that while in-person friendships provide the most positive emotional experiences, digital bonds are common. Nearly half of young people in the United States have at least one close friend they have never met in real life. Instagram and Discord are the primary platforms used in the US to maintain these online-only affiliations. Men often find digital acquaintances through gaming, whereas women typically use social media to cultivate their connections. The study suggests that those relying on AI or online-only friends may face higher odds of loneliness.

David Bickham, the research director of the Digital Wellness Lab, stated that adolescents seek various contexts to socialize. He explained that young people growing up with AI are simply more engaged with its social capabilities. Bickham noted that while AI can fill a social gap, it cannot fully compensate for loneliness. Andrew Dugan, a principal researcher at Gallup, suggested that AI companionship will likely become more common over the next five years. He questioned whether AI reinforces lonely feelings or serves as a necessary tool for those who feel isolated.

This research arrives as countries like Australia and the UK implement social media bans and age restrictions for minors. In the United States, many citizens support banning social media for children under 16, and some legislators want to curb addictive design features. Experts like Jon-Patrick Allem argue that measuring total screen time is a deficient approach to understanding youth mental health. Instead, they advocate for investigating the actual content consumed and the quality of the relationships formed online.

Articles.Title: A Gallup survey of 15,925 people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries finds that more than 33% rely on AI for companionship, rising to 50% among daily AI users (Jason Parham/Wired)

stories.headline_source: A Gallup survey of 15,925 people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries finds that more than 33% rely on AI for companionship, rising to 50% among daily AI users

stories.Headline: Apacer wins Taiwan Excellence Award for BiCLO AI accelerator powered by DEEPX chips
stories.Summary:
The Taiwanese company Apacer developed an edge artificial intelligence accelerator card called BiCLO that won a 2027 Taiwan Excellence Award. This achievement was announced by the fabless semiconductor company DEEPX on November 18, 2026, regarding the recognized hardware. The award winning device utilizes specialized neural processing units to enhance computing capabilities at the edge of a network. This specific recognition comes from a comprehensive evaluation of research, design, quality, and marketing conducted by the Ministry of Economic Affairs in Taiwan. The BiCLO accelerator card incorporates two DX-M1M neural processing units and utilizes a standard PCI Express interface for connectivity.

Each individual chip provides 25 trillion operations per second of AI computing performance while utilizing 2GB of SRAM. The total system delivers 50 TOPS of computing performance while maintaining a low power consumption of approximately 10 watts. Because each chip consumes about 5 watts, the device can process dozens of video streams, such as CCTV feeds, without any latency. This architecture allows for real-time processing and storage at the edge to reduce the risk of leaking information to external cloud servers. DEEPX is the entity responsible for developing the neural processing units that power the award winning BiCLO accelerator card.

The company stated that the hardware is designed to perform inference on multiple video streams simultaneously to improve efficiency. They highlighted that the technology is particularly useful for applications in smart cities, transportation systems, and various manufacturing facilities. By keeping data processing local, the system avoids the security vulnerabilities associated with transmitting sensitive information over a network. The company believes this approach provides a more secure alternative to traditional cloud based AI processing. More to follow.

Articles.Title: DEEPX-Powered AI Accelerator Wins Taiwan Excellence Award - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.headline_source: DEEPX-Powered AI Accelerator Wins Taiwan Excellence Award

stories.Headline: Texas environmental regulators grant SpaceX an air permit for a 750-megawatt gas plant at Starbase
stories.Summary:
The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality issued an air permit on Monday, Nov. 16, for a gas-fired power plant that SpaceX plans to build to run a supercomputing data center in the Rio Grande Valley, Politico reported on Nov. 17. TCEQ spokesperson Laura Lopez confirmed the issuance and said the agency had resumed its normal permit review process. The plant would generate 750 megawatts from 35 natural gas-burning turbines on a 444-acre site in the Brownsville area that was annexed to the city of Starbase in September, and it would not connect to the state grid. SpaceX did not respond to Politico's requests for comment. The permit allows the plant to emit up to 248 tons of nitrogen oxides a year, just below the 250-ton-a-year threshold that triggers a more extensive review, including a public hearing.

SpaceX filed for the permit on Sept. 8 under TCEQ's standard permit for electric generating units, with an initial set of 35 turbines from GE Vernova, Mitsubishi and Solar Turbines, later to be replaced by eight larger GE Vernova 7E units. The permit came three days after FracTracker Alliance and Public Citizen filed a complaint with TCEQ alleging that SpaceX had begun building at the site without a permit, in violation of the Clean Air Act, citing satellite and aerial images of cranes and gas turbines between Oct. 9 and Nov. 12. Kathryn Guerra of Public Citizen said the TCEQ is attempting to quickly and quietly move data center air permits forward, and Public Citizen has called on TCEQ's commissioners to resign. Gov. Greg Abbott ordered TCEQ in a Sept. 21 letter to stop approving data center permits until the grid operator, ERCOT, completed a review of data centers seeking grid connections. TCEQ received notice from Abbott's office on Friday, Nov. 13, that grid officials had finished gathering information on potential community impacts, one of several issues Abbott asked them to study, and it then resumed reviews, the Texas Tribune reported.

ERCOT plans to present its full findings to the Public Utility Commission on Dec. 10. Abbott's office did not respond to requests for comment from either outlet, and Abbott lost the Nov. 3 election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who pledged during the campaign to keep data center approvals paused until the Legislature passes new state laws. SpaceX said on Nov. 12 that it plans to invest more than $24 billion in an AI supercomputing campus at Starbase and about $50 billion in a second campus in Cochise County, Arizona. Starbase has posted notice of a Dec. 9 hearing on SpaceX's request for a property tax abatement, which says the company plans to construct, own and operate a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility, Politico reported. SpaceX's AI unit, the former xAI, has run into permitting fights over gas turbines at its Memphis-area data centers.

Articles.Title: Texas issues the air permit for SpaceX's 750-megawatt gas plant at Starbase as data center permits resume - MLQ.ai

stories.headline_source: Texas issues the air permit for SpaceX's 750-megawatt gas plant at Starbase as data center permits resume

stories.Headline: MangoBoost and PFN sign AI inference infrastructure agreement and plan AI Token Factory proof of concept
stories.Summary:
MangoBoost and Preferred Networks, also known as PFN, signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18 to collaborate on artificial intelligence inference infrastructure technologies. The two companies intend to conduct a proof of concept for a next-generation architecture called the AI Token Factory. This partnership aims to increase AI inference throughput and reduce latency to improve overall system utilization. An official signing ceremony for this agreement will take place at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago between November 15 and November 20.

The proposed heterogeneous computing system combines MangoBoost data processing units and storage solutions with PFN MN-Core AI inference processors and AMD graphics processing units. AMD GPUs will manage the prefill stage for processing input instructions, while PFN chips will handle the decode stage to generate tokens. MangoBoost will provide key-value cache pooling storage and prefill-decode disaggregation solutions to optimize data transfers and memory management. These specialized data processing units are designed to handle communications, security processing, and storage input and output within the AI infrastructure.

Jangwoo Kim, the CEO of MangoBoost, and Takahiro Ogura, a division head at PFN, are leading this collaborative effort to optimize computing resources and networking. The companies stated that they will first validate the new architecture within a simulation environment to test its effectiveness. Once samples of the MN-Core L1000 chip are available, the partners will expand their testing to include performance validation on actual hardware. They also plan to consider publishing a joint research paper based on the results of these evaluations.

Articles.Title: MangoBoost, PFN Partner on Heterogeneous AI Inference Systems - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.headline_source: MangoBoost, PFN Partner on Heterogeneous AI Inference Systems

stories.Headline: Darío Gil calls AI, quantum and supercomputing the three legs of a stool for science
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration’s second term has brought deep funding cuts and delays to many fields of science, including public health and climate research, according to Science News. Artificial intelligence and quantum science, by contrast, have found firmer footing under the same administration. Darío Gil, the undersecretary for science at the U.S. Department of Energy, described these technologies, together with supercomputing, as the three legs of a stool that will transform how science and engineering is done. The article, written by Emily Conover and published on November 16, 2026, reports this contrast in how different research areas have fared.

The article does not give specific budget figures, program names or dates beyond the publication date and the administration’s second term. It says only that AI and quantum science have found firmer footing while other fields have struggled with funding cuts and delays. Gil’s comment places supercomputing alongside AI and quantum as one of three pillars for future science and engineering. The piece presents these as the topics the administration has chosen to favor.

Gil, the undersecretary for science at the Department of Energy, is the only person quoted in the article. He said the three technologies are going to be the three legs of the stool that is going to transform how science and engineering is done. The article does not attribute any other statements to administration officials or to researchers in the affected fields. It also does not say what specific actions the administration has taken on AI, quantum or supercomputing.

The context the article gives is that many fields of science have struggled under the second Trump administration, with public health and climate science among those hit by funding cuts and delays. Against that backdrop, AI and quantum science stand out as areas with firmer footing. The article does not say what happens next, whether through new funding, legislation or agency programs. It offers no timeline for future decisions on these technologies.

Articles.Title: What the Trump administration’s focus on AI and quantum means for science - Science News

stories.headline_source: What the Trump administration’s focus on AI and quantum means for science

stories.Headline: Microsoft launches Cobalt 200 AI servers as agent workloads demand far more computing
stories.Summary:
Microsoft formally launched servers equipped with the Cobalt 200 on November 17, which is an in-house central processing unit for artificial intelligence. This move follows the development of the Maia custom processor series intended to replace graphics processing units from Nvidia and AMD. The company is responding to a surge in demand for central processing units as the market shifts from chatbots to autonomous agents. These agents act as assistants that carry out tasks on their own rather than just generating text.

This transition requires significantly more infrastructure and processing capacity because agent-based workloads operate autonomously to generate outputs. Alistair Speirs, the general manager of Azure infrastructure at Microsoft, noted that developers can consume up to 3,000 times more computing resources than existing chatbots or the generative Copilot. He explained that this level of capacity cannot be built immediately because it would require several times the size of existing data centers. Even utilizing every high-performance chip in the world would not make such a scale achievable right now.

Alistair Speirs stated that the shift toward agentic AI makes inference more important, which increases the standing of central processing units. While graphics processing units were central to the generative AI era due to machine learning, the new era relies more on the brain-like functions of the CPU. Other companies have also entered this space, with users turning to personal agents like Anthropic's Claude Duet, OpenAI's Dots, and Meta's Muse. These tools have been used in earnest by various companies since last year.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Says AI Agents Can Use 3,000 Times More Computing Than Chatbots - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.headline_source: Microsoft Says AI Agents Can Use 3,000 Times More Computing Than Chatbots

stories.Headline: ZeroEyes holds advanced talks with Chicago on AI gun detection pilot
stories.Summary:
ZeroEyes, a company whose artificial intelligence software detects visible firearms on existing security cameras, is in fairly advanced talks with Mayor Brandon Johnson's administration to join a Chicago public safety technology pilot that could launch early next year, the company's chief strategy officer Kieran Carroll said in a CBS Chicago report published November 17, 2026. The system is already used at Navy Pier and, after a pilot that began in 2024, at all Chicago Transit Authority train stations, where the CTA says it has led to 30 arrests. The possible pilot follows a referendum in which more than 72 percent of Chicago voters backed bringing gunshot detection technology back to the city. City Hall has not confirmed which companies will take part.

Carroll said ZeroEyes is not an acoustic detection system and would not directly replace ShotSpotter, the gunshot detection technology Johnson shut down in Chicago in 2024, but could complement one. The software plugs into existing cameras, looks for a visible gun, and sends images to the company's team for review and verification before alerts go to security on the ground, which Carroll said means a city pilot could be running within weeks. The company says the technology uses no facial recognition, does not record, and does not store or train on customer data, and that screenshots are typically purged within 30 days, or sooner if a customer wants a stricter procedure. In 2024, Navy Pier Security Director Dan O'Shea praised the system, saying police need to know anytime a weapon is displayed.

Johnson said Tuesday he is less concerned with a speedy rollout than with finding the right system, saying the city needs systems that work and that his urgency is in getting it right. At a special City Council meeting on Wednesday, alders will vote on an ordinance directing the city's chief procurement officer to finalize negotiations and issue a new contract for acoustic gunshot detection technology within 30 days. If no contract is awarded within 60 days, the officer would have to give the chair of the Committee on Contracting Oversight and Equity a written explanation and could be called to testify at a public hearing. Several City Council members have been frustrated by the lack of transparency over which companies will be in the pilot.

Articles.Title: Chicago public safety technology pilot program could include AI-powered gun detection system used at Navy PIer - CBS News

stories.headline_source: Chicago public safety technology pilot program could include AI-powered gun detection system used at Navy PIer

stories.Headline: Okta Korea's Hwang Kyu-eon says AI agents drive record enterprise revenue and a push into banking
stories.Summary:
Okta expanded its enterprise business in South Korea recently to address rising hacking threats and the spread of artificial intelligence agents. Hwang Kyu-eon, the country manager of Okta Korea, discussed these developments on November 19 at a press briefing. This event took place ahead of the Oktane on the Road Seoul conference held at Hotel Eliena in Seoul's Gangnam district. The company is seeing a surge in demand for unified security solutions as corporations manage more accounts and access privileges. This growth has led to the highest revenue recorded since the Korean unit was first established.

The company plans to focus on winning commercial banks and other financial sector clients starting in the next year. Okta already provides security solutions to some financial firms and has applied its technology to an internet only bank's internal network. To support this expansion, the company intends to add finance specialists to its team during the coming year. The business requires the easing of regulatory constraints regarding the use of software as a service within internal financial networks. These specific changes are necessary because current rules limit how the company can apply its software in those environments.

Hwang Kyu-eon stated that domestic enterprise revenue overtook the commercial segment starting last year as large corporations adopted the solutions. He noted that domestic revenue grew by double digits this year, which is a rate that outpaces the company's global growth. Hwang explained that a few departments at large companies typically use the solution first before expanding it across the organization. He argued that stitching together individual security solutions creates fragmented visibility, which becomes a security threat for the company. He also mentioned that the company must now monitor abnormal behavior after login because attackers often hijack sessions.

Large corporations and financial firms are affected by the need to manage identities and credentials that serve as primary attack paths. Companies find it difficult to manage accounts consistently when they operate multiple separate security solutions across their different internal systems. For example, access privileges may remain on some systems even after an employee leaves the company or changes their department. This lack of coordination means that abnormal behavior detected on one system might not trigger an immediate block on others. Consequently, systems that can quickly trace an intruder's actions and cut off access have become more important for these firms.

The growth is driven by three shifts, including the addition of AI agents to employees and existing corporate systems. These AI agents increase the number of accounts and access privileges that a company must manage to remain secure. In April of this year, Okta launched Okta for AI Agents to detect unidentified agents and manage their activity. In September, the company launched the Blueprint Alliance with Zscaler, CrowdStrike, and Amazon Web Services to share security warning signs. This alliance allows participating global firms to coordinate responses, such as blocking access, across their linked security systems.

Okta Korea will use the Oktane on the Road Seoul event to present its unified security strategy for the AI era. The company will discuss specific solutions to the security challenges that companies face as they multiply their AI agents. They will continue to target the financial sector while hoping for regulatory changes to allow broader software as a service use. The articles leave open whether the Korean government will actually ease the regulatory constraints on financial internal networks. It remains unclear how many new commercial banks will adopt the technology in the coming year.

Articles.Title: Okta's Korean Enterprise Sales Surge as AI Agents Multiply Accounts - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.headline_source: Okta's Korean Enterprise Sales Surge as AI Agents Multiply Accounts

stories.Headline: TrendForce predicts HBM4 memory prices will rise to between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit in 2027
stories.Summary:
TrendForce forecast memory price changes during its Roadshow Korea in Seoul on November 18, 2026. The firm predicted that sixth generation HBM4 memory prices will rise significantly next year. These costs will increase from $2.05 per gigabit in 2026 to a new range. The expected 2027 price band is between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit. This represents a price gain of about 46% to 168%.

HBM4E prices should exceed $5 per gigabit with terms set in early 2027. General DRAM contract prices will rise 10% to 15% in late 2026. These gains narrow to 0% to 5% by the second half of 2027. HBM will use 30% of DRAM wafer input in 2027, up from 23%. HBM4 doubled the interface to 2,048 bits, according to the provided reports.

TrendForce stated that 8-high HBM stacks carry a 10% to 20% per-gigabit premium. They explained that base die costs do not shrink as DRAM layers increase. SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung told Reuters that 2027 would be the worst supply year. Micron said 75% of fiscal 2027 volume is committed at prices above 2026 levels. Samsung reportedly seeks a mid-to-high $4 range per gigabit for HBM4.

GPU and ASIC makers are considering less HBM per device because supply is scarce. IDC projects PC shipments will fall 11.3% in 2026 with no relief through 2027. A June 25 class action alleges HBM is a pretext to restrict older chips. This lawsuit was filed in the Northern District of California under the Sherman Act. Cloud giants face higher memory costs, which Nvidia uses to justify server price hikes.

HBM bits consume three to four times the wafer area of conventional DRAM bits. One 12-high HBM4 stack from Micron holds 36 GB, which equals 288 gigabits. Nvidia's Vera Rubin accelerator uses eight such stacks for a total of 2,304 gigabits. China's CXMT and YMTC appear on the Pentagon's Section 1260H list of military companies. YMTC has been on the U.S. Entity List since December 2022.

New DRAM capacity will begin ramping in the second half of 2027. Substantial output contributions from this new capacity are not expected until 2028. NAND supply sufficiency is forecast to turn positive in 2027 as new capacity arrives. Enterprise SSD price growth is expected to accelerate in the fourth quarter of 2026. The articles leave open whether Samsung will confirm individual 2027 contract price terms.

Articles.Title: HBM4 Memory Price Forecast: TrendForce Sees $3 to $5.50 Per Gigabit Next Year, Up From $2.05 Now - Tech Times

stories.Headline: Applied Materials posts record DRAM revenue and raises 2026 packaging growth outlook
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials is seeing growing demand tied to AI infrastructure, as chipmakers look to expand DRAM production and meet rising high-bandwidth memory requirements, according to a Zacks article published by Yahoo Finance on November 16, 2026. The company said most leading-edge DRAM fabs are running at full capacity. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, DRAM revenues within its Semiconductor Systems segment rose 52% year over year to a record level. Applied Materials also introduced enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD tools, which it says improve DRAM performance and enable higher-layer-count HBM. Management expects a sizable increase in DRAM revenues during the second half of 2026, keeping memory-related process spending central to the company's growth.

Applied Materials now expects advanced packaging revenues to grow more than 70% in 2026, up from its prior outlook of more than 50%. The company is extending its portfolio across HBM and 3D chiplet stacking with Nokota VMax 2 plating, Opta Quad CMP and two new eBeam systems for metrology and defect analysis. The article notes that the benefits depend on sustained customer capital spending, since memory remains a cyclical industry. The article states that Applied Materials' broad portfolio positions it to capture a larger share of customer spending while keeping competitors like Lam Research and Camtek at bay. Lam Research competes across deposition and etch technologies, including advanced atomic layer deposition systems, while Camtek focuses on inspection, metrology, advanced packaging and high-performance computing applications.

Applied Materials shares have climbed 44.2% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, which appreciated 7% and 8.1% respectively. The stock trades at a price-to-sales multiple of 6.38X, above the industry's 3.01X, and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Applied Materials' fiscal 2026 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 42.4%, and the estimates have been revised upward in the past seven days. The article frames the memory demand trend as a likely tailwind for the company in 2026 and beyond, provided customer capital spending holds up.

Articles.Title: Can Applied Materials Capitalize on Rising HBM Demand in 2026? - Yahoo Finance

stories.Headline: Germany and ten EU states urge the European Commission to propose AI copyright rules
stories.Summary:
On November 17, 2026, Euronews reported that Germany and ten other European Union member states urged the European Commission to propose new copyright legislation for the AI era. These eleven countries requested that the Commission create new rules and make the existing opt-out for creators easier to enforce. The group included Austria, Croatia, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Spain. This joint appeal seeks to protect human creative work while simultaneously enabling AI innovation within Europe.

The proposed changes would build upon the current AI Act, which already requires general-purpose AI model providers to maintain a copyright policy. These providers must also publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used for training their models. The European Commission recently held a targeted consultation that closed on November 10, 2026, after an extension from its original deadline. This consultation covered four specific areas, including online piracy, copyright in scientific research, and the use of protected content by AI.

The European Commission is responsible for managing these policies and has stated that current provider obligations are distinct from the existing copyright opt-out. The member states argued that stronger enforcement is necessary to ensure that the rights of creators are respected in the digital age. According to reports, the Commission has scheduled a broader package regarding copyright, simplification, and digital transformation for the second quarter of 2027. This upcoming package will likely address the concerns raised by the eleven member states.

Articles.Title: EU AI copyright proposal: 11 states urge new rules - NeoTeo

stories.headline_source: EU AI copyright proposal: 11 states urge new rules

stories.Headline: German official urges innovation-friendly EU AI rules to keep pace with US and Asia
stories.Summary:
A prominent German official said in mid November 2026 that Europe’s current rules for artificial intelligence risk holding back domestic innovation, and called for a more innovation-friendly approach so the bloc can compete with AI leaders in the United States and Asia. The intervention came as the EU AI Act, the world’s first comprehensive law for AI, moves from legislative debate into enforcement across member states. German officials argued that fundamental rights and safety remain paramount, but that implementation must be calibrated to avoid disproportionate burdens on research environments and early-stage startups. They focused on flexible mechanisms inside the existing structure rather than rigid compliance requirements.

Germany is implementing the act through a national statute, the KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz, known as KI-MIG, which sets up market surveillance while seeking to balance oversight with competitive innovation. A central pillar of the German proposal is expanding and accelerating AI regulatory sandboxes, called KI-Reallabore, which give researchers and startups controlled, supervised environments to test systems without the threat of immediate enforcement. The call also includes demands for more investment in computing infrastructure, avoidance of heavy taxation on technology, and improved access to compute for academic and industrial research hubs. The European Commission has already begun recalibrating enforcement timelines through AI Omnibus packages, so technical standards and compliance tools can mature before penalties are levied.

Some research institutions and university technology transfer offices welcomed the emphasis on flexibility, citing the risk that compliance costs could cause a regulatory brain drain as top researchers move to less prohibitive jurisdictions. Civil society groups cautioned that innovation-friendly language could be used as a euphemism to weaken oversight, warning that exemptions to safety and ethics requirements could have long-term consequences for AI-assisted research outcomes. Industry associations such as eco in Germany have argued that European competitiveness in enterprise AI and industrial automation is increasingly disadvantaged by compliance costs and uncertainty. Research offices must now navigate national details such as KI-MIG that may differ slightly in their approach to sandboxes and enforcement.

The debate will likely intensify as the European Commission gathers feedback on the first wave of AI Act implementation, and future adjustments, including guidance on how researchers can use regulatory sandboxes, will be crucial. Research administrators should monitor national announcements from their respective AI agencies about the formal opening of sandbox applications and support tools for high-risk system classification. Universities should expect a period of regulatory learning in which they engage actively with national AI bodies, especially where high-risk AI research is involved. The call for enhanced compute infrastructure underscores that European research institutions will need stable, competitive compute resources to remain attractive to top-tier AI researchers.

Articles.Title: Germany: EU AI Rules Need Innovation Focus - CASRAI

stories.headline_source: Germany: EU AI Rules Need Innovation Focus

stories.Headline: Taiwan Mask expands 14-inch capacity to target advanced packaging and silicon photonics growth
stories.Summary:
Taiwan Mask, which operates as a subsidiary of the Star Fusion Group, announced an expansion of its 14-inch capacity on November 18, 2026. The company is currently overhauling its product mix to better capture surging market demand. This strategic shift focuses on growth within the sectors of advanced packaging and silicon photonics. The firm is also targeting the increasing need for advanced-node photomasks in the industry. These operational changes require the company to expand its overseas presence to reach more global customers.

The expansion specifically targets the growth of CoWoS technology and other advanced packaging solutions. By increasing its 14-inch capacity, the company aims to support the complex requirements of modern semiconductor manufacturing. These technical upgrades are designed to align with the rapid evolution of AI and photonics. The leadership at Taiwan Mask is responsible for these changes to ensure the company remains competitive.

They stated that the overhaul is necessary to capture the rising demand for specialized chip components. The company believes that diversifying its product offerings will lead to sustainable long-term growth. This move reflects a broader industry trend toward more sophisticated packaging and photonic integration. More to follow.

stories.Headline: ECIJA appoints María Luisa Mena Durán as Of Counsel in Valencia to lead AI governance and AI Act advisory work
stories.Summary:
The law firm ECIJA appointed María Luisa Mena Durán as Of Counsel at its Valencia office on November 17, 2026. This strategic hire aims to strengthen the firm's advisory capabilities regarding artificial intelligence and digital law. Mena brings over 20 years of professional experience and a strong academic record in technology law to the team. She currently serves as the Vice-Dean of the Faculty of Law, Business and Political Science at CEU Cardenal Herrera University.

This new role requires Mena to expand the firm's specialization within the Technology, Media and Telecommunications practice group. She will focus on governance, technology regulation, and the implementation of the European Artificial Intelligence Regulation, also known as the AI Act. Her responsibilities include designing governance models, preparing specialized legal reports, and developing AI literacy initiatives for clients. Mena holds a PhD in Law and an LL.M. in Transnational Law from King’s College London.

Salvador Silvestre, a partner at ECIJA Valencia, stated that businesses face new regulatory challenges that require highly specialized advice. He noted that Mena's academic and practical background will help clients adopt new technologies with strategic vision and legal certainty. Mena explained that the primary legal challenge is translating new regulatory frameworks into practical solutions for safe innovation. She believes joining ECIJA allows her to apply her expertise in technology contracts to a firm focused on digital innovation.

The appointment responds to an increasing demand from businesses for specialist advice as artificial intelligence integrates into corporate processes. Mena has previously published a 2026 monograph on algorithmic contracting and has lectured at institutions like ESADE and IE Executive Education. She also coordinates the TECH Law diploma programme at CEU Cardenal Herrera University. ECIJA intends to use this expansion to better support organizations during their digital transformation and adaptation to new laws.

stories.Headline: TrendForce projects HBM4 prices will rise up to 2.7 times next year due to AI demand
stories.Summary:
Market research firm TrendForce projected on November 18, 2026, that prices for sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM4, will rise significantly next year. This increase is driven by the growing demand for artificial intelligence accelerators and a shift in production strategies by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. The firm expects HBM4 prices to reach between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit in 2027, which is up to 2.7 times the 2026 price of $2.05 per gigabit. Additionally, the seventh-generation HBM4E is expected to cost more than $5 per gigabit, with clearer pricing arriving in the first half of 2027.

This price surge requires a shift in manufacturing, as Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Micron will increase HBM wafer input from 23 percent in 2026 to nearly 30 percent in 2027. Because HBM consumes three to four times more wafers than standard memory, PC DRAM bit supply is forecast to decline by 7.9 percent while HBM supply grows by 65.7 percent. Consequently, conventional DRAM prices are expected to rise 10 to 15 percent in the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by smaller quarterly gains throughout 2027. Meanwhile, China's CXMT may increase its DRAM capacity by 20 percent in 2027, though U.S. export controls on graphics processing units limit its current growth.

Senior researcher Ellie Wang stated that strong momentum should continue through 2027 because of expanding investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. She noted that global cloud service providers will likely increase capital expenditure by 104 percent in 2026 and another 60 percent in 2027 to reach $1.5158 trillion. Wang explained that the market direction after 2028 will depend on the balance between demand and the opening of new production facilities. She suggested that memory prices might reach an inflection point around the middle of 2028 as the current boom potentially slows down.

The market may shift between 2028 and 2030 as new plants, including the Pyeongtaek P5 plant and the Yongin semiconductor cluster, begin operations. Samsung Electronics plans to build two phases of Pyeongtaek P5 with monthly capacities of 200,000 wafers each, while SK hynix intends to add 300,000 wafers per month at Yongin. These expansions will increase overall manufacturing capacity, though HBM shipment growth is projected to decelerate from 50 percent in 2027 to around 10 percent in 2028. CXMT also plans to add 100,000 to 200,000 wafers per month after 2028, which could further impact global supply.

stories.Headline: Nvidia moves to annual GPUs as Vera Rubin holds HBM capacity flat
stories.Summary:
Nvidia has moved to annual GPU introductions, and its Vera Rubin generation keeps about 288 GB of HBM per GPU while delivering more than twice the memory bandwidth of Blackwell Ultra, 24/7 Wall St. reported on November 18, 2026. Dr. Robert Castellano wrote the article for the site. The piece said the annual upgrade cycle no longer produces consistent increases in high-bandwidth memory capacity per GPU. It said Micron and other memory manufacturers can benefit from HBM4’s higher performance and pricing. It said future revenue growth will depend increasingly on system shipments, memory technology, and manufacturing economics.

The article’s Table 1 gives HBM per GPU and memory technology from 2020 to 2027. The A100 of 2020 had 80 GB of HBM2e, the H100 of 2022 had 80 GB of HBM3, the B200 Blackwell of 2024 had 192 GB of HBM3e, and the B300 Blackwell Ultra of 2025 had 288 GB of HBM3e. Vera Rubin in 2026 has 288 GB of HBM4, and Rubin Ultra in 2027 is projected at about 1 TB of HBM4e. The article said capacity rose from 80 GB in the H100 to 288 GB in the B300, a 3.6-fold increase, and that the B200 to B300 step raised capacity from 192 GB to 288 GB, an increase of 50%. The article names Micron Technology, Samsung Electronics, and SK hynix as the three principal suppliers of advanced HBM.

It said Micron has invested heavily in HBM manufacturing technology, advanced packaging, and DRAM capacity to expand its participation in AI infrastructure. It said Micron’s investment opportunity increasingly depends on qualification for successive GPU generations, manufacturing yields, and the profitability of higher-value memory products. It said SK hynix has established a strong position in advanced HBM and benefits from its manufacturing experience and relationships with leading AI accelerator customers. It said Samsung is pursuing the same opportunity through advanced DRAM manufacturing and HBM packaging investments. The article said the central investment question is whether future HBM revenue growth will be driven primarily by increasing memory capacity per accelerator or by higher-value memory technology, more systems deployed, and improved manufacturing economics.

It said the distinction matters because these factors can produce very different revenue and profitability outcomes for memory suppliers. It said HBM4 provides substantially higher bandwidth through a more advanced memory architecture, including a wider interface and more demanding manufacturing requirements. It said these improvements increase the value and complexity of the memory supplied, even when the number of installed gigabytes remains unchanged. It said revenue can increase through higher selling prices and a richer product mix without a comparable increase in total memory capacity. The article’s Table 2 compares rack-level HBM capacity and bandwidth.

The GB200 NVL72 contains approximately 13.4 TB of HBM across 72 GPUs, rising to 20.7 TB in the GB300 NVL72, a 54.7% expansion. Vera Rubin NVL72 maintains approximately 20.7 TB while increasing aggregate HBM bandwidth from 576 TB/s to 1,400 TB/s, about 2.4 times the bandwidth with no increase in installed HBM capacity per rack. The article said a hypothetical deployment of 10,000 GB300 NVL72 racks would require approximately 207,000 TB of HBM capacity, and that replacing them with 10,000 Vera Rubin NVL72 systems would require approximately the same aggregate HBM capacity. It said 15,000 Rubin racks would raise total installed HBM to approximately 310,500 TB, an increase of 50%, with that growth coming from additional systems rather than greater memory capacity per system. The article said Nvidia explained in a recent technical discussion of memory optimization how hardware and software improvements can increase the amount of useful computation performed with a given quantity of memory.

It said the company reported that Vera Rubin NVL72 can deliver up to 30 times the agentic AI throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72 in a specified workload, even though installed HBM capacity remains approximately unchanged. It said that figure is workload-specific and should not be interpreted as a universal 30-fold performance improvement. It said the transition from H100 to B300 combined increasing GPU shipments with a dramatic expansion in memory installed per accelerator, multiplying demand for advanced DRAM capacity. It said Rubin Ultra could eventually reverse the capacity plateau if Nvidia delivers approximately 1 TB of HBM per GPU. The article said investors should distinguish that projected future increase from the current Rubin architecture rather than assuming every annual GPU transition follows the same pattern.

It said higher bandwidth alone does not guarantee higher revenue if pricing premiums decline or production costs increase. It said a supplier that achieves strong HBM4 yields could capture meaningful margin benefits, while one experiencing production difficulties could face higher costs despite favorable demand. It said Samsung’s ability to improve yields and secure high-volume customer qualifications will influence its participation in the next generation. The article ended mid-sentence at “the next,” leaving Samsung’s outlook and the rest of its assessment unfinished. More to follow.
