stories.Headline: Commentary: Despite AI Boom, China’s Chipmakers Have Yet to Catch Up to Nvidia
stories.Summary:
Chinese semiconductor shares recently experienced a rally, but this financial trend does not indicate a technical breakthrough in computing power. Domestic AI chip companies are expanding their reach because restrictions on American technology provide strong incentives for local buyers. However, engineers still require significant time to build reliable alternatives to the hardware produced by Nvidia Corp. The primary challenge is whether these domestic chips can run leading AI models reliably and economically at scale. Industry estimates for 2025 place the combined accelerator revenue of seven public Chinese suppliers at approximately 17.7 billion yuan, or 2.7 billion dollars. Including smaller independent vendors brings that total to roughly 3 billion dollars, while Huawei is estimated to contribute another 10 to 11 billion dollars.

Total domestic market revenue for 2025 is expected to reach between 13 and 14 billion dollars. Projections for 2026 suggest the listed group will earn 5 to 5.5 billion dollars, while Huawei Ascend could reach 15.5 to 18 billion dollars. The author of the commentary argues that a captive market should not be confused with a competitive product. They state that Chinese developers still prefer Nvidia because of the mature CUDA software platform and superior cluster reliability. The author suggests that China must compete at the system level, using strategies like the Huawei supernode to overcome manufacturing limits.

They believe vendors must provide transparent benchmarks and compatibility with frameworks like PyTorch and vLLM to reduce switching costs. The domestic industry currently faces obstacles regarding advanced fabrication capacity and high-bandwidth memory, which limit the delivery of competitive accelerators. Reliance on regulatory loopholes to obtain foreign hardware is described as a vulnerability rather than a sound industrial policy. To succeed, the author claims that China must direct more engineering toward domestic systems and demand measurable results. Future progress depends on whether these companies can move beyond demonstration projects to create repeat deployments that actually work.

Articles.Title: Commentary: Despite AI Boom, China’s Chipmakers Have Yet to Catch Up to Nvidia - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: DeepSeek limits user access to its AI services due to insufficient computing capacity
stories.Summary:
DeepSeek restricted conversations and document reading on its website and app due to insufficient computing capacity. These restrictions began on November 15 for individual users of the service. The company limited the processing of long conversations that were inactive for 72 hours. Document reading was also capped at 10,000 tokens or the first 20 pages. These changes expose constraints pushing Chinese AI developers to seek growth beyond large models.

DeepSeek charges only via API and lacks a paid consumer tier for its users. On November 13, it announced application APIs for online search, file input, and model safety. Text and image search fees are 5 yuan per 1,000 calls, while text recognition costs 1.5 yuan. Z.AI shares closed at HK$335 on November 17, down 32.9 percent over four trading days. MiniMax shares closed at HK$116 on November 17, falling 35.6 percent over four trading days.

Yao Shuqiao of Haitong International said DeepSeek must allocate limited resources to paying customers. He expects computing power to remain tight and demand to grow exponentially by 2027. Yao also noted a broader cutoff risk tied to developments regarding Nvidia Corp. AI expert Xiao Rui compared the model to a horse and the harness to equipment. Xiao characterized harness development as an engineering challenge rather than a computing capacity challenge.

Users on Xiaohongshu complained about restrictions and offered to pay for a subscription service. Moonshot AI suspended new Kimi K3 subscriptions in July and apologized for rate limits. Enterprise customers now generate more than 70 percent of revenue for Moonshot AI's Kimi. A Menlo Ventures report says Chinese models account for 89 percent of U.S. enterprise spending. Z.AI announced a cooperation agreement with China Mobile for token technology and industry solutions.

Chinese labs are slowing foundational model advances to emphasize agents, software tools, and partnerships. DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash on September 10 but has not released a Pro version. MiniMax has not yet released its Pro model which has roughly 3 trillion parameters. Moonshot AI launched Kimi Hosted Agents on November 5 for running agents in the cloud. DeepSeek introduced its MIT-licensed DeepSeek Harness on August 13 to lower participation barriers.

DeepSeek launched a desktop version on September 29 that reached 1.5 million daily users. Daily token consumption for this version reached around 92 trillion by November 4. Harness-optimized smaller models can deliver 90 percent of larger model capabilities at 4 percent cost. Developers are now competing on ecosystem completeness as differences among the models continue narrowing. The articles leave open how developers will manage the risk of Nvidia-related chip cutoffs.

Articles.Title: In Depth: DeepSeek’s Computing Crunch Pushes China’s AI Developers Beyond Models - Caixin Global

stories.headline_source: In Depth: DeepSeek’s Computing Crunch Pushes China’s AI Developers Beyond Models

stories.Headline: LinkedIn data shows Singapore firms with stronger AI capabilities record higher headcount growth across all sizes
stories.Summary:
LinkedIn released platform data on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, regarding Singaporean firms. The data shows that businesses with stronger artificial intelligence capabilities record higher headcount growth. This trend occurs across all company sizes within the city-state. The findings cover the period from September 2025 to September 2026. These results suggest AI capabilities associate with business growth for smaller companies.

AI-enabled firms have at least 5 per cent of employees with AI-related talent. Mid-market enterprises, with 201 to 1,000 employees, saw a 1.8 percentage point growth advantage. Small and medium businesses, under 201 employees, had a 1.4 percentage point advantage. Singapore ranked second for mid-market growth at 2.3 per cent, behind Germany at 3.5 per cent. Other markets included the UK, Italy, Netherlands, UAE, Australia, France, US, and Brazil.

Chua Pei Ying is the head economist for LinkedIn in the Asia-Pacific region. She stated that AI frees up resources by automating routine tasks and improving productivity. Chua noted that investing in AI skills helps smaller businesses find new ways to grow. She explained that headcount growth differs from hiring rates by measuring net workforce changes. Chua attributed mid-market success to Singapore being a connected regional business hub.

Traditional sectors like utilities, real estate, and logistics show large headcount growth advantages. Utilities recorded a 10 percentage point advantage, while real estate and equipment rental saw 7.3. Transportation and logistics followed with a 4.7 percentage point advantage for AI-enabled firms. Hiring activity softened for all, with large enterprises over 5,000 employees seeing an 11 per cent drop. Mid-market firms saw a 9.4 per cent decline, and smaller businesses saw 10.5 per cent.

Large enterprises have 25.1 per cent AI engineering skills compared to 12.5 per cent for SMBs. AI literacy is 11.4 per cent in large firms but only 3.3 per cent in SMBs. SMB AI engineering skills grew by 3.5 percentage points and literacy by 1.5 percentage points annually. Mid-market enterprises grew by 7 per cent, while smaller businesses grew by 6.7 per cent. SMB average headcount grew by a more modest 1.1 per cent between 2025 and 2026.

Hiring activity in Singapore typically peaks in May and January each year. December and February are the quietest months for recruitment according to decade-long data. Global economic uncertainty has made businesses more cautious about when they recruit new staff. The data does not establish a causal relationship between AI adoption and workforce expansion. The articles leave open how smaller firms will specifically close the AI skills gap.

Articles.Title: AI adoption raises headcount growth among Singapore firms of all sizes: LinkedIn - The Business Times

stories.headline_source: AI adoption raises headcount growth among Singapore firms of all sizes: LinkedIn

stories.Headline: Hong Kong police deploy AI surveillance network to prevent crime and protect national security
stories.Summary:
The Hong Kong Police Force announced on Wednesday that the city's AI-powered surveillance camera network serves to prevent crime and safeguard national security. This system, known as SmartView, activated its facial recognition technology on Monday to help maintain public order and protect lives. Officers intend to use these advanced tools to locate missing children in large crowds and investigate criminal activities more efficiently. The network was originally launched in 2024 as a regional government initiative to expand surveillance across the city.

The police have already deployed more than 10,000 cameras on government buildings, police vehicles, and both ordinary and smart lampposts. Authorities plan to increase the total number of cameras to 60,000 by 2028 and will connect the network to shopping mall systems this year. To protect privacy, surveillance footage is kept for no more than 31 days, while facial recognition data is stored for a maximum of 180 days. The police force stated that personal data will be held only as long as necessary and for no more than six months.

The police force told the Global Times that facial recognition features are restricted to a small number of trained officers who need supervisory approval. They explained that the AI functions as an investigative tool to help officers analyze footage, but all flagged information requires human review. Every operation is logged and reviewed for compliance to ensure that officers follow existing procedures and privacy laws. The force emphasized that they still rely on other investigative methods before deciding on any further action.

Articles.Title: Hong Kong’s AI-powered surveillance camera network also safeguards national security, personal data protected, police force tells GT - Global Times

stories.headline_source: Hong Kong’s AI-powered surveillance camera network also safeguards national security, personal data protected, police force tells GT

stories.Headline: China approves agreement to establish the World AI Cooperation Organization
stories.Summary:
On November 10, 2026, China's National People's Congress Standing Committee approved the agreement establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization, making China the first of its 38 founding members to do so. The decision was taken at the 25th session of the committee's 14th term. China proposed the organization, which it hosts, and its president unveiled it at a July event held alongside the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference. Thirty-eight countries joined as founding members, and the organization's stated aim is to help countries share in the opportunities AI brings. Preparations are still underway before full operations begin, and more countries are invited to join.

The articles say Beijing has named cooperation and support for developing AI capabilities in the Global South as priorities. According to the reporting, the organization should encourage consultation and shared contributions among members, support AI for the public good, and promote a governance framework that is fair and reasonable. The report on China's approval sits alongside an editorial from China Daily dated November 11, 2026, which argues for Sino-US AI cooperation. That editorial urges both countries to prioritize cooperation while keeping competition within reasonable limits. It also calls for multilateral platforms such as APEC to help bridge gaps on AI governance.

The editorial describes remarks by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at the National Committee on US-China Relations in New York on Tuesday. Bessent called for a constructive relationship based on balance and reciprocity and hoped the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen this month would advance a new bilateral AI dialogue. He said the dialogue aims to guard against shared risks and prevent misunderstandings between the two systems. According to the editorial, Bessent said both sides expect to exchange best practices for testing advanced models before release and have agreed to set up a direct channel for alerting each other to serious incidents.

The China Daily editorial also criticizes Washington's current restrictions on Chinese technology. It says Microsoft and other companies and trade groups have reportedly urged the administration to reconsider a planned ban on imports of a crucial component used in AI data centers, arguing the ban would hurt US competitiveness. It further notes that Washington has been weighing bans on new Chinese optical transceivers over claims of data theft or malware risk that the editorial says have never been substantiated. The editorial concludes that AI risks cross borders and that Washington would benefit from moving beyond zero-sum thinking and heeding the business sector.

Articles.Title: Sino-US AI cooperation necessary for the common good of humanity: China Daily editorial - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: Sino-US AI cooperation necessary for the common good of humanity: China Daily editorial

stories.Headline: Nvidia revenue grows 103 percent as AI infrastructure demand drives third quarter gains
stories.Summary:
The American chipmaker Nvidia reported a massive surge in third-quarter revenue for fiscal 2027 on November 17. The company earned 115.8 billion U.S. dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase from the previous year and a 20 percent rise from the last quarter. This growth was primarily driven by the ongoing global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The firm also recorded a net income of 65.3 billion dollars for the period ending October 25, nearly doubling its profit from the same time last year.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, accounting for about 93 percent of total revenue and increasing 110 percent year on year. Financial metrics included a GAAP gross margin of 74.8 percent and GAAP diluted earnings per share of 2.70 dollars. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to reach approximately 130 billion dollars for fiscal 2027. Additionally, Nvidia returned 28.1 billion dollars to shareholders through cash dividends and repurchased shares during the third quarter. The board previously approved a 150 billion dollar increase to share repurchases, leaving 227.3 billion dollars remaining in that authorization.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress is now responsible for the company after founder Jensen Huang stepped down from his role. Kress stated that the company's momentum is real and praised the relentless innovation of the staff. She noted that the Vera Rubin project has had an explosive start and that the company's roadmap remains on track. Kress further emphasized that the ambition of the technology leader has never been greater than it is now.

Nvidia will pay a quarterly cash dividend of 25 cents per share on December 23 to shareholders of record on December 2. This payment follows the strong financial performance reported in the first quarterly report since the change in leadership. The company continues to focus on expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities to maintain its position as a technology leader. Future growth depends on the successful execution of the current roadmap and the continued demand for high-end chips.

Articles.Title: Nvidia's Q3 revenue surges 103 pct as AI demand drives growth - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Nvidia's Q3 revenue surges 103 pct as AI demand drives growth - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Xinhua Institute report says AI reshapes global information ecosystem and communication power balance
stories.Summary:
A Chinese think tank has reported that artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the global information ecosystem and the balance of power in communication, bringing both new opportunities and new challenges. The report, titled "AI Plus Media: Global Development Report 2026," was compiled by the Xinhua Institute and released during the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing. It was published on November 11, 2026, and the summit itself ran from November 5 to 9 under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." Nearly 500 representatives from almost 330 media outlets, think tanks and government bodies in 112 countries and regions attended, along with the United Nations and other international organizations.

According to the report, advances in generative technology are expanding the supply of content while also making it easier than ever to fabricate it. It describes several paradoxes in AI's effect on the industry. AI platforms are opening new routes to reach audiences, yet they weaken the direct link between news outlets and their readers. AI tools are raising production efficiency, but they also place new demands on the organizational abilities and professional standards of media organizations.

The report adds that the spread of the technology is helping more people while widening the AI divide between regions. The report calls on news media worldwide to act as enablers of technological inclusiveness, pioneers in digital ethics, co-builders of rules for applications, guardians of digital rights and interests, and bridge-builders for exchange and mutual learning. It argues that global news media should work together to build a new information and communication order that is trustworthy, fair and oriented toward the common good. The authors are the Xinhua Institute, which compiled the document.

The article does not give further statements from individual officials about the report. The World Media Summit was first held in 2009 and has since become a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The article presents the report as a contribution to that discussion rather than as a binding measure. It does not say what follow-up steps, if any, the report's recommendations will lead to.

Articles.Title: AI reshaping global media landscape, bringing opportunities and challenges: report - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: AI reshaping global media landscape, bringing opportunities and challenges: report - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Armenia approves seven-year program to develop physical AI and robotics
stories.Summary:
Armenia has officially approved a comprehensive seven-year program to develop physical artificial intelligence, which focuses on robotics and intelligent systems. This strategic initiative was announced on November 17 and aims to train specialists who can compete on an international level. The program targets the creation of AI systems that can interact directly with the physical world through machines. Local media reports indicate that the government intends to build a strong foundation for future technological growth.

The project requires a collaborative effort through public-private partnerships and co-financing involving three major academic institutions. Yerevan State University, the National Polytechnic University of Armenia, and the American University of Armenia will all participate in the implementation. State funding for the initial phase is set at 1.684 billion drams, which is approximately 4.3 million U.S. dollars. These funds will primarily cover the salaries of researchers and the development of necessary infrastructure, while private investors are expected to provide more money.

The government has set specific goals for the seven-year period, including the training of about 330 graduates. They aim to secure around 10 major research grants and register at least one patented invention during this time. The program also plans to organize 12 scientific conferences and establish five new startups or spin-off companies. Additionally, the participating universities intend to publish about 20 papers in academic journals that are ranked internationally.

Those responsible for the program seek to develop specialized research teams at the participating universities to ensure long-term success. They believe that strengthening cooperation with international academic networks will be essential for the growth of physical AI. The initiative focuses on creating a sustainable ecosystem where academic research translates into practical, intelligent machines. By integrating public funding with private investment, Armenia hopes to establish itself as a hub for robotics and intelligent systems.

Articles.Title: Armenia launches 7-year program to develop physical AI - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Armenia launches 7-year program to develop physical AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Australian Capital Equity CEO identifies growth potential in China AI and manufacturing
stories.Summary:
Yizhou He, the managing director and China CEO of Australian Capital Equity, discussed investment opportunities during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026. This event took place on Tuesday and Wednesday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, where he shared his views on the local economy. He explained that the combination of artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing provides the most promising prospects for international investors. His company has already acquired equity stakes in several technology firms based in the city of Shenzhen.

He believes that the next five years must focus on growth quality by translating scientific advances into higher productivity and globally competitive businesses. This strategy requires prioritizing foundational technologies and infrastructure over standalone applications, as breakthroughs often demand years of patient capital. He evaluates frontier technologies based on their reliability, measurable value in real applications, and a credible path toward a scalable business model. He also highlighted the potential of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to merge manufacturing strength with financial expertise and digital asset ecosystems.

Yizhou He stated that China's ability to turn innovation into industrial strength supports his confidence in the long-term economic outlook. He noted that core AI technologies and industrial applications reinforce each other, allowing innovations to reach production lines at a massive scale. Regarding international expansion, he suggested that headquarters should set clear governance expectations while giving local teams the authority to act. He also argued that closer cooperation on the mutual recognition of testing results and clearer regulatory guidance would make cross-border projects much smoother.

Articles.Title: Investor sees long-term growth potential in China‘s AI sector - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: Investor sees long-term growth potential in China‘s AI sector

stories.Headline: APEC member economies coordinate policies to share artificial intelligence benefits across the region
stories.Summary:
Nicolas Miailhe, a board member and AI lead of the France-Pacific Territories Economic Cooperation Committee of the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council, recently discussed regional cooperation. He spoke about these issues ahead of the APEC Shenzhen 2026 meeting to address global prosperity. The discussions focused on the leadership of President Xi Jinping and his call for deeper collaboration. This effort aims to ensure that the benefits of artificial intelligence are shared widely.

The initiative requires economies to work together to distribute the advantages of AI to citizens and consumers. Without this collective effort, individual nations will likely struggle to spread prosperity across their populations. The goal is to forge a shared global prosperity during the current age of artificial intelligence. This process involves coordinating policies across the various member economies of the Asia-Pacific region.

Nicolas Miailhe described the leadership and the call for deeper regional cooperation as very encouraging. He emphasized that cooperation is essential because economies cannot successfully share AI benefits in isolation. The focus remains on creating a system where technological advancements lead to widespread economic growth. He believes that working together is the only way to ensure that AI serves everyone.

Articles.Title: APEC cooperation advances shared prosperity in the AI age - China Daily

stories.headline_source: APEC cooperation advances shared prosperity in the AI age

stories.Headline: UNESCO official urges AI to serve culture while preserving human meaning
stories.Summary:
Shahbaz Khan, the director of the UNESCO Regional Office for East Asia, spoke at a forum in Changsha, Hunan province, on Monday. This event was the 2026 International Youth Forum on Creativity and Heritage along the Silk Roads. He discussed how artificial intelligence can assist people in sharing stories about their heritage through innovative methods. However, he emphasized that only human beings can provide the actual meaning to these cultural narratives.

The use of AI requires a careful balance to ensure it serves culture without causing harm. It offers new possibilities for researching, documenting, transmitting, and raising awareness regarding living heritage. These tools must not extract cultural knowledge without consent or misrepresent the traditions of various groups. Furthermore, the technology should not treat heritage as mere data that is detached from the communities sustaining it.

Shahbaz Khan explained that while AI provides helpful tools, it also poses significant risks to cultural integrity. He argued that the technology must remain a servant to human creativity and community identity. The official stressed that the human element is essential for maintaining the authenticity of historical stories. He cautioned against the dangers of stripping cultural knowledge away from its original social context.

Articles.Title: Changsha forum: UNESCO official says AI should serve culture - China Daily

stories.headline_source: Changsha forum: UNESCO official says AI should serve culture

stories.Headline: Global leaders and educators call for collaboration to use AI to close learning and economic divides
stories.Summary:
John Lee Chi-kin chaired a high-level session on AI ethics and social responsibility in Hong Kong on October 27 and 28, 2026. This event occurred during the Global University Presidents and Leaders Summit 2026 to discuss high-tech innovation and the future of education. China also hosted APEC 2026, which focused on the three pillars of openness, innovation, and cooperation for the Asia-Pacific community. Participants at the 2026 Global South Modernization Forum in Cairo, Egypt, also called for the effective use of artificial intelligence. These leaders aim to use technology to close divides in learning, information, and economic opportunities across different global societies.

The mission requires collaboration between governments, academia, the technology sector, and the business community to dismantle barriers to accessibility. Hong Kong serves as a bridge to ASEAN and Belt and Road Initiative countries, supported by the Chinese mainland. The Education University of Hong Kong, or EdUHK, is ranked within the top seven globally in education by QS. Since 2017, EdUHK has served as a core consultant for World Bank education initiatives in Vietnam to foster digital transformation. The university also promotes policy dialogue and talent development in the United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan, and various ASEAN countries.

John Lee Chi-kin and other leaders believe that education is central to harnessing AI for productivity and human development. Shannon Kane, an assistant clinical professor at the University of Maryland, says candidates must be prepared to judge AI outputs. Jennifer Kidd from Old Dominion University believes teachers must understand how AI works and its different impacts on learning. Justin Reich of MIT's Teaching Systems Lab argues that domain knowledge is necessary to tell if AI output is useless. Tracy Rock from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte says faculty should be critical rather than just AI cheerleaders.

Novice educators are affected by these changes, as over half of teachers now use AI for parts of their jobs. A 2023 ISTE report found that 56 percent of new teachers lack confidence in using technology in the classroom. K-12 school districts are affected by inconsistent policies, with some districts banning AI while others embrace the new technology. Students at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, are now studying the benefits and drawbacks of AI in instruction. Many teacher candidates are also affected, though nearly a quarter of them do not want AI preparation in programs.

Teacher preparation has long struggled to effectively prepare aspiring teachers to integrate technology into their classroom instruction. An EdWeek Research Center survey of 268 teacher educators in August and September 2026 revealed various hurdles in AI integration. About 60 percent of faculty members decide individually whether to include an AI focus in their specific university courses. Many programs struggle to offer AI instruction because other priorities and national accreditation standards take precedence over new technology. Faculty professional development is limited, with only 14 percent of respondents reporting that they receive ongoing professional development.

Next, programs must navigate the rapid development of AI, which 57 percent of respondents cited as a major hurdle. Faculty at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte are using communities of practice to learn about tools like Gemini. Some instructors, like Jennifer Kidd, must revamp their course materials every single semester because the technology changes so quickly. The articles leave open whether K-12 school district leaders will actually prize AI skills when hiring new teacher candidates. It remains unclear if high-quality research will soon prove whether AI tools can actually improve student learning outcomes.

Articles.Title: Bridging the divide: how education and AI can build a shared future - China Daily

stories.headline_source: Bridging the divide: how education and AI can build a shared future

stories.Headline: iQIYI returns to non-GAAP operating profit by using AI to increase efficiency
stories.Summary:
The online entertainment provider iQIYI reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 on November 17, 2026. The company achieved a return to non-GAAP operating profit by utilizing artificial intelligence to increase efficiency and implementing strict cost cuts. These strategic measures helped the firm offset the impact of a lighter content slate during the period. The company successfully narrowed its operating loss to 41.9 million yuan from 121.8 million yuan the previous year.

Revenues for the quarter fell ten percent year over year to 6.01 billion yuan, or 896.0 million dollars. Membership services revenue dropped six percent to 3.97 billion yuan, while content distribution and other revenues fell by 38 percent and 39 percent respectively. Online advertising grew three percent, and content costs decreased 13 percent to 3.52 billion yuan. The firm held 4.04 billion yuan in cash and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026, and spent 76.4 million dollars to repurchase 64.2 million ADSs.

Chief Executive Officer Gong Yu stated that the company maintained the top domestic market share for films, children's content, and long-form dramas. He noted that short-form dramas reached the top quarterly share for the first time under a new social media model. Chief Financial Officer Tian Ying explained that the company intends to improve investment efficiency through a larger portfolio of revenue-sharing content. Both executives highlighted that the integration of decentralization and artificial intelligence is producing encouraging early results for the business.

Articles.Title: iQIYI's AI-driven efficiency push pays off in Q3 - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: iQIYI's AI-driven efficiency push pays off in Q3

stories.Headline: Tencent and the China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association host AI collaboration event in London
stories.Summary:
More than one hundred artificial intelligence researchers and professionals gathered in London on Friday, November 13, 2026, to discuss the connection between academic study and industrial innovation. The China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association and the Chinese technology giant Tencent hosted the event to foster deeper collaboration between the two nations. Speakers at the conference included representatives from the University College London, Oxford University, and various business units within Tencent. These experts focused on the intersection of cutting-edge research and the practical application of technology in the real world.

The event required a collaborative effort to highlight how the United Kingdom and China possess highly complementary strengths in the field of intelligence. Ding Mingqin, who serves as the minister counselor and head of the science and technology section at China's Embassy in the UK, emphasized the need for international cooperation on global governance. He noted that while the UK maintains a competitive edge in frontier research, China excels in engineering, advanced manufacturing, and large-scale industrial deployment. This synergy creates a solid foundation for future collaboration because China is currently one of the largest markets for AI applications.

Ding Mingqin stated that China remains consistently committed to strengthening international partnerships to ensure the responsible development of these powerful technologies. Richard Parnes, a senior director at Tencent Games, argued that artificial intelligence cannot replace human taste or the judgment that gives meaning to creative work. He compared the rise of AI to the introduction of spreadsheets, suggesting that technology makes talented creative teams unbeatable rather than replacing them entirely. Simon Stringer from the Oxford Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience and Artificial Intelligence and Professor Peter Latham from the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit also shared their specialized research.

The participants engaged in a panel discussion where they shared diverse opinions on cross-border collaboration and the implementation of real-world innovation. They explored the complex connections between the human brain and large language models to better understand how artificial intelligence can evolve. By bridging the gap between academia and industry, the attendees hoped to accelerate the pace of technological breakthroughs through shared knowledge. The conference concluded with a collective agreement that human oversight remains essential for the meaningful application of these advanced digital tools.

Articles.Title: AI conference bridges academia and industry - China Daily

stories.headline_source: AI conference bridges academia and industry

stories.Headline: China's LineShine supercomputer remains the fastest system in the world
stories.Summary:
China's LineShine supercomputer maintained its position as the fastest system in the world during rankings released in Chicago on Monday. The machine, which is located at the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, first claimed this top spot in June. It outperformed the American El Capitan system in both the TOP500 rankings and the High Performance Conjugate Gradients Benchmark. This achievement demonstrates the resilience of Chinese technological innovation despite various restrictions imposed by developed economies.

The system reached a sustained performance of 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack benchmark, placing it roughly 21 percent ahead of El Capitan. LineShine also led the HPCG Benchmark tests with 22 petaflops, while the American system reached 17.41 petaflops. It is the first supercomputer in TOP500 history to exceed 2 exaflops of sustained double-precision performance using only domestic central processing units. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced chips sent to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun stated that the United States is overstretching the concept of national security to target the high-tech industry of China. He argued that Washington views artificial intelligence competition as a zero-sum game and abuses export controls to interfere with normal trade. The Chinese government believes these discriminatory rules disrupt global supply chains and primarily serve to maintain American technological dominance. They maintain that China promotes inclusivity and open source models while the US coerces other nations into closed ecosystems.

The two nations previously agreed in September to create a communication channel for exchanging best practices and addressing unexpected AI incidents. Current APEC meetings in Shenzhen provide an opportunity to put this consensus into practice through active cooperation. Both countries share a responsibility to ensure that artificial intelligence remains under human control and advances general human progress. China warns that a fragmented AI landscape could leave developing economies lagging behind during the next technological revolution.

Articles.Title: Make AI a field for cooperation, not rivalry: China Daily editorial - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: Make AI a field for cooperation, not rivalry: China Daily editorial

stories.Headline: New AI platforms help global students and teachers practice and assess Chinese language skills
stories.Summary:
New AI-powered Chinese learning platforms were recently unveiled at the World Chinese Language Conference held in Beijing to support teachers and learners. These digital tools aim to standardize assessments and encourage more global students to practice speaking the language in their classrooms. The Yufei Smart Chinese Classroom connects lesson preparation and oral practice, and it has already been implemented in over 900 schools worldwide. These systems move the concept of artificial intelligence into actual classroom practice to help students find their voice.

The Yufei system was used in a Thai public school with 1,800 students, where 29 teachers manage 70 different classes. Over 330 days, students there generated 23,093 speaking practices and more than 65,000 pronunciation diagnostic records on the platform. In Myanmar, a school with 10,000 students used an AI oral evaluation system for levels 1 to 8 since May 2025. This specific school has held 2,127 oral exams and conducted more than 1.2 million evaluations to ensure scoring consistency. Additionally, the SureChinese 2.0 app from BlingABC now serves over 200,000 registered users and 40,000 monthly active users.

The SureChinese 2.0 platform offers 1,000 guide videos and 7,000 exercises across four HSK 3.0 levels while supporting 12 system languages. CEO Qiao Lei explained that the app evaluates accuracy and fluency while providing pronunciation guidance and automated learning reports. Xie Fei of iFLYTEK stated that the primary goal is to provide tools that do not increase the burdens placed on teachers. Principal Zhang Qiuyuan noted that AI handles repetitive scoring and initial screening, but human review remains necessary for abnormal results. Wang Zhanglong described a dual-teacher model where a virtual teacher leads while local teachers provide essential assistance.

The Yufei International Chinese Education Vertical Large Model was jointly released by iFLYTEK and the Center for Language Education and Cooperation. This model incorporates authoritative teaching materials to help teachers design exercises and explain complex language points more effectively. The technology is designed to provide a reliable content source rather than replacing the professional judgment of human educators. By using color marking to identify specific words, these tools offer targeted exercises for learners from various language backgrounds. These advancements continue to expand the reach of Chinese language education through integrated digital assessment and interactive learning.

Articles.Title: AI tools help global learners find their voice in Chinese - China Daily

stories.headline_source: AI tools help global learners find their voice in Chinese

stories.Headline: Amateur creators use AI to produce a viral historical short drama with 12 billion views in China
stories.Summary:
A group of six amateurs created a viral AI-generated short drama called Armed Into the Song Dynasty, which first premiered in August. The production team includes a former rideshare driver, a stay-at-home mother, an interior designer, a wholesale business owner, and a former pharmaceutical sales representative. This historical series has already reached ten seasons and consists of approximately 1,000 episodes that each last about three minutes. The show has gathered more than 12 billion views on Bilibili and Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

The series is adapted from a web novel by Chagen’er that began publishing in April and follows five modern soldiers traveling back to the Northern Song dynasty. This production reflects a broader industry shift, as 490,000 micro-dramas were released in the first nine months of 2026, which is 13 times the total for 2025. An October report from the National Radio and Television Administration stated that AI-generated content now makes up over 90 percent of these dramas. The same report noted that the monthly active audience for short dramas has now exceeded 600 million viewers.

Zhang Hansheng, the 54-year-old head of the production team, told domestic media that the series cost roughly 1 million yuan, or 150,000 dollars, to produce. While Zhang declined to share the specific earnings of the team, rumors of high returns have encouraged other grassroots creators to learn AI tools. Some viewers expressed interest in making their own dramas, though others warned about scams involving AI-related courses. This success follows other historical AI dramas like Inkstone Edge Green Plum and Assuming a Noble Identity, which premiered last year.

The rise of these high-quality productions challenges the reputation of short dramas as mindless entertainment featuring formulaic characters and implausible plots. However, critics have requested more scrutiny regarding how artificial intelligence depicts the history of China. Last year, the National Radio and Television Administration began a campaign against AI videos that distort heroic, revolutionary, or historical themes. They specifically targeted content that alters classic television, film, or literary works to ensure historical accuracy is maintained.

Articles.Title: China’s Short Dramas See Quality Shift With AI-Made Historical Hit - Sixth Tone

stories.headline_source: China’s Short Dramas See Quality Shift With AI-Made Historical Hit

stories.Headline: COP31 climate case studies feature AI-powered waste-to-energy project in Wuhan
stories.Summary:
A waste-to-energy project located in Wuhan, Hubei province, was featured in a collection of climate action case studies on November 9. This announcement occurred during the COP31 UN climate talks which were held in Antalya, Turkiye. The project was included in a bilingual publication that highlights various efforts to combat climate change. This specific collection was released to the public during a news conference on the opening day of the summit. The publication presents thirty different examples of climate action taken by Chinese companies and various industrial parks.

It was compiled by the publicity and education center of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment along with several partner organizations. The materials are designed to share practical and replicable approaches to achieving low-carbon development across different regions. These case studies aim to promote international exchanges regarding the most effective methods for climate action. Event organizers stated that the primary goal of the publication is to provide a roadmap for sustainable growth.

They believe that sharing these specific industrial examples will help other nations implement similar green technologies. The organizers emphasized the importance of cooperation and the exchange of knowledge to meet global environmental targets. By showcasing the Wuhan project, they hope to demonstrate the viability of AI-powered energy solutions. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Wuhan's AI-powered waste-to-energy project featured at COP31 - China Daily

stories.headline_source: Wuhan's AI-powered waste-to-energy project featured at COP31

stories.Headline: Unitree CEO warns that AI robotics breakthroughs will strain mass production capabilities
stories.Summary:
Unitree Robotics CEO Wang Xingxing discussed the potential for a technical breakthrough in general-purpose robot models on Tuesday morning. He shared these insights during his appearance at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 held in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. The leader noted that the increasing utility of large language models has created high expectations for robots to solve practical problems. He believes that while the technology is advancing, the ability to scale up production will present significant challenges.

The primary technical obstacle involves creating models that allow robots to function in homes without needing repeated retraining for every unique setting. This advancement would require robots to begin working immediately upon deployment rather than undergoing extensive site-specific adjustments. Such a shift would change how the industry approaches the deployment of general-purpose machines in domestic environments. The goal is to move beyond current limitations to achieve a more seamless integration of AI into physical robotics.

Wang Xingxing is responsible for leading the company and provided these perspectives on the current state of the industry. He explained that the success of AI in other fields has pushed the robotics sector toward similar breakthroughs. The CEO emphasized that the gap between technical possibility and mass production remains a critical point of concern. He suggested that the industry must overcome these specific hurdles before robots can be widely adopted for everyday household tasks.

Articles.Title: Nearing AI Robotics Breakthrough Would Strain Production, Unitree Founder Says - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: China Securities Regulatory Commission denies requiring mutual funds to report AI exposure
stories.Summary:
The China Securities Regulatory Commission issued a formal denial on Wednesday regarding reports about new reporting rules. Online claims suggested that the agency had forced mutual fund companies to disclose their artificial intelligence exposure across all products. The regulator clarified that these specific rumors circulating on the internet were entirely untrue and lacked any factual basis. This official statement was published on the agency's official WeChat account to correct the misinformation.

The regulator emphasized that it has not required fund managers to submit any data regarding their AI investments. According to the agency, mutual fund managers are responsible for independently determining their own investment targets and portfolio weightings. These decisions must be made in accordance with their specific fund contracts and internal investment decision-making procedures. No new mandates have been implemented that would change how these companies report their holdings to the government.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission stated that the claims regarding mandatory AI exposure reporting were false. Separately, the China Association for Public Companies used its rumor-debunking platform to address another set of false claims. This platform noted that reports of a State Council executive meeting suggesting a lack of stock market support were fabricated. The association warned that such distorted information disrupts capital market expectations and has an extremely detrimental impact on investors.

The association urged internet users and investors to rationally assess information they find online and refrain from spreading rumors. They claimed that the false reports involved fabricated meeting content and a serious distortion of current government policies. The regulator continues to maintain that fund managers retain their autonomy over the assets they choose to hold. No further actions or policy changes were mentioned regarding the oversight of artificial intelligence investments in mutual funds.

Articles.Title: CSRC denies requiring funds to report AI exposure - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: CSRC denies requiring funds to report AI exposure

stories.Headline: European Central Bank warns that AI valuations and sovereign debt threaten euro area financial stability
stories.Summary:
The European Central Bank published a Financial Stability Review on Wednesday, November 18, which highlighted several looming threats to the financial stability of the euro area. This comprehensive report warns that artificial intelligence valuations, sovereign debt levels, and geopolitical tensions are creating significant vulnerabilities across the region. The bank specifically noted that the non-bank financial sector is particularly exposed to these emerging risks in certain segments. These combined pressures could potentially test the overall resilience of an economy that grew by 0.4 percent during the third quarter of this year. The report explains that investors face direct exposure to AI valuation risks through euro-denominated debt issuances intended to fund expensive AI infrastructure.

High earnings expectations and extreme market concentration in United States technology firms increase the likelihood of an abrupt market repricing. Simultaneously, sovereign yields for longer-term maturities have climbed to their highest levels in twenty years and are expected to rise further. This environment of rising interest rates and inflation means that both banks and non-banks holding sovereign debt may suffer significant valuation losses. The European Central Bank stated that rising exposures to sovereign debt and artificial intelligence warrant close attention from financial regulators.

Officials warned that a sudden shift in the narrative surrounding AI could trigger market instability within a highly uncertain geopolitical environment. They also noted that the ongoing war in the Middle East could deteriorate macro-financial conditions and increase credit risks for various financial institutions. These authorities believe that the combination of prolonged headwinds and high valuations creates a precarious situation for the euro area. More to follow.

Articles.Title: ECB warns of looming risks from AI valuations, sovereigns, geopolitics - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: ECB warns of looming risks from AI valuations, sovereigns, geopolitics - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Chinese cement producers adopt AI and digital sensors to create smart green factories
stories.Summary:
Chinese cement producers are integrating artificial intelligence and digital sensors to transform energy intensive plants into smart, green factories as of November 18, 2026. Major companies like Anhui Conch Group Co., Ltd. in Wuhu, Anhui Province, are deploying driverless trucks and remotely operated excavators to automate the challenging raw material extraction process. These upgrades include the use of radar sensors that allow unmanned vehicles to navigate quarry roads safely even during periods of low visibility. The shift is part of a broader national effort to embed low carbon technologies and intelligent systems into traditional manufacturing sectors.

The transition requires the implementation of complex AI models, such as the one developed by Anhui Conch Group Co., Ltd. and Huawei, which utilizes computer vision and predictive analytics. This specific model identifies over 200 AI scenarios across 15 categories and has already deployed more than 40 applications for quality control and production optimization. One key tool is a clinker strength prediction model that allows operators to adjust kiln parameters in real time before laboratory results are finished. Additionally, a carbon capture project in Wuhu processes 50,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually to create industrial products and boost greenhouse tomato yields.

Company officials and industry experts are leading these changes, with Xu Yue of Conch Cement noting that AI allows for immediate adjustments to production parameters. Huang Yong of the same group explained that unmanned trucks now coordinate with excavators to improve the efficiency of hauling raw materials. Kong Xiangzhong, the former executive president of the China Cement Association, stated that nearly 70 companies have become smart manufacturing demonstration factories since 2021. Peng Shou from the Chinese Academy of Engineering added that market forces and policy are pushing the sector toward circular resource use and lower emissions.

This industry shift aligns with a wider government drive where the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology reports that over 30 percent of large manufacturing firms adopted AI by the first half of the year. Other leaders in the field include CR Cement, whose Tianyang plant in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region became the first lighthouse factory in the sector. Meanwhile, BBMG Jidong Cement Group Co., Ltd. has established a zero employee production line at its Tongchuan plant with a daily capacity of 10,000 tonnes. These developments signal a strategic transition toward higher end products and a significant reduction in standard coal consumption.

stories.Headline: Nadia Shaw urges businesses to keep offline backups and manual procedures for AI outages
stories.Summary:
Nadia Shaw wrote an opinion piece on November 19, 2026, regarding the risks of relying solely on artificial intelligence. She argues that while these smart systems offer efficiency, they also create new vulnerabilities for both individuals and businesses. The author suggests that maintaining physical backups, such as paper notebooks, is a prudent strategy for the modern age. This approach ensures that essential tasks can continue even when digital services or networks fail completely.

The author explains that cybersecurity experts now warn that AI helps attackers find and exploit weaknesses at a greater scale. For businesses, this requires implementing security layers that restrict data access and limit what automated agents can do. Companies should require human approval for consequential transactions and ensure a specific person can revoke access immediately. Additionally, households are encouraged to keep small amounts of cash and physical copies of essential documents.

Nadia Shaw highlights the concept of cognitive debt, a term used by computer scientist Margaret-Anne Storey to describe a loss of shared understanding. This happens when teams move so quickly with AI that they can no longer explain how their systems work. Shaw suggests that the pressure to review AI work at high speeds leads to stress and fatigue for employees. She believes that people must continue practicing the skills needed to challenge and verify automated tools.

The article concludes that while digital payments and AI are useful, they cannot replace resilience during a total system failure. Businesses are advised to maintain tested offline backups and manual procedures that do not require an email login. The author emphasizes that a recovery plan is useless if it is trapped behind a failed digital account. Ultimately, the goal is to ensure that basic operations remain possible if the computer screens go dark.

Articles.Title: When AI fails, a notebook still works - macau daily times 澳門每日時報

stories.headline_source: When AI fails, a notebook still works

stories.Headline: Ransomware groups use AI to raise global attacks as ransom payments fall
stories.Summary:
Ransomware groups used AI tools to increase global attacks during 2026, according to reports released in November of that same year. These cybercriminals used large language models to create convincing phishing emails and identify sensitive data more quickly than before. The number of groups claiming success grew from 75 in the first quarter to 111 in the third quarter. These attackers targeted various industries and regions, though the number of attacks on US companies remained fairly steady. The Gentlemen became the most active group, surpassing Qilin in the number of victims they targeted.

Halcyon reported 2,766 claimed breaches in the third quarter of 2026, which was nearly 40% higher than the previous quarter. This figure represents a 31% increase from the first quarter and a 39% increase from the second quarter of 2026. Sophos found that 62% of retail attacks succeeded in encrypting data, compared to 48% in 2025, but only 32% paid. The median ransom demand dropped to $700,000 in 2026, which is a significant decrease from $2 million in 2024. About one third of claimed successes came from groups that did not exist six months prior to the quarter end.

Cynthia Kaiser of Halcyon said AI removed language barriers for phishing, which led to more convincing messages in languages like Japanese. She noted that Japan is treating these AI driven attacks almost as a state of emergency for the country. Chester Wisniewski of Sophos stated that the efficacy of ransomware in generating money for criminals has been declining recently. He observed that local government and school districts are largely not paying ransoms regardless of whether data theft occurred. Duy-Phuc Pham of Trellix explained that AI allows small crews to do the work of large ones faster.

Retail firms were affected, but 71% recovered their data from backups, with most recovering within one week of the attack. Manufacturing remains the top target because shared platforms among partners can expose engineering data beyond the first targeted company. Victims in Europe saw an increase in attacks, while the share of US victims remained the same or decreased. Law enforcement spent the year targeting shared services that these groups depend on, including criminal VPNs and laundering services. These groups continue to broaden their campaigns against more industries and regions due to the scale AI enables.

The articles state that AI allows attackers to scan, exploit, and move through networks with very little human effort required. This technology removes historical barriers to targeting smaller populations by creating social engineering messaging in a variety of different languages. The growth in the number of groups continues to pose a threat even as the ransom payments fall. The manufacturing sector is targeted because a single compromise can expose data across a network of suppliers and partners. These trends show that ransomware is not going away despite the decline in actual money generated for crooks.

The manufacturing sector will likely remain the top targeted group in 2027 as international organizations account for a greater share. Cynthia Kaiser expects continued growth in attacks, especially in regions outside the United States, during the coming year. It remains an open question whether more attacks will actually result in more money for the ransomware groups. The articles suggest that countries newly feeling the pain may improve international cooperation to fight these AI driven threats. The reports leave open whether law enforcement can successfully dismantle the shared services these criminal groups rely upon.

Articles.Title: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, But Payments Decline - Dark Reading

stories.headline_source: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, But Payments Decline

stories.Headline: Varonis reveals TheMailer phishing kit that uses AI to personalize lures and evade filters
stories.Summary:
Varonis researchers revealed a new phishing kit called TheMailer on November 17, 2026. This commercial tool uses attacker supplied AI models to personalize lures and evade filters. The kit allows cybercriminals to scale their campaigns to tens of thousands of targets. It orchestrates most elements of an attack through integrated large language model functionality. The system can rewrite email lures until they successfully bypass various spam filters.

A lifetime license for the kit costs between 3,000 and 6,000 dollars in cryptocurrency. Operators must provide their own SMTP servers, proxies, target email lists, and API keys. The software supports AI models including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Grok, Gemini, and Mistral. One campaign showed nearly 25,000 emails sent to a list of 145,000 targets. The tool personalizes the email address, body, subject line, and attachments for every recipient.

Varonis senior security researcher Daniel Kelley wrote about the kit in a blog post. He stated that the tool is built to scale against many different targets. Kelley noted that the personalization is opportunistic rather than being a true spear phishing tool. He explained that the kit removes AI writing patterns to make emails look realistic. He believes more kits will follow because buyers will start asking for these features.

The kit affects organizations that rely on content filters to block malicious email lures. Varonis suggests that defenders enforce email authentication practices like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. They recommend monitoring for new domains and checking links through full redirect chains. Training should teach users to be wary of urgency and unexpected login prompts. Least privilege access and data monitoring can limit damage if a user clicks.

Phishing kits and phishing as a service platforms have gained popularity in recent years. Most AI functionality previously focused on reconnaissance, coding websites, and automating simple repetitive tasks. TheMailer distinguishes itself by automating the phishing process from end to end using AI. It can generate lures from a short prompt or a real brand email. This represents a degree of AI leverage hardly seen in the cybercriminal ecosystem.

Varonis assesses that TheMailer currently has a large customer base among cybercriminals. It remains unclear how successful the kit is because AI task success rates vary. The articles leave open whether other sellers have already integrated similar AI capabilities. Defenders must now adapt training because bad grammar is no longer a reliable warning sign. Future kits are expected to follow the model established by this specific tool.

Articles.Title: 'TheMailer' Phishing Kit Puts AI in the Driver's Seat - Dark Reading

stories.headline_source: 'TheMailer' Phishing Kit Puts AI in the Driver's Seat

stories.Headline: Chinese AI stocks fall as US administration plans to block data center equipment imports
stories.Summary:
Investors sold off Chinese artificial intelligence hardware exporters and hyperscalers on November 18, 2026, as signs of tougher United States technology curbs emerged. This market decline occurred ahead of a scheduled meeting between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and United States President Donald Trump. The downturn followed the removal of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer of Nvidia after Republicans lost the United States midterm election. These events pushed China's stock benchmark toward its lowest levels since mid-2025.

The Trump administration intends to block imports of Chinese data center equipment despite opposition from American technology firms. The Federal Communications Commission previously sought to ban new models of Chinese optical transceivers due to national security concerns. Nvidia now assumes it will have no data center chip sales to China, while Senator Tammy Baldwin introduced legislation to revoke the normal trade status of China. Consequently, the CSI300 and Shanghai Composite Index both fell roughly 0.4 per cent, and the Hang Seng Tech index dropped 1.5 per cent.

Louis-Vincent Gave of Gavekal Research stated that the downfall of Jensen Huang could have consequences extending far beyond the artificial intelligence sector. He noted that tighter financing might threaten the investment boom while political tensions reshape the relations between the two nations. Other affected companies included Alibaba, Tencent, and MiniMax, as well as optical parts makers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink. The latter two firms have seen their values drop more than 70 per cent from their peak levels.

President Trump met with leaders from Australia, Japan, and India in the Philippines on Tuesday before a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen. The Quad expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, although the group did not explicitly name China in its statement. While most tech stocks fell, the Star Chip Index rose 0.5 per cent on expectations that domestic chipmakers would benefit from restrictions. Gold stocks also tumbled nearly 5 per cent because of expectations that the United States would raise interest rates.

Articles.Title: China AI stocks, hyperscalers hit by signs of tougher US tech curbs - The Business Times

stories.headline_source: China AI stocks, hyperscalers hit by signs of tougher US tech curbs

stories.Headline: Asean members sign grid pact to share clean power and back regional AI growth
stories.Summary:
All eleven Asean member states signed an enhanced memorandum of understanding in Manila earlier this week. This pact entered into force on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The agreement establishes an integrated regional electricity network called the Asean Power Grid. This network aims to share clean power across borders in South-east Asia. The deal coincides with the COP31 conference taking place in Turkey.

The pact anchors cross-border interconnections, multilateral power trade, and financing for subsea cables and overland lines. Asean estimates it needs 764 billion US dollars for generation and transmission investment through 2045. The APG Financing Initiative involves the Asean bloc, the World Bank Group, and the Asian Development Bank. The Philippines, which just ended its 2026 Asean chairmanship, faces bottlenecks in its Mindanao, Visayas, and Luzon grids. These regional links provide a buffer when domestic generation is tight.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the memorandum brings commitment to resilience, innovation, and partnership into practical focus. She stressed the importance of attracting multilateral and private capital for these projects. Robert Cooke of the Global Renewables Alliance said policymakers can use data centres as a force for renewables. He stated that hyperscalers have a commercial stake in funding grid upgrades to secure green electricity. These upgrades also shield server farms from extreme weather.

Rexor Amancio of the Global Renewables Alliance warned that data centres might displace green power from other users. He said this could drive up fossil gas and increase power prices for everyone. Over nine in ten Philippine business leaders say their country relies too much on fossil-fuel imports. This is the highest share among 18 economies surveyed by E3G, the Global Renewables Alliance, and the We Mean Business Coalition. Data centre operators are the primary group affected by these constraints.

South-east Asia wants to be an artificial intelligence hub, but grids rely on imported gas and coal. Global data centre electricity consumption rose 17 per cent in 2025, while AI-focused demand surged 50 per cent. Data centres accounted for roughly 40 per cent of global corporate renewable power-purchase agreements last year. The Philippines has a liberalised wholesale market, retail competition, and a green energy option programme. However, developers still face wheeling charges, permitting delays, and congested transmission lines.

The region must now turn digital infrastructure growth into investments for transmission, storage, and renewable generation. Regulators are under pressure to close accounting loopholes regarding 100 per cent renewable status claims. The International Renewable Energy Agency has a COP31 green data centre programme to prove electricity is locally sourced. Some builders are already installing onsite gas turbines to avoid multi-year connection queues. The articles leave open whether the sector will accelerate the green transition or lock in fossil-fuel demand.

Articles.Title: Asean Power Grid deal raises stakes for regional AI boom - The Business Times

stories.Headline: Xi Jinping urges South Korea to cooperate on AI and supply chains
stories.Summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in Shenzhen. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to discuss bilateral relations. During the thirty-four minute conversation, the Chinese leader called for a joint effort to protect global supply chains. He also urged the two nations to deepen their economic policy coordination and foster cooperation regarding artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

The leaders discussed the substantial conclusion of the second phase of free-trade talks between their two countries. China and South Korea have been working to upgrade their existing trade agreement since 2018. President Xi stated that this progress would help consolidate the sound momentum of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation. These changes aim to strengthen the economic ties and technological partnerships between the two East Asian powers.

President Xi Jinping took responsibility for leading the call for increased cooperation in high-tech industries. He praised the recent outcomes of the trade negotiations as a positive step for both nations. By emphasizing the importance of supply chain security, he signaled a desire for more stable economic interactions. The leaders focused on creating a framework where emerging technologies could be developed through shared efforts.

Articles.Title: Xi Jinping urges South Korea to cooperate with China on AI and supply chains - South China Morning Post

stories.Headline: Kyndryl finds 64% of leaders report positive AI returns as readiness for external risks falls to 24%
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl released findings from its third annual Readiness Report on November 10, 2026, in New York, showing a widening divide between AI returns and readiness to manage risks. The report found that 64% of leaders report positive returns on AI investments, up 10 points from 2025. Average readiness across external risks fell seven points to 24%, with the steepest declines in readiness for cyber threats and competitive disruption. The report captures the attitudes and actions of 3,700 senior business leaders across 21 countries. The data shows organizations racing to deliver returns on significant AI investments while feeling ill-equipped to navigate the implications for the AI era.

Significantly fewer leaders describe themselves as in the experimentation phase compared to a year ago, down 13 points from 2025 to 49%. Nearly half, 48%, substantially changed their AI strategies this year, with implications across tech, people and governance. About a quarter, 24%, saw an AI investment fail, and 21% canceled a major AI initiative. Just 27% have formally updated roles and responsibilities around AI, and 29% have fully implemented change management for AI adoption. Those who have done both are 28 points more likely to be completely ready for their AI implementation and 8 points more likely to report positive ROI on their AI investments.

Martin Schroeter, Chairman and CEO of Kyndryl, said that as AI creates significant opportunity, organizations are now focusing on how to make early returns sustainable. He said this year's Readiness Report shows a new kind of readiness gap, with AI ambitions moving faster than the systems needed to support them. He said the bar for readiness keeps moving as AI becomes more integrated in enterprises. He said Kyndryl's data shows that focusing on people, technology and governance can help organizations win with AI and keep the ability to adapt as opportunities evolve. Kyndryl is described as a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services and trades on the NYSE under KD.

For the third year in a row, security concerns topped the list of external risks and contributed most to the overall decline in readiness. Just 26% of firms said they were completely ready for cyberattacks, a drop of 11 points from last year. Three in four leaders say AI helps their organizations identify threats faster, even as confidence in their ability to respond to cyberattacks has declined. The second-largest drop in readiness came from leaders' concerns about competitive disruptions outside of their industry, down 10 points from 2025 to 23%. Retailers are weighing how to benefit from AI shopping assistants without forfeiting direct customer relationships, software companies face questions about SaaS models as AI rebalances the build-versus-buy equation, and financial institutions are challenged by emerging lending models.

The research captures how leaders are considering digital sovereignty in a year marked by greater actions by governments, most visibly in the European Union. Leaders in the EU are slightly less likely to have taken sovereignty-related actions compared to those in the rest of the world. 68% say solutions offering full operational control, should they need it, are worth a premium of 10% or more, and 60% say greater control is worth slower deployment and adoption of advanced capabilities. For the third year in a row, leaders said upgrading their IT infrastructure was the number one action their organizations are taking to mitigate external risks, and 71% rate their infrastructure as mostly or fully modernized. Yet two-thirds of CIOs surveyed think their technology foundations need significant re-architecture before being fully ready for AI at scale.

The report is Kyndryl's third annual Readiness Report, and the 2026-27 Readiness Report is promoted on Kyndryl's site as exploring how organizations are navigating AI adoption, IT modernization and evolving business demands. Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report is described as revealing a decline in workforce readiness as AI adoption surges, and what leading organizations are doing to prepare. The articles state that 66% of CIOs believe their infrastructure requires significant re-architecture before it can support AI at scale. The articles do not state what Kyndryl plans to do next with the findings, and they leave open which specific countries or industries drove the declines. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Kyndryl report: Executives see value in AI investments as readiness drops - Kyndryl
