stories.Headline: Tencent IEG and other firms increase demand for AI proficiency in 2026 hiring processes
stories.Summary:
Game developers and job seekers are integrating AI into their work and hiring processes during 2026. Tencent IEG increased demand for AI positions in its 2026 intern recruitment documents. Some of these roles now include AI interviews or AI coding assessments. This trend reflects a global shift toward requiring AI proficiency for employment. Many practitioners now view AI as a general skill for the modern workplace.

Tencent IEG and other firms are changing how they evaluate new talent in 2026. GDC reported in November 2026 that 40 percent of game practitioners use generative AI. Among those users, 57 percent utilize the technology every single day. Educators show a gap, as 62 percent encourage AI use but only 20 percent of students do. A 2025 report from the Game Working Committee of China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association surveyed 22 enterprises.

An HR manager from a listed company told Chuapp that AI is often just a tool. He stated that professional basic skills remain the most important factor for any candidate. This manager noted that AI tools only account for 5 to 10 percent of initial interviews. He believes that applicants must still demonstrate a deep understanding of the specific project. The manager emphasized that AI cannot replace the need for human thinking and reasoning.

Job seekers like Lin feel that AI skills are now as essential as English. Some artists argue that AI creates a forced inevitability that increases worker anxiety. These practitioners worry that companies will simply add AI workloads to already full schedules. Junior user researchers are particularly affected because AI can now perform some of their basic tasks. Many feel that those who cannot use AI will suffer professional losses.

The 2025 survey showed AI application rates of 86.36 percent in R&D and 77.3 percent in operations. Most current industry use remains shallow and tool based rather than deep. One medium company tried connecting planners, programmers, and artists via AI from 2025 to 2026. However, this integrated workflow has not been fully put into operation yet. Companies now provide regular employees with quota authorizations for mainstream AI models.

A 51job report from August 2026 provides insights for the 2027 campus recruitment market. It shows 39.3 percent of AI talent needs understanding of large models. Another 25.9 percent of requirements focus on problem decomposition and business understanding. The articles leave open whether AI will eventually replace more complex human roles. They do not specify if the current involution in the game market will stabilize.

stories.Headline: AI music platforms Suno and Udio destroy livelihoods of independent musicians
stories.Summary:
AI platforms like Suno and Udio are wiping out independent musicians in 2026. These technologies generate millions of songs daily, which destroys the livelihoods of emerging artists. The process removes the need for human producers, arrangers, and mixing engineers. This shift happened as AI production costs plummeted compared to traditional methods. Many behind the scenes musicians are now disappearing from the industry.

Suno has 100 million users and 2 million paid subscribers earning 300 million US dollars. Global song registrations reached 51.2 million in 2025, which is 2.6 times the previous year. AI songs cost 0.1 yuan, while traditional songs cost 50,000 to 150,000 yuan. In 2025, AI songs made up 40 percent of new Tencent Music tracks. Deezer reports that 44 percent of daily uploads are AI generated.

Tianjin musician Zhang Yide says AI music has almost no flaws for most listeners. He believes unknown behind the scenes musicians have almost all been wiped out. Zhang claims that music is essentially mathematics and AI simply pushes computing power to extremes. He argues that audiences, not the songs themselves, provide the emotion and story. He notes that AI music is often too perfect, lacking human pitch flaws.

Independent musicians are affected, while top stars like Jay Chou and Hua Chenyu remain safe. Chou's new album earned 100 million yuan in four days, and Chenyu's performances drew 540,000 people. Surveyed musicians show 52 percent have no income and only 7 percent make a living. Revenue per 1,000 streams on domestic platforms is only 0.16 yuan to 1 yuan. Many former workshop owners have switched careers to open bars and restaurants.

AI music revenue shares are much lower than those for human made music. QQ Music pays 0.2 to 0.4 yuan for AI versus 1 to 2 yuan for humans. NetEase Cloud Music pays 0.7 to 1.2 yuan for AI versus 2 to 3 yuan for humans. Douyin Music pays 0.35 to 0.6 yuan for AI versus 1 to 2 yuan for humans. Traditional song quotations have dropped from 20,000 yuan to just dozens of yuan.

The trend of AI music is described as almost irreversible by the articles. Technology has erased thresholds for music theory, arrangement, and recording for all people. This creates a narrative where everyone can be a musician on the same starting line. The articles leave open whether this will cause a major downgrade in human aesthetics. It remains unclear if listeners will still pursue better things over homogeneous communication.

stories.Headline: Vection wins Italian business award in Melbourne for its Algho sign language AI system
stories.Summary:
Vection Technologies won an Innovation Award at the Italian Business Awards 2026 in Melbourne for its Algho Sign Language system, with UNOX presenting the award at the annual event hosted by the Italian Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Australia for Victoria and Tasmania. The company said the recognition highlights a product designed to let deaf people hold live conversations in sign language with an AI agent, supporting two-way conversations in International and Italian Sign Language. The system reads hand gestures, posture and facial expressions, then responds by signing in real time rather than using pre-recorded video. According to Vection, the sign-recognition tools, generation models and 3D agents used in the system were developed internally and integrated into its broader Algho conversational AI platform. The sign language system is already operating in several Italian transport hubs, including Roma Termini and Milano Centrale railway stations and Cagliari airport.

At Milan Bergamo Airport, Vection said its accessibility system, developed with Sorint.tek, serves as the main self-service terminal for passengers with disabilities, and it also serves wheelchair users and blind passengers. Based on unaudited airport data cited by Vection, 97% of passengers with disabilities can use the system independently, compared with 38% on a standard kiosk. The product was developed with ENS, Italy's national association for deaf people, and the National Research Council of Italy, and Vection also said it is developing real-time human interpreter support as an additional feature. The award comes as the business expands in Australia following its acquisition of Digital Experience Labs, which Vection described as an applied AI, process automation and decisioning services business. Vection said Algho Sign Language is one application of its broader Algho AI platform, which allows organisations to build and deploy AI agents without coding and is used for customer engagement, internal knowledge management, business process automation and decision support.

Earlier this year, Vection announced about AUD $4 million in new Algho AI contracts across 10 industry sectors in Italy, including rail transport, healthcare, water utilities, hospitality and education, and it said those contracts were close to the AUD $4.6 million in AI contracts it secured in the whole first half of FY26. In a separate agreement, the company announced a three-year framework deal with Swiss technology company URBANnext to commercialise Algho across European smart cities, public infrastructure and urban services, including a minimum annual purchase commitment of AUD $2.5 million and a minimum aggregate contract value of AUD $7.5 million over the initial term. Vection linked the latest award to its work on practical uses for AI in public-facing services, and it has positioned Algho as a platform for use across multiple sectors as well as in accessibility settings. Luis Nejo, Chief Executive Officer APAC at Vection Technologies, said the company was proud to receive the recognition from the Italian business community in Australia and that Algho Sign Language shows what inclusive AI can do outside the lab, with deaf passengers in some of Italy's busiest stations and airports now able to ask for help in their own language in real time.

stories.Headline: Tencent uses next-generation WorkBuddy to build a closed loop for AI-native applications
stories.Summary:
Tencent released its third quarter financial report on November 18, 2026, detailing its latest revenue and AI progress. The company is focusing on its next-generation WorkBuddy to create a successful closed loop for AI-native applications. This strategic shift follows internal meetings where leadership discussed the urgent need to adapt to rapid AI advancements. The company aims to move from enhancing existing businesses to building new AI-native increments. WorkBuddy now serves as the primary vehicle for this transition into the AI era.

The Q3 2026 report shows revenue of 2073.36 billion yuan, while profit for equity holders was 665.19 billion yuan. Value-added service revenue rose 3% to 983 billion yuan, and local market games reached 476 billion yuan. Marketing service revenue grew 19% to 430 billion yuan, and fintech and enterprise services reached 637 billion yuan. Cloud service revenue specifically saw a 35% year-on-year increase driven by Model-as-a-Service and GPU leasing. These figures reflect growth in games like Delta Action, Valorant: Source Energy Operation, and Honor of Kings.

Pony Ma stated in May that the company initially felt it had boarded the AI ship, but found it leaking. During the November 11 LinkTime meeting, he compared the AI wave to a tide swallowing hills and turning land warfare into naval warfare. He urged employees to upgrade their skills and get on board quickly to meet the battle. Tencent believes WorkBuddy has become the largest AI application in China, driving growth in cloud services. The company views WorkBuddy as a platform or operating system for the Agent era.

QuestMobile reported that Doubao, Qwen, and DeepSeek lead AI-native apps, while Tencent's Yuanbao saw monthly active users drop to 37.33 million. Nomura Securities noted ByteDance's ecosystem share rose to 38.3% in April 2026, while Tencent's share fell to 30.8%. WorkBuddy affects 14 million enterprises through WeCom and covers 50% of China's top 500 enterprises across 50 industries. Over 50,000 developers and collaborators now use the tool. Competitors like Alibaba and ByteDance are catching up with Qwen Office and Doubao Work.

Tencent previously relied on a C to B strategy, using consumer habits to enter business scenarios. The company shut down several AI products, including QClaw, Tencent Meta-Element, Tencent Translator, and Zhiying, to migrate capabilities. WorkBuddy evolved from CodeBuddy, an internal tool where teams worked on-site with enterprise customers to iterate. This allowed the tool to move from technical coding to general office scenarios for non-technical users. It now integrates with Tencent Docs, QQ Mail, and Tencent News.

On October 29, Tencent launched Buddy One to connect internal tools like Tencent Meeting and Tencent Cloud Drive. WorkBuddy currently has over 10 million daily active users who consume over 100 trillion tokens every day. In September, it led AI office rankings with 32.35 million monthly active users. The company continues to expand enterprise orders in banking, insurance, hospitals, FMCG, construction, and media. The articles leave open how Tencent will maintain its lead as competitors narrow the gap.

stories.Headline: Knightcorp report warns AI and cloud gaps leave insurance cover open to dispute
stories.Summary:
Knightcorp has launched its Forerunner Report - Technology, which examines insurance issues linked to AI, cyber risk, cloud exposure, directors' liability and connected devices, according to an article published by IT Brief Australia on 16 November 2026. The research argues that insurance reviews are struggling to keep pace with how technology businesses now operate, particularly when companies rely on AI tools, cloud infrastructure and third-party software platforms. It presents insurance less as an annual procurement exercise and more as part of broader risk governance for finance leaders, boards and technology teams. One of the report's central findings is that policy wording may not clearly address AI-related claims, and Knightcorp said some professional indemnity and cyber policies are silent on AI, which could leave room for disputes over whether cover applies when businesses build AI into their own products or use AI embedded in third-party platforms. The report says AI exclusions are appearing in some policy wordings, citing Lander & Rogers, which adds pressure on companies to check whether their existing insurance arrangements match their use of the technology.

On cloud cover, Knightcorp said undeclared systems, or systems that do not fit a policy's wording, can become a point of dispute during claims, and it suggests businesses map third-party systems that handle client data and then test how each one is treated in policy applications and wording. The report applies the same logic to connected hardware, saying companies that make or supply smart devices should check whether new mandatory security standards apply to them, including rules banning universal default passwords on in-scope consumer devices manufactured after a specified threshold. It also highlights action by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission over misleading sustainability claims, noting that penalties in greenwashing cases involving Mercer Superannuation and Vanguard Investments fell on the companies involved, and it notes that organisations covered by the Privacy Act that use automated decision-making in certain ways will need to disclose that use in their privacy policies. Trent Brown, Chief Executive Officer of Knightcorp, said the issue for companies is whether insurance arrangements still reflect the pace of change inside technology businesses, and he said the question is no longer simply whether a company is insured but whether its risk and insurance arrangements still reflect the business it has become. Brown said that uncertainty is most likely to surface in policy interpretation and claims handling, particularly once an incident has already occurred.

Justin Geldart, Account Director at Knightcorp, said that where a policy is silent on AI the outcome is uncertain and coverage can be disputed, and he encouraged technology leaders to ask how their cover treats AI they build versus AI they buy because the answer can differ. Jessica Tanner, Technology Account Director at Knightcorp, said claims tend to be tested on what was declared and how the policy defines it, and that for a technology business the practical question is whether the wording and the application reflect the platforms the business actually relies on. The report also refers to a Federal Court development in the Medibank matter, where Deloitte reports prepared after the cyber incident were found not to be protected by legal professional privilege, underlining the importance of how post-incident reviews are commissioned. It includes several tools intended to help organisations assess these questions, including a matrix of exposures, a broker checklist for AI risk, examples of where claims uncertainty can begin, and an 11-question insurance readiness checklist. It also features a client endorsement from Spriggy Co-Founder Alex Badran, who said that before working with Knightcorp it felt like the company was trying to piece together off-the-shelf solutions from different providers and that Knightcorp spent the time to understand its unique needs and built insurance solutions to fit its business.

Articles.Title: Knightcorp warns tech leaders over AI & cloud gaps - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Pronto Software marks 50 years with accelerated AI investment and security-first ERP roadmap
stories.Summary:
Melbourne-based ERP company Pronto Software is marking 50 years in business, using the anniversary to highlight an accelerated investment in artificial intelligence that it has been developing since 2021, when it began exploring machine learning before speeding up its roadmap after generative and agentic AI emerged. Managing Director and CEO Chad Gates, who has led the company for a decade and joined 21 years ago, said the rapid pace of development has forced software providers to reconsider how they build and deliver products. Pronto has taken what it describes as a deliberate, security-first approach, building its own GPU infrastructure within Pronto Cloud and hosting large language models internally while still allowing connections to external models so it is not dependent on a single provider. The architecture is designed around authentication, permissions and access controls so that AI agents and connected systems cannot access information or perform actions beyond their authorised capabilities. Gates said the company took the position early that it would provide a high-trust model, describing AI as a capability rather than a technology and saying the data is where the value lies rather than the AI itself.

He said customers are primarily concerned with two issues, security and productivity, wanting to know how AI can improve efficiency while worrying about exposing sensitive information or investing in technology that fails to deliver returns. Pronto has operated debt-free since its inception, and Gates said its independent ownership structure and local presence remain competitive advantages against large multinational providers, particularly with owner-operated customers who can speak directly with staff. He said the technology will change dramatically but the truth should never change. Looking ahead, Gates said AI will fundamentally change how employees interact with ERP platforms, potentially reducing the need for traditional interfaces filled with screens, forms and menus as staff increasingly rely on AI assistants and agents to retrieve information, generate reports and interpret business data through conversation.

He suggested future product development could become less reliant on building dedicated screens for every new feature, with AI generating interfaces and reports when users need them. He identified agent-to-agent communication as another significant area of development as businesses deploy larger numbers of autonomous agents, raising questions around coordination, permissions and the management of data and workflows. Quantum-safe encryption is also a priority, with Gates warning that advances in quantum computing combined with increasingly capable AI systems could create considerable security challenges that providers need to prepare for before the technology becomes mainstream. Gates believes the scale and speed of change now underway will exceed anything the business has experienced previously, and he said the challenge will be continuing to innovate while maintaining the security, reliability and customer relationships that have underpinned the company's longevity.

stories.Headline: Instructure launches Foundry venture and Athena AI study coach for Canvas
stories.Summary:
Instructure has launched Instructure Foundry, a standalone venture focused on AI development for education, and its first project is Project Athena, an AI study coach designed to work with Canvas, according to an announcement reported on 17 November 2026. The venture brings together small teams to develop and refine new products with input from educators and institutions, while Instructure continues developing its existing platforms, including Canvas, Mastery and Parchment. Project Athena is being built to give students study support based on material already in their Canvas courses, using course content, assignments and upcoming assessments to generate personalised quizzes, study guides and coaching prompts. Athena will connect to the learning environment through a read-only link governed by existing student permissions, and Instructure said student conversations with the tool will not be used to train external AI models. In the United States, Hinds Community College is involved in the initiative following an initial pilot, and the project is expected to extend access to its 7,000 students.

The tool is intended to give students extra support outside classroom and tutoring hours, and by drawing on a student's own course context in Canvas it is expected to identify gaps in understanding and adjust prompts as learning progresses. Instructure said the structure is intended to help it move faster on emerging technologies without affecting the stability of products already used by schools, universities and vocational education providers. Shiren Vijiasingam, Chief Product Officer at Instructure, said AI has changed what is possible, with small teams now able to build and test new ideas faster than before, and he said Foundry gives those teams space to iterate on emerging solutions rapidly while core products continue to get sustained investment. He said Project Athena represents what Instructure believes responsible AI in education should look like, grounded in learning science, connected to the learning environment and built to support understanding through skill mastery, and he said it will coach toward mastery rather than answers. Zach Pendleton, Chief Architect at Instructure, said the pace of change has outrun the conventional roadmap, and he said investors have provided incremental funding so the venture does not compete with investment the core products need.

He described Instructure as running two tracks, one that serves and scales what it has built and one that explores what is next. The launch reflects a wider debate in education over how institutions should use AI while protecting student information, maintaining academic integrity and keeping educators central to teaching, and providers in Australia and elsewhere have been weighing whether to adopt new tools within systems they already use or through separate applications. The announcement comes as education providers seek AI tools that can be integrated into existing platforms rather than used as standalone consumer applications, which creates pressure on software companies serving the sector to show both speed of development and controls around privacy, security and educator oversight. Athena is under development and is being created with educators and institutions, and as the first project to emerge from Foundry it will test whether tightly integrated AI study support can gain traction with institutions seeking more direct control over how students use generative AI.

stories.Headline: Tencent increases capital expenditure to build data centers and servers for its AI business
stories.Summary:
Tencent released its third quarter financial report on November 18, 2026, detailing a massive increase in spending. The company spent 81.433 billion yuan on capital expenditure, which is over five times the amount from last year. This spending was primarily used to purchase servers and build data center facilities to support its AI business. Revenue for the company rose by 8 percent, but adjusted operating profit dropped by 6 percent. The company also spent 32.362 billion yuan on research and development during this specific quarter.

The capital expenditure of 81.433 billion yuan exceeded market forecasts by 26 billion yuan. Actual cash paid out reached 65.1 billion yuan, while prepayments for computing power rose to 162.9 billion yuan. Property and equipment values grew from 149.9 billion to 242.5 billion yuan, and construction in progress reached 23 billion yuan. Operating profit was 59.1 billion yuan under international standards, but 68.1 billion yuan on a non-international basis. Excluding five AI products, the operating profit was 83.3 billion yuan, maintaining a 40 percent margin.

The five core AI products are Hy, Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, and Xiaowei. Martin Lau stated that Tencent was previously cautious about China's enterprise software market but now sees AI as a catalyst. He noted that the next generation of the Hunyuan model will take longer to launch due to chip restrictions. Lau also reported that WorkBuddy has over 10 million daily active users and 100 trillion daily token consumption. He compared the revenue potential of these AI tools to the mechanics of online games.

James Mitchell, the Chief Strategy Officer, stated that capital expenditure has reached its peak level for now. He believes the cloud business will not be materially or negatively affected by United States chip controls. WorkBuddy affects many businesses, with 60 percent of China's top 100 enterprises now using the tool. Half of China's top 500 enterprises across more than 50 industries have also become customers. One specific user spent 40,000 yuan on token purchases in a single month.

Tencent Cloud services revenue grew by 35 percent this quarter, driven by GPU leasing and Model as a Service. MaaS revenue increased by more than 300 percent quarter on quarter, while WorkBuddy revenue grew fivefold. The Hy4 flash model reduced costs by activating only 12 billion of its 224 billion parameters. This efficiency allows the model to be priced 95 percent lower than the standard Hy4 version. The company is now sending engineers to customer sites to increase the usage of WorkBuddy.

Spending is expected to fluctuate at current levels through next year before declining after 2027. James Mitchell expects the financial situation to improve by 2028 as equipment prices drop and efficiency rises. WorkBuddy's annualized gross revenue has already exceeded 500 million US dollars based on recent performance. The company is shifting to a subscription and token usage billing model for its enterprise software. It remains uncertain how future chip control policies will change or impact long term training.

stories.Headline: OpenAI's model lifts AMD GPU IP performance 14% in under five months
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 19, 2026, that its model boosted the PPA of AMD's flagship GPU IP by up to 14% in less than five months, work that previously took human engineers about a full year. OpenAI's research proved the model can explore brand-new processor architectures in RISC-V evaluation tasks and achieve incremental optimization on mature mass-produced designs such as Jalapeño, AMD's next-generation flagship GPU and CPU. Jalapeño, OpenAI's first self-developed inference chip, adopts the model's modification scheme, reducing the vector unit's standard cell area by about 13% and the matrix unit's by about 10%. OpenAI said these optimization effects were verified during Jalapeño's tape-out and debugging phase. OpenAI evaluated multiple generations of models sequentially against two open-source processor designs to measure end-to-end chip design capability.

All five models, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5, scored higher designing processor cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs. OpenAI is cooperating with Synopsys to integrate AI capabilities into the EDA toolchain engineers use for chip design and verification. In early 2025, GPT-4o was already used to assist in designing Jalapeño, achieving notable PPA optimizations. The vector unit handles parallel computing tasks, and its gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers, conversion circuits, reduction logic and special function units, with the model exploring logic schemes and pipeline splits. The matrix unit's gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers and low-precision dot product circuits, with one multiplier redesigned to cut synthesized cell area by about 15% and latency from two clock cycles to one.

OpenAI collaborated with AMD on PPA optimization, achieving a maximum 14% performance improvement for the flagship GPU IP on top of the original deeply optimized baseline. OpenAI said the model taps more optimization space by rewriting the code describing the chip's circuits, equivalent to completing about a full year of R&D workload in less than 5 months. AMD has applied some optimized changes to designs recently sent for tape-out, and other schemes were incorporated into mass production design files for subsequent iterative versions. Researchers observed the model can reach the level of a senior micro-architect and perform reasoning analysis on RTL code. The model rewrites circuits for arithmetic operations, control operations and data movement, using Synopsys tools to verify every rewrite preserves the module's original function and to evaluate power, performance and area trade-offs.

AMD's verification shows that with the design generated by OpenAI's model, multiple core modules of its next-generation flagship CPU achieved several percentage points of PPA improvement. The results on Jalapeño and AMD chips prove the model can optimize mass-production-level designs. OpenAI tested with two open-source 32-bit RISC-V cores: PicoRV32, a streamlined core for reprogrammable chips such as FPGAs, and OpenTitan, which uses Ibex as an embedded processor in its secure chips. Researchers gave each model generation the original hardware description code of each core and asked it to improve throughput, verifying each design by simulation, scoring 0 if it failed verification or occupied more than 16 times the original core's area. Passing designs were measured with test workloads the model had never seen, using instructions per clock cycle, the geometric mean of results, and maximum clock frequency estimated by Yosys to estimate instructions per second.

For each processor core, researchers set the optimal throughput observed under the same constraints as the baseline of 1.0. Under about 112,000 tokens per single call, GPT-6.2 Astra had the highest average score on both cores, and GPT-6.1 Sol scored higher than GPT-5.6 Sol on both. In the second task, researchers provided written requirements and templates in the open-source code defining how the core connects with other system parts, and the model independently chose the internal data flow path and multi-stage pipeline split. For both cores, correctness verification, storage and cache configuration, and throughput targets matched the earlier RTL optimization task. With about 112,000 tokens per single call, all five models scored higher designing cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs, holding for both PicoRV32 and Ibex.

GPT-6.2 Astra's improvement on Ibex was greater than on PicoRV32, and 9881 valid scoring runs were completed across two tasks, two cores and all token resource configurations. Designing from scratch lets the model omit some native functions of the original core, such as performance counters and extended instructions, whose contribution to throughput under the test workload was limited, partially explaining the higher score. OpenAI says that if these functions were forced to be retained, stricter circuit area constraints set, and timing checks performed after physical synthesis, the tests would be closer to real mass production chip design. OpenAI's results show AI can already tap incremental benefits on mature mass-produced designs and independently explore microarchitecture space based on specifications. This may give rise to a new battlefield for future chip competition, with chip manufacturers needing to focus not only on process, packaging and architecture but also on using AI to improve efficiency, converge PPA faster and shorten R&D cycles.

The article is from the WeChat official account Zhidx, authored by Cheng Qian and edited by Li Shuiqing, published with authorization from 36Kr. OpenAI's evaluation covered two tasks, two processor cores and all token resource configurations, and the articles leave open which specific optimization schemes AMD incorporated into mass production files versus tape-out designs. The articles do not state when Jalapeño tapes out or ships, nor the timing of further Synopsys toolchain integration. They do not give the PPA figures for AMD's next-generation flagship CPU beyond several percentage points, nor name that CPU. They do not say whether the omitted native functions will be restored in future evaluations or how the 14% GPU IP improvement was measured.

stories.Headline: HCLTech and Cohere partner to build sovereign AI solutions for enterprises and governments
stories.Summary:
HCLTech and Cohere announced on 17 November 2026 that they have partnered to build and deliver sovereign artificial intelligence solutions for enterprises and governments. Under the agreement, HCLTech will become one of Cohere's preferred global systems integrator partners in Canada and Germany. The two companies plan to combine Cohere's sovereign AI platform and models with HCLTech's professional services and AI implementation capabilities. They also intend to extend the partnership to other markets beyond Canada and Germany. The initial development work will focus on insurance, financial services, and manufacturing, according to the companies.

Potential applications include jurisdiction-aware claims assessment, secure analysis of sensitive financial data, and faster access to technical documentation. The partnership will use Cohere's models and its North agentic AI platform, alongside domain-adapted models and retrieval and reasoning capabilities. The companies said the solutions would be deployed in customers' preferred environments to address data residency, security, and regulatory requirements. Phil Blunsom, Chief Technology Officer at Cohere, said organisations should not have to choose between the benefits of AI and control over their data. He said the partnership with HCLTech would help customers tackle complex, industry-specific challenges while meeting their security, governance and data sovereignty requirements.

HCLTech Executive Vice President and Canada Country Head Dave Chopra said the partnership would combine Cohere's platform with HCLTech's local presence in Canada to help organisations adopt AI. The companies also said both hold ISO 42001 certification, the international standard for AI management systems. Cohere was co-founded by Aidan Gomez, Nick Frosst, and Ivan Zhang in 2019, and Gomez was the youngest co-author of the landmark Google research paper that invented the Transformer architecture powering generative AI. The agreement follows HCLTech's October partnership with Anthropic to expand enterprise adoption of agentic AI through its Claude models, which included plans for a dedicated Anthropic business unit and a Centre of Excellence. HCLTech has also pursued sovereign AI initiatives in India, and in February HCLSoftware partnered with Sify Digital Services to develop a sovereign AI stack for Indian enterprises.

stories.Headline: Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud partner to expand AI education across over 1,000 Indian schools and colleges
stories.Summary:
Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud announced on 17 November 2026 that they will partner to expand AI education across more than 1,000 public and private schools and colleges in India, combining hands-on learning programmes with industry-aligned certifications. The initiative will pair Accenture LearnVantage's learning programmes with Google Cloud's unified AI stack to set up AI Labs in schools and Centres of Excellence in higher education institutions. The programmes will cover foundational AI literacy, applied generative AI, agentic AI and AI engineering, with the stated aim of preparing students for emerging technology roles. The partnership will also introduce structured learning pathways for students and educators, supported by Google's AI tools and personalised coaching through Gemini.

At the school level, the two companies plan to establish AI Labs powered by Google Gemini that introduce younger students to foundational AI concepts in controlled learning environments where they can experiment with AI tools and develop practical skills. For higher education institutions, the partnership plans Centres of Excellence, centres and academies that will serve as hubs for applied learning, innovation and industry collaboration, giving students access to modern tools, expert mentorship and opportunities to work with emerging technologies. The curriculum will include generative AI and agentic AI literacy, applied generative AI and agentic AI programmes, an AI developer programme and AI engineering, and students who complete the programmes and assessments will receive certifications. The platform will also offer guided learning pathways, multilingual voice capabilities and AI-driven content to make learning more accessible, and institutions will be able to explore customised offerings, including degree programmes, aligned with changing industry requirements.

Anurag Bansal, Managing Director of Accenture LearnVantage for Asia Oceania and the Middle East, said in a statement that the future of learning will be shaped by how learning pathways and talent creation for careers are reimagined as those careers continue to evolve. The collaboration will also support Accenture LearnVantage's existing national AI initiatives, including the National AI Olympiad and AI Infinity, which aim to encourage AI literacy and introduce students to careers in emerging technologies. The announcement was published by Analytics India Magazine on 17 November 2026, the same day the outlet listed a related story on HCLTech partnering with Cohere to target sovereign AI markets. The articles do not say what funding the initiative involves, how institutions will be selected or when the labs and centres are expected to open.

stories.Headline: Dreamteam raises $53m to build AI-native CRM with four AI sales teammates
stories.Summary:
Dreamteam has raised $53 million across its seed and Series A rounds to build an AI-native customer relationship management platform that uses multiple AI teammates to manage sales workflows and customer relationships. The funding was led by Together Fund and Accel, with participation from Premji Invest, according to an article published by Analytics India Magazine on 17 November 2026. The company says more than 100 companies across 13 countries currently use its platform. The money will help Dreamteam expand the platform, which aims to reduce the manual work involved in maintaining traditional CRM systems. The platform currently offers four AI teammates, each assigned a specific sales function.

Rachel acts as a market analyst who researches prospects and their companies, while Sally manages deals and follow-ups. Raj monitors sales pipelines and identifies potential risks, and Alex handles CRM configuration based on business requirements. The four agents operate through a shared system called Company Brain, which keeps customer information from calls, emails and meetings, so the agents can access previous conversations, customer priorities and outstanding commitments instead of working independently. The system is also designed to update CRM records as customer relationships and business requirements change. Anand Venkatraman, co-founder and CEO of Dreamteam, said AI finally gives the company a way to change the foundation of CRM.

He said Dreamteam learns from the work a team is already doing, keeps the context alive and gives every salesperson skilled AI teammates that can reason over it and move work forward. Dreamteam argues that conventional CRMs, where representatives manually record interactions, update deal information and track follow-ups, often fail to capture important details from customer conversations. The company says its agents operate within company-defined policies, pricing rules and approval limits, that emails require human approval before being sent, and that users can inspect the sources behind recommendations and correct information stored by the system. Dreamteam plans to expand the agents' responsibilities beyond individual sales tasks to manage broader customer journeys, including lead generation, renewals and account expansion. It also envisions its agents eventually communicating with buyers' AI systems to exchange requirements and handle routine business interactions.

stories.Headline: Chinese content platforms launch AI creator competitions to build sustainable production ecosystems
stories.Summary:
Domestic content platforms launched an intensive wave of AI creator competitions starting in the second half of 2026. These activities aim to build thriving ecosystems rather than just grabbing talent. The platforms seek creators who can tell distinctive stories and create recognizable aesthetics. This movement focuses on the upper reaches of the content production chain. It marks a new era of large scale talent acquisition.

iQIYI launched its New Year's Eve Gala call on November 13 for the 2027 event. It offers 10,000 yuan to ten winners and provides Nado Pro computing power points. Orca Entertainment's Whale Sharp competition offers a 10 million yuan pool with 2 million yuan maximum prizes. Tencent Video's Fire Dragon AIGC Hackathon runs from December 5 to 7 in Hangzhou. The Fire Dragon Manhua Drama Challenge began September 28 and ends December 20.

Platform leaders believe creativity is the core barrier of content creation now. They state that technical problems can be solved using platform tools and resources. The industry consensus is to value narrative and creativity over showing off technical skills. Platforms no longer ask which models creators use for their work. They now focus on what stories creators want to tell.

Filmmaker Zhang Xiaobei says screenwriters will become more important in the AI era. He argues that image costs have been leveled across all themes and types. This shift affects individual creators, creative teams, and professional institutions. These groups must now compete on emotions, aesthetics, and unique perspectives. The competitions target a wide range of creators, including ordinary people of all professions.

ByteDance launched the AI Creation Wave Plan on September 4 and the Hongguo plan on October 15. Jimeng started a partner plan on October 30 for institutions instead of individuals. Kuaishou began its second AI National Creation Season on November 16. Baidu's AI Future Creation League S5 runs from October 23 to January 23, 2027. Mango TV and Migu Digital Media started a youth competition on October 30.

Platforms will use these competitions as tools for public bidding and talent screening. They intend to embed AI capabilities into the mainstream content production process. The goal is to find long term partners for dramas, galas, and films. The articles leave open how the signing and incubation processes will function. stories.Headline: CtrlS Datacentres targets 4.4 GW of data centre capacity by 2030
stories.Summary:
CtrlS Datacentres is targeting 4.4 GW of data centre capacity by 2030, the company said in an interview published by Analytics India Magazine on 16 November 2026. Rahul Dhar, President of Global Data Centre Operations, Enterprise Colo Delivery, Programme Management and Energy R&D at CtrlS Datacentres, gave the interview to AIM. CtrlS recently announced a ₹10,000 crore investment in Bihar to set up a 150 MW AI factory in Bodh Gaya. The company is also expanding its presence in Bihar with a ₹400 crore data centre in Patna. CtrlS’s Patna data centre currently has 12 MW of IT capacity, with scope to scale up as demand increases.

The strategy is to bring infrastructure closer to customers, particularly content-based businesses that need to serve users in smaller cities, Dhar said. Dhar said the new facility would support demand for digital infrastructure in Bihar and eastern India. CtrlS plans to establish more than 20 edge data centres across tier-2 and tier-3 cities over the coming years with improved fibre connectivity. It currently operates 19 data centres across 10 cities, including Lucknow, Noida, Kolkata and Gandhinagar, and operates a containerised data centre in Bhubaneswar. Hyperscalers constitute the largest source of demand for CtrlS, although the company also serves nearly 40 Indian public and private sector banks.

Nikhil Kamath, Co-founder of Zerodha, and entrepreneur Sreeram Reddy Vanga recently invested a combined ₹250 crore in CtrlS Datacenters. Canadian Pension Plan Investment Board also invested around ₹7,000 crore in the company earlier this year. Dhar attributes investor interest in CtrlS to its focus on hyperscale campuses, advance planning for high-capacity grid power, and modular designs. CtrlS is building greenfield data centre campuses for hyperscalers in Hyderabad and Mumbai. It is also in discussions with neocloud companies seeking capacity, and expects to deliver against its existing commitments over the next 12, 24 months.

This year, the central government introduced a 21-year tax holiday for foreign companies providing global cloud services using India-based data centres. Dhar said it won’t affect CtrlS’s existing demand, which is driven by domestic customers as well as global technology companies. He said that even with the tax holiday and a possible influx of foreign investors, Indian colocation providers have a good order book in hand. Dhar said India needs to shorten the period for forecasting data centre power requirements and speed up approvals for power transmission lines and fibre networks. Utilities and government departments typically seek power consumption on 7, 8 year horizons, he said.

Dhar said the projection that typical governments or power or utility departments ask for can be reduced to three to four years. Data centres are growing from facilities with capacities of around 5, 8 megawatts to campuses ranging from 10, 100 MW. Dhar said operators are bulk consumers of power, so they need better planning or better awareness among various government departments on how much power they need, at what time and at which location. He also called for faster right-of-way approvals to lay fibre networks and transmission lines, particularly when operators acquire land on city outskirts. CtrlS is providing inputs to government bodies and industry associations, including the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, NASSCOM and the Confederation of Indian Industry, on India’s recently proposed data centre policy.

Several states, including Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, have already introduced data centre policies. According to Mordor Intelligence estimates, India consumed about 150 billion litres of water in 2025 to cool about 1.5 GW of data centre capacity, a figure expected to more than double by 2030. CtrlS uses closed-loop chillers to limit water loss and is reusing treated wastewater at one of its Mumbai facilities to reduce dependence on fresh water. The company also owns and operates a nearly 100 MW captive solar farm in Nagpur, with the power fed into the grid to offset consumption at its Mumbai data centres and similar initiatives planned for other locations, including Hyderabad. CtrlS also operates its facilities at a power usage effectiveness of around 1.4.

Dhar said CtrlS is prepared to support customers deploying liquid-cooled infrastructure, including GPU providers and cloud companies. He said all of CtrlS’s data centres are rated tier-4 data centres, and the company uses external certification and has introduced an Integrated Command and Control Centre in Hyderabad to monitor infrastructure centrally. The centre supports predictive analysis and preventive maintenance, and CtrlS is also applying AI to infrastructure monitoring, including CCTV systems, to improve responses to operational issues. Dhar said data centre operators will need to keep adapting their facilities to changing chip technologies, power densities and cooling systems as AI workloads increase infrastructure requirements. The article was published on 16 November 2026.

stories.Headline: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory inference engine to provide enterprises with local model access in India
stories.Summary:
The AI unicorn Sarvam AI launched its Token Factory inference engine on November 18, 2026. This new offering allows enterprises to access various AI models through a single API. The system runs workloads on GPU clusters located within India. Sarvam AI intends to capture the local AI inference market with this tool. It aims to compete against global giants in the technology sector.

Token Factory hosts a 105B model from Sarvam and open-weight models from Google, DeepSeek, GLM, and Kimi. The system uses a three-tier caching architecture to provide high latency and throughput speeds. It operates on India-based GPU clusters to help enterprises meet strict data residency mandates. The company offers on-premises inference deployments and dedicated GPU capacity for BFSI customers. Developers can switch between these models without setting up their own compute.

Sarvam AI is responsible for the launch of this new inference engine. The company claims that its speeds rival those of global inference leaders. It positions itself as a champion of sovereign Indian AI infrastructure. The firm says that hosting global models locally supports necessary data residency. Sarvam believes Indian enterprises will pay for multi-model flexibility and local inference.

Critics argue that hosting overseas models may dilute the push for homegrown AI capability. Other companies like Krutrim have hosted DeepSeek models on Indian servers since last year. OpenAI recently introduced India-based API inference for GPT-6 Luna workloads. Anthropic offers in-country inference for select Claude models through Amazon Bedrock. These existing services make some wonder if Sarvam is arriving too late.

The company is operating in a crowded arena with cloud giants and global providers. The AI ecosystem is expected to add 1.7 trillion dollars to India's GDP by 2035. Global giants like OpenAI and Anthropic have opened offices and increased investments in India. Sarvam must navigate a market where competitors are moving very quickly. The firm relies on the demand for sovereign infrastructure and data residency.

Sarvam must continuously invest in software, GPUs, and enterprise relationships to win clients. The company needs to maintain its competitive edge against fast-moving global inference providers. It remains to be seen if the local playbook will successfully attract enterprises. The articles do not state the specific pricing for the Token Factory service. They leave open whether Sarvam can outpace the global giants in this market.

stories.Headline: Reliance Jio stops new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription
stories.Summary:
Reliance Jio has stopped accepting new claims for its free Google AI Pro subscription, which gave eligible users up to 18 months of access to Google's premium Gemini features. The redemption window ran from October 30, 2025, to October 29, 2026, according to terms and conditions listed on Jio's website. Jio's support page now says the offer is unavailable on new recharges or plan upgrades. The offer initially covered users over the age of 18 on unlimited 5G plans priced at ₹349 or above. Starting February 11, 2026, Jio temporarily extended eligibility to users on plans priced at ₹299 or above that offered 1.5 GB of data per day.

Users who activated the offer can continue using the subscription for up to 18 months from activation, provided they maintain an eligible recharge plan. Eligible users could activate the subscription, valued at ₹1,950 per month, through the MyJio app. Subscribers were required to maintain an eligible recharge plan throughout the subscription period to retain access to the benefits. Jio reserved the right to suspend access if users failed to maintain the required plan. The development comes a year after Reliance Industries Ltd, through its AI arm Reliance Intelligence, partnered with Google to accelerate AI adoption in India by offering free Google AI Pro access to Jio users.

Announcing the partnership, RIL said the 18-month subscription would provide access to Gemini 2.5 Pro through the Gemini app, higher limits for image and video generation using Nano Banana and Veo models, expanded access to NotebookLM, and 2 TB of cloud storage, among other benefits. The company valued the combined package at ₹35,100 per user. Beyond the consumer-facing offering, the partnership also positioned Reliance Intelligence as a strategic Google Cloud partner in India, with plans to expand access to Google's proprietary AI hardware accelerators, or TPUs, for local organisations. Inc42 has reached out to Jio for further details on the development, and the story will be updated on receiving a response. Separately, Jio Platforms is in talks with the Indian Space Research Organisation, Skyroot Aerospace, and other domestic launch providers for its proposed constellation of 1,600 satellites in low Earth orbit.

The company is exploring whether it can carry out the programme in India, from satellite design to launch and operations. It is also in discussions with SpaceX. Jio Platforms listed on the BSE and NSE on October 28 at ₹1,358 apiece, a 21.4% premium to its issue price of ₹1,119. On the financial front, the company reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, marking a 13.7% increase from ₹7,379 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, net profit grew 8% from ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue rose 11.4% YoY and 3.3% sequentially to ₹40,475 Cr in the quarter under review. The offer was the consumer-facing part of Reliance's AI partnership with Google, which also covers the distribution of Gemini Enterprise and access to Google's AI chips for Indian organisations. The redemption window ended on October 29, 2026, a year after the offer launched. Eligible subscribers could activate the offer through the MyJio app. More to follow.

stories.Headline: PwC and Harvey launch a Pillar Two tax assistant spanning 21 countries
stories.Summary:
PwC and Harvey launched the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant, a specialist research tool within Harvey, on November 17, 2026, according to a post by the Harvey Team. The assistant covers the OECD Pillar Two rules alongside country-specific material supplied by PwC network firms and currently spans 21 countries. It draws only on vetted public sources: enacted and draft local legislation, tax authority guidance, and other official publications such as government consultations. Online sources are refreshed weekly, new documents are added monthly, and the content is reviewed quarterly. Users select it as a source in Harvey, filter by the countries they need, and use it alongside Harvey's other platform features.

More than 8,000 multinational groups are in scope of Pillar Two, the OECD framework that sets a 15% global minimum effective tax rate for groups with consolidated revenue of €750 million or more. According to the OECD, 45 jurisdictions have already taken steps to introduce the Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) rules. GloBE calculations generally start from each entity's financial accounts, as prepared for the parent's consolidated statements, and then require jurisdiction-specific adjustments, and some domestic regimes may substitute consolidated statements with local accounts. The assistant has been rolled out to more than 17,000 PwC users across 21 countries and has recorded more than 70,000 user activities across more than 24,000 conversation threads. Monthly use grew roughly 17x, from about 700 activities in October 2025 to more than 12,000 in September 2026.

The assistant is PwC's go-to tool for Pillar Two technical research, and PwC has also rolled it out to clients, with positive feedback. A PwC Senior Associate, International Tax, Japan, said the module significantly improves the efficiency of their day-to-day Pillar Two work by helping them quickly navigate filing obligations, deadlines, and jurisdiction-specific requirements. A PwC Manager, International Tax, Germany, noted the module provides quick, well-structured overviews and access to relevant guidance and legislation, making country-specific research more efficient and effective. A Head of Tax of a multi-national group said they had a very positive experience with the module and would certainly recommend it to other clients looking for additional support and guidance on Pillar 2. The assistant drafts memos on the rules, on elements of the effective tax rate calculation, and on safe harbours and exclusions, and it also helps users check their analysis and prepare reports and emails.

Answers include citations that link directly to the underlying legislation and guidance, so users can check the work quickly. Users can upload a group's facts to see what data the rules require, and they can explore scenarios that might change the top-up tax payable, or test whether simplifications or safe harbours could apply. A custom Harvey Agent tests each jurisdiction in a group against the FY2025 transitional CbCR safe harbours: the de minimis test, the simplified ETR test, and the routine profits test. The agent normalizes and reconciles the underlying data and flags any breaks, and where a jurisdiction fails all three tests, it calculates an indicative top-up tax and shows where it would be collected, either locally or at the parent.

It also lists open questions by priority, links each result to its source data, and compares results across reporting perimeters, and the output is an Excel workbook showing the ETR working with live formulas, along with a self-contained interactive HTML view of the results. For tax teams, two challenges stand out, the first being data and the second being interpretation. Working out exactly what data each country's rules require, and whether a group's data supports it, is often the hardest part. The OECD rules don't settle every local nuance, so teams must read the global rulebook alongside each country's legislation.

The framework is global, but implementation is local, and those local differences decide what a group files, when it files, and how much top-up tax it owes. The assistant gives tax teams a single, trusted place to work through Pillar Two, which is complex, varies by country, and constantly changes. Harvey will demonstrate the Pillar Two Tax AI Assistant and the Pillar Two Agent live at the PwC Tax Evolution Summit on November 18 in Madrid, Spain. PwC said people can contact their local PwC team to learn more about how they are helping clients with Pillar Two.

The articles do not say what the assistant will cover beyond the current 21 countries or when further countries might be added. They do not give the price of the tool or the terms of the PwC and Harvey arrangement. They do not say how the quarterly content review is carried out or who performs it. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Jastech wins South Korea world-class product status for its JFS humidity control solution
stories.Summary:
South Korean semiconductor humidity-control specialist Jastech said its second-generation humidity control solution, JFS, also called a Jet Flow Straightener, has been selected as a 2026 World-Class Product by South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, known as KOTRA. The selection marks the second consecutive year the company has earned the certification, following its first-generation N2 LPM product last year. The World-Class Product designation is a certification program under which the ministry and KOTRA award domestic products after comprehensively evaluating their global market competitiveness, technological prowess and growth potential. With the latest selection, Jastech has received official recognition of its technological competitiveness in the semiconductor humidity-control field.

JFS manages humidity by precisely controlling airflow inside semiconductor manufacturing processes, and applying it alongside N2 LPM can reduce cleanroom humidity, typically around 45% in ambient air, to as little as 1%. The first-generation N2 LPM laid the groundwork for yield improvement with nitrogen purge technology and can lower humidity to below 5%, while JFS adds precision airflow control for a higher level of humidity control. Jastech developed JFS for the first time in the world after about three years of research and development, and is currently supplying it to major global integrated device manufacturers. According to industry sources, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and U.S.-based Micron are known to have adopted Jastech's humidity-control solutions.

Cumulative sales of N2 LPM have now surpassed 300 billion won, approximately $225.4 million, and the company has set a goal of achieving 300 billion won in total company revenue by 2030 through expanded JFS supply. Ha Jung-min, director of Jastech's research institute and a vice president, said JFS is an optimal solution for improving yields in the increasingly ultra-fine and advanced HBM process environment. He said that as cumulative sales of the first-generation N2 LPM have comfortably exceeded 300 billion won, the company will make JFS a solid foundation for achieving 300 billion won in revenue by 2030. The certification is significant in that it comes as miniaturization of advanced memory processes such as HBM accelerates, and humidity management had been a relatively underappreciated process variable.

As circuit linewidths shrink and stacking becomes more advanced, yield sensitivity is rising, raising the possibility that equipment demand will grow as well. For Jastech, the certification amounts to securing a bridgehead to expand the global customer base built with its first-generation product to its second-generation product. However, the pace of capital investment by global semiconductor companies and the flow of equipment orders tied to HBM expansion plans are expected to act as variables before JFS translates into actual revenue contributions. As the company's 2030 revenue target of 300 billion won also exceeds the cumulative performance of its first-generation product, the speed at which the second-generation product penetrates the market is likely to be the key factor.

These contributions bring the total accumulated financing for the company to nearly 600 million USD.

The company intends to use these funds to build AI intelligent infrastructure that is directly oriented toward the real world. This effort requires connecting models, software, hardware, and physical execution to move AI from digital spaces into complex physical systems. MegaRobo Technologies submitted a listing application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in June 2025. At that time, the company reported having 1.5 billion RMB in hand orders according to its prospectus. The firm operates two main segments known as industrial intelligence and scientific intelligence to support these goals.

Founder and CEO HUANG Yuqing stated that the company will increase investment in core technology and global business. He noted that AI must move beyond learning from human knowledge to help create new materials and products through continuous feedback. HUANG Yuqing described a contradiction between the growing demand for data from scientists and relatively backward productivity. He believes the company is building the necessary infrastructure to enable this capability to occur on a large scale. The firm plans to strengthen its cooperation in markets across North America, Europe, China, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East.

The company previously shifted from building general robots to creating the MegaRobo Kunpeng Lab as a data factory for life sciences. This platform has evolved from automated execution to an autonomous agent-driven system that uses dry and wet lab brains. It has already delivered infrastructure to more than 500 customers and provided research services for over 200 clients. Recent achievements include advancing 31 drug research pipelines in seven months and launching a protein design challenge with Twist Bioscience and Tencent Cloud. The company now offers both intelligent infrastructure products and AI-Native Research Organization services to accelerate scientific discovery.

stories.Headline: Australian couple Amy and Jarrad launch AI ghost-hunting app GhostTube SEER, topping 1 million Google Play downloads
stories.Summary:
An app called GhostTube SEER, described as the world's first AI ghost-hunting tool, has become a hit in the overseas paranormal investigation community, and its downloads on the Google Play Store have exceeded 1 million. Millions of foreign users hold their phones at midnight waiting for ghosts to appear and pay for memberships for AI-powered ghost hunting. The app was created by an Australian couple, Amy and Jarrad, whose full-time job is shooting paranormal investigation videos. They go to stay overnight wherever is famous for being haunted, and in one episode they went to the Winchester Mystery House in California. The couple has made five ghost-hunting apps one after another, with downloads often exceeding millions.

In the app, a user stands in a haunted house and asks what happened there before, and after a while an image pops up on the screen, such as a woman or an old house. The screen shows the corridor captured by the phone under a dark filter, with a magnetic field indicator said to show magnetic field changes in the house. Free users have a daily limit on how many ghosts they can see, and a membership costs $3.99 per month and $14.99 per year. The couple also sells a head-mounted display called GhostTube Lens, which works like cheap mobile VR headsets by inserting your phone, and buying it in the app comes with a one-year membership. The app's community collects more than 1000 haunted locations around the world, and users post the images they captured in different places to watch and comment on each other.

Jarrad sat in a room in the Winchester Mystery House, opened the app and asked the air to show what happened in that room before. A wooden wall with golden curtains hanging on it first appeared on the screen, looking like an old-fashioned bedroom, then an image of a woman reading a book popped up, then a woman wearing a black shawl, and finally a group of white birds flying up appeared. A long-time follower who has watched all their videos said what gave her the most goosebumps was that the corridors and rooms generated by the app matched the place where the two of them were staying at that time. An old user who claims to be a born medium had his annual fee deducted normally but his account restricted, and he cursed in the comment section and dropped a harsh word, roughly meaning that the spirits had been angered.

The article says the setting that how often ghosts appear depends on whether you pay the money is the most cyber, post-modern and consumerist paranormal setting it has ever seen. The Winchester Mystery House is one of the most famous haunted houses in the United States, and legend says a medium told the hostess that the wronged souls killed by Winchester rifles were haunting her after her husband and daughter passed away one after another. The house was built day and night, expanding from 8 rooms to about 160 rooms, with doors that lead nowhere, stairs that go nowhere, and the number 13 appearing repeatedly in the house. In the paranormal investigation community there is an old method in which one person covers their eyes and wears noise-canceling headphones to isolate the senses of the real world, then another person asks questions beside them and the blindfolded person shouts out whatever they hear.

The article says people once waved radios to scan across channels insisting there were ghost cries in the noise, and once cameras were invented a translucent shadow in a photo was pointed at as that thing. The article says that in ancient times people had Zhong Kui and yellow talismans, which relied on handcraft skills, but later the work became technology-driven. SEER can respond thanks to a small chip called a magnetometer in the phone, which almost every phone has and whose original job is to measure the strength and direction of the surrounding magnetic field so that map apps can know which direction you are facing. The whole process from a ghost being generated to appearing on your screen has three steps: scan the magnetic field, draw a random word, and turn the word into an image.

Wires are buried in the walls, and motors in refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners change their power output all the time when running with electricity, which may affect the nearby magnetic field. Magnetic strips are embedded in the sealing strips of refrigerator doors, and permanent magnets are installed in motors, which still exist even when the device is turned off, while reinforced bars, iron pipes and other iron objects slightly deviate the direction of the earth's magnetic field nearby. After putting on the head-mounted display, a user can choose something to stare at: smoke, flames, a swinging pendulum clock, or full-screen static noise. More to follow.

Dario Amodei said physicists learn new things extremely quickly and contribute fast to machine learning. The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for neural network discoveries. These researchers used concepts like energy functions and statistical physics to develop the Boltzmann Machine. Li Feifei, who studied physics at Princeton, promoted the ImageNet dataset around 2007. Misha Laskin was inspired by the 2016 AlphaGo match while studying physics at the University of Chicago. A domestic Internet company founder specifically interviewed physics candidates for AI roles this year.

Seven researchers left OpenAI in early 2021 to found Anthropic during the epidemic. They met in a backyard while wearing masks and staying six feet apart. Dario Amodei studied at Princeton and Stanford, while Jared Kaplan studied at Stanford and Harvard. Sam McCandlish studied quantum gravity and holographic theory at Stanford before joining OpenAI in 2018. In January 2020, these researchers published the Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models paper.

Anthropic now employs software engineers, machine learning researchers, and experts in ethics, neuroscience, policy, and operations. stories.Headline: US blocks Chinese companies from accessing AI chips through overseas data centers
stories.Summary:
The United States government blocked Chinese companies from accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips through overseas data centers. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security released these export control rules on the 18th. This decision extends controls beyond direct exports to cover indirect routes using chips in foreign centers. The move aims to close a loophole used by Chinese firms to bypass existing restrictions. These measures put Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix on high alert.

Rules apply to data centers providing AI services exceeding 12 million total processing performance to China and other controlled countries. Supplying advanced chips to these centers now requires U.S. government approval. Existing providers must obtain a license within 90 days of the rules taking effect. Licensing was tightened for exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. The U.S. found Chinese companies placed data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere to avoid restrictions.

The Bureau of Industry and Security is responsible for these new export control rules. The U.S. government stated that Chinese companies were avoiding restrictions by using overseas data centers. Officials narrowed the avenues for Chinese-affiliated chip designers to prove their products are not subject to controls. The government now requires overseas contract manufacturers and packaging firms to verify the location of design companies. They must also verify the ultimate parent companies when producing advanced chips.

Samsung Electronics may see orders shrink in its foundry business due to more demanding verification procedures. SK hynix faces risks of weaker demand for high-bandwidth memory supplied to Nvidia. Both companies worry that reduced GPU installations at overseas data centers will contract Chinese demand. The industry estimates that GPUs accessed by China through indirect routes account for 20 percent of global usage. These measures could increase the time and money needed to deal with Chinese-affiliated customers.

The Federal Reserve released a financial stability report on the 13th warning about AI data center investment risks. New debt for advanced computing infrastructure exceeded 680 billion dollars from January through October this year. This exceeds the 130 billion dollars raised during all of 2023. Risk exposure at large U.S. banks for technology companies and data center developers is about 1 trillion dollars. Seven large technology companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Oracle, owe over 3 trillion dollars in obligations.

Future purchases of GPUs and server DRAM could decline if data center operators scale back investment. This may weigh on the pricing power and profitability of Samsung and SK hynix. Samsung stated last month that its entire 2027 high-bandwidth memory supply was already sold. SK hynix has secured substantial volumes through long-term supply contracts with major customers. It remains open whether a rapid market downturn could lead buyers to forfeit advance payments.

stories.Headline: UNIST and Korea University researchers develop Q-Edge-popup to find smaller, noise-resistant quantum AI circuits
stories.Summary:
Researchers developed a technique to identify essential regions of complex quantum artificial intelligence circuits on November 18, 2026. This method cuts computational load and noise induced errors at the same time. A team led by Professor Yoon Sung-hwan of UNIST developed the process. They worked with a team led by Professor Kim Joong-heon of Korea University. The researchers mathematically proved that high performing small circuits exist inside large quantum neural networks.

The team created an algorithm called Q-Edge-popup to find these circuits in practice. They established a quantum strong lottery ticket hypothesis to account for the characteristics of quantum computation. The findings were presented at the CIKM 2026 conference in Rome from November 7 to 11. The research used a quantum neural network made of 3,840 rotation gates for simulation. This process requires sufficient quantum gates and specific initial settings to produce results close to target outputs.

First author Kwon Hong-gyun said high performing small circuits are likely to exist when specific conditions are met. He noted that these circuits do not exist in every single quantum circuit. Professor Yoon stated the key is searching for circuits that cut gate numbers while maintaining performance. He added that this work helps develop quantum AI models combining efficiency with stability. The research received support from the National Research Foundation of Korea and the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation.

The study affected the way researchers approach the slimming of quantum neural network models. In conventional AI, the strong lottery ticket hypothesis allows for slimming without changing weights. This theory could not be applied directly to quantum networks because gate order and measurement affect outcomes. The new algorithm scores each gate based on task performance to build a small circuit. Performance is then pushed higher by fine tuning only the parameters of the remaining gates.

The researchers confirmed the slimming effect through a computer simulation involving handwritten digit image classification. Keeping half of the gates produced a classification accuracy of 75.2 percent without changing any parameters. Training the selected gates raised accuracy to 79.4 percent, which approached the 81.3 percent of the full circuit. In mixed noise environments, the full circuit accuracy plunged 71.3 percentage points from 81.3 percent down to 10.0 percent. A circuit with 25 percent of gates held accuracy at 74.7 percent, down only 1.5 points from 76.2 percent.

The next step involves using these findings to create more stable and efficient quantum AI models. The Q-Edge-popup algorithm allows for the practical location of these high performing small circuits. The researchers proved that keeping a subset of gates with fixed parameters can maintain high accuracy. The articles do not state when these circuits will be used in real hardware. They also leave open how this technique will scale to even larger quantum neural networks.

Moritz charges corporate clients fees that are 80 to 90 percent lower than established firms. Athena reduced a 20 hour complex case to two hours and 40 hour reviews to 40 minutes. Inside Practice notes that these firms use per-document rates, subscriptions, performance-based pricing, and flat fees. Norm AI raised 120 million dollars in a Series C round at a 1.2 billion dollar valuation. Norm Law is the firm associated with the parent company Norm AI.

Pamir Esas, the chief executive of Moritz, discussed the lower fees the firm charges its clients. Richard Ferris, a co-founder of Covenant, stated that every law firm will be AI-native in five years. Mike Schmidtberger joined Norm Law this year as a partner and chairman. He previously served as the executive committee chairman at the global firm Sidley Austin. These leaders emphasize efficiency gains and the shift away from traditional hourly billing.

Citigroup and Morgan Stanley are pressing large law firms to reduce fees due to AI efficiency. Junior associates are affected as their work is displaced and hiring for them is shrinking. A Citibank survey found 47 percent of firms saw summer internship hiring fall from last year. Another 49 percent of firms expect next summer's internship hiring to fall further. These changes put pressure on established firms to cut their own rates.

The AI Firm Index showed 60 AI-native firms worldwide as of September, doubling the previous six months. More than half of these firms are in the United States, Britain, Australia, and Germany. Crunchbase reported that legal-tech investment reached a record 4.586 billion dollars last year. GCVC is a venture fund for legal AI startups launched by current and former in-house counsel. Traditional firms rely on junior associates to prepare documents for senior lawyer sign-off.

Investment in legal-technology startups continues to increase as the use of AI widens in the field. AI agents now produce work products first, which lawyers then verify and review afterward. The industry is moving away from the unwritten rule of billing clients for hourly work. The articles do not state how traditional firms will respond to the pressure to lower fees.
