stories.Headline: Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 matches 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost
stories.Summary:
Microsoft unveiled a new lineup of specialized AI models at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, making a direct run at Anthropic and OpenAI in coding, cybersecurity and image generation. The company pitched models trained to do particular jobs at substantially lower cost instead of one chatbot that beats everyone at everything. The biggest claim involves MAI Code 2, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance on common enterprise coding tasks for just 5% of the cost. Microsoft also claims 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price. OpenAI also released GPT-6.2 on Tuesday, so Microsoft's Sol comparison already concerns an older generation.

Those figures average results from four evaluations focused on practical software development, including fixing code and completing multi-file changes. Microsoft ran three of the tests on its own evaluation platform, used outside results for the fourth, and calculated MAI Code 2's costs using a 50% promotional discount. A lighter Code 2 Flash model targets routine fixes and quick edits, with Microsoft claiming performance comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5 at 20% of the price. Microsoft says MAI Cyber 2 Flash succeeded on 92.3% of CyberGym-E2E's evaluated vulnerability-discovery tasks, compared with 91.5% for GPT-6 Astra, at less than 2% of the cost per task. Microsoft excluded 92 of 905 tasks after identifying overlap between their source material and its training data.

Microsoft has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Its security system will begin replacing an older MAI model for eligible MDASH customers in mid-December, building on the vulnerability-scanning approach Decrypt previously covered. Microsoft's own documentation says Code 2 is not yet optimized for fundamental scientific research or very long-running autonomous assignments. Microsoft quotes about $35 per 1,000 images for MAI Image 2.7 and $10 for its Flash version, versus roughly $211 for GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst at maximum quality in Artificial Analysis's comparison. Microsoft is also offering selected business customers the ability to customize and run its models' licensed weights inside Azure, reducing reliance on outside vendors without making the technology open source.

On Artificial Analysis's image-editing test, which asks people to choose between anonymously generated edits and turns those preferences into an Elo rating, MAI Image 2.7 currently leads with 1,215 points against GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst's 1,211. The four-point gap is small enough that their reported uncertainty ranges overlap, and the separate text-to-image generation ranking puts Microsoft in fourth place. Google's Nano Banana 2.1 is about $34 per 1,000 images there, while Nano Banana Pro is about $134, and actual bills depend on the provider, resolution and settings. Both coding models are already in GitHub Copilot, putting Microsoft's in-house technology directly into a product that has relied heavily on outside AI suppliers. Microsoft also announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash and which can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, and track decisions and extract useful information from Teams.

Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023 and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property. Anthropic competes in the cheaper end of the market with Haiku, not just its premium Opus models, so Microsoft is entering a race its rivals already understand. OpenAI has taken a related approach with its Mini and Nano models, letting cheaper workers handle routine tasks while larger systems tackle the exceptions. Our earlier testing of MAI Image 2 found excellent realism but frustrating limits on editing and output formats, and the newer release adds interactive editing through Microsoft's Canvas workspace, transparent backgrounds and broader access through Foundry. Microsoft says the numbers it is reporting use a 50% introductory discount, and the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided.

For the next test of its specialist strategy, Code 2 is already available in GitHub Copilot, and the Cyber 2 Flash rollout is scheduled to start in mid-December. Microsoft is touting that it is integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 and Fabric. The company has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests, and benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads.

stories.Headline: Microsoft AI launches MAI Image 2.7 editing models near top of leaderboards
stories.Summary:
Microsoft AI launched two MAI Image 2.7 models built for image editing on October 27, 2026, as a preview, and the pair arrived near the top of the industry scoreboards. The launch post describes the models as ranking among the best image-editing systems available, at lower prices, and the release has one job, which is improving pictures that already exist rather than generating new ones from text prompts. On Artificial Analysis's AA-Image-Editing v2.1 leaderboard, MAI Image 2.7 scored 1,193 Elo, which places it at second directly behind OpenAI's GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, which leads with 1,199 Elo. The model also landed at third on Arena Edit, another editing leaderboard, and that result pushed Microsoft AI to the second spot overall among labs in that ranking.

The upgrade over MAI Image 2.6, which shipped in August 2026, is broad, and according to the Artificial Analysis tracking the new model improved across all ten use cases and all seven editing actions the platform measures. On the main AA leaderboard, the score for MAI Image 2.7 is a 42-point gain over its predecessor, and two specific categories saw especially big jumps. Composition and framing improved by 57 Elo, which covers how well the model arranges subjects within an image, and text edits rose by 49 Elo. The model tops or leads in several categories, including scene and style editing, text and symbol edits, reasoning-based edits, and enhancement and restoration.

MAI Image 2.7 is currently available through MAI Playground, Arena and Artificial Analysis, which are mostly testing and comparison venues rather than production pipelines. Specific details on API access and pricing have not been disclosed, and that creates a slight tension with the lower-price framing in the launch post, since businesses cannot yet put the cost claim to work in their own budgets. The release is the latest step in a fast cadence, with Microsoft AI releasing MAI Image 2 in March 2026, followed by MAI Image 2.6 in August 2026, and now 2.7 in October. That makes three image model releases in roughly seven months.

stories.Headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent as US ad revenue growth reaches 31%
stories.Summary:
Baron Capital released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter for the Baron Durable Advantage Fund, and in it the firm reported that Meta Platforms contributed 1.30% to the fund's returns during that quarter, with Meta shares rising 28.8% over the period. The letter said Meta's second-quarter results showed the core advertising engine getting stronger, with U.S. advertising revenue growth accelerating to 31% as new AI ranking and recommendation models lifted conversions. It also noted that Advantage+, Meta's AI-driven advertising suite, passed $75 billion in annual revenue run-rate. Meta closed at $626.41 per share on November 16, 2026, with a market capitalization of $1.60 trillion, and the stock had pulled back 9.77% over the past month while remaining up 4.81% over the last 52 weeks.

The letter described a bigger catalyst in September with the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, which reached number one on the U.S. App Store within days. At its Meta Connect conference, the company introduced real-time voice, a Mac app with computer use, and commerce partners including Stripe, Shopify, PayPal, Walmart and Best Buy, so that Muse can complete purchases. Meta also brought Muse to its smart glasses and to Charm, a new handheld device. The fund said these moves strengthened Meta's positioning and added new potential avenues for monetization while improving its contextual understanding of users, which should further advance its ability to match the right ad to the right user at the right time.

Baron said it believes current earnings understate Meta's earnings power because the company invests ahead of revenue, and it retains strong conviction that Meta's data, compute, distribution and founder leadership will make it a leader in consumer AI. The firm also said it believes AI will remain a tailwind for Meta's core business, helping the company sustain a long duration of growth. The fund returned 2.2% in the quarter, in line with the S&P 500's 2.3%, and is up 5.7% year to date, trailing the index's 12.8%. The letter cited the Federal Reserve raising interest rates, the 10-year Treasury yield reaching its highest since 2002, Middle East developments, inflation, and the AI build-out and AI bubble debate as influences on market volatility.

stories.Headline: Microsoft releases Windows endpoint security platform and previews baseline protection
stories.Summary:
Microsoft released its Windows endpoint security platform to general availability on Windows 11, the company said in a blog post dated November 17, 2026. Dana Huang, corporate vice president of Windows Security, wrote the post about Windows security at Ignite 2026. The post said the release marks a milestone in Microsoft's work with the security ecosystem. That work aims to reduce reliance on kernel drivers while preserving the capabilities security solutions depend on. Microsoft also said Windows baseline protection is now available in preview.

Baseline protection brings secure boot, virtualization-based security and memory integrity together into a single, versioned security state. It will appear in an updated Windows Settings experience, the post said. Windows is expanding post-quantum protection in the Windows TLS stack, including pure post-quantum key exchange and authentication. Microsoft Execution Containers, announced last month, provide governed boundaries for agent execution. Microsoft is extending Intune and Windows Autopatch to eligible Windows Server scenarios, in preview.

Huang said AI is changing the threat landscape as fast as it is changing the way we work. She said attackers are using AI to find vulnerabilities, build exploits and scale campaigns faster than ever. She said the time between a weakness being discovered and being used against an organization is shrinking. She said devices configured securely and patched quickly remain one of the most effective defenses. She said the security strategy for users and data must now extend to AI and agents as well.

The post thanked the partners who joined Microsoft on the endpoint security platform journey. It said the investments extend work shared at Build 2026. It said the investments help organizations establish a known and measurable security state and prepare for emerging threats. It said Windows Hello improvements make passwordless sign-in more consistent and get users to their desktop faster.

It said new observability gives IT greater insight into whether users authenticate using biometrics or PIN. The post said Microsoft shared last year how Windows was working with security partners to evolve the platform. It said that work aimed to better integrate with the ecosystem while remaining resilient. It cited the Driver Quality Initiative and broader work to reduce kernel exposure and strengthen recovery.

It said these investments help make Windows more resilient by design. It said baseline protection will continue to evolve as more security capabilities are added. The post listed sessions for Ignite, including BRK405 on what's new in Windows security. It also listed BRK398 on building a more resilient Windows estate and BRK392 on preparing apps for evolving Windows security standards.

It pointed readers to the Windows Security Guide and Microsoft Learn for practical guidance. It said customers can explore the story through sessions spanning a more secure-by-default Windows and governed AI agents. It did not give a date for general availability beyond the post date. More to follow.

stories.Headline: UBS analyst Karl Keirstead starts Meta coverage with a Buy rating and $815 target
stories.Summary:
UBS analyst Karl Keirstead assumed coverage of Meta Platforms on November 17, 2026, with a Buy rating and an $815 price target that implies roughly 30% upside from the stock's Monday close. He argued that enthusiasm around Meta's Muse AI models and Meta Business Agents could offset investor worries about rising spending and financing needs. Keirstead said Meta trades at about 20 times estimated 2027 GAAP earnings per share, a valuation he called attractive given recent progress in AI models and applications. He described CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Meta's leadership as building what he called an AI maximalist version of Meta after a significant overhaul of its AI strategy over the past 18 months.

Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, helped by a 10% increase in advertising impressions and a 14% rise in average advertising prices. Capital expenditures in the quarter reached $34.91 billion, and quarterly free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. The company expects fiscal 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, narrowing its earlier forecast of $130 billion to $145 billion. Management said it expects to keep investing aggressively in its core business and emerging AI initiatives in 2027, though it has not given a full-year revenue forecast.

Keirstead said UBS would focus mainly on the development and training of the Muse AI models, the rollout of Meta's personal AI agent and the expansion of business and enterprise applications. The firm will also examine the computing infrastructure needed to support these efforts, including its scale and associated costs. UBS said its coverage of cloud infrastructure providers, including Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Oracle and CoreWeave, would inform its analysis of Meta's AI investments. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained bearish on November 17, and Meta shares have fallen nearly 4% so far this year, while the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF has risen over 2% in the same period.

stories.Headline: Meta expands content protection to Instagram and adds spoken word matching to detect AI copies
stories.Summary:
Meta is expanding its content protection feature from Facebook to Instagram in an effort to reduce unauthorized copying of creators' original Reels through reposting and AI generation, according to the company's announcement. The tool automatically looks out for visual matches to creators' original videos and sends a notification when a match is found across Instagram and Facebook. Creators who receive a match have four options, which are to keep monitoring the post, make the post no longer viewable to other users, add an "original by" label linking viewers back to the creator's initial video, or allow the video to stay up. Meta said it has heard growing concern about AI-generated content that uses elements of original work but may not visually match it, and it is starting to show videos in content protection that match the spoken words in an original video even when the visuals have been replaced by AI.

To become eligible for content protection, creators must meet Meta's originality and integrity requirements, the articles state. Meta initially launched content protection on Facebook in November 2025, and since then it has altered its recommendation algorithms across Facebook and Instagram feeds to prioritize original content. In March 2026, Meta updated its content guidelines, further defining original content as a post filmed or created by the publisher or production company, as new episodes, clips or trailers of a show posted by the producers, talent or network, or as an enhanced version of something previously posted. By expanding rights protections to Instagram and unauthorized AI-generated duplication, Meta is trying to give creators more ownership over their videos while cutting out more replicated, reused content a user might see in their feed.

Meta is responsible for the feature and described its purpose in its announcement, saying the company knows how frustrating it can be to see aggregators benefit from creators' work. The company said the tool automatically looks out for visual matches and notifies creators when a match appears across Instagram and Facebook. Meta also said it is beginning to incorporate relevant additions to the detection process, including matching spoken words even when visuals have been replaced by AI. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the expansion and the detection additions.

stories.Headline: BNY Mellon and Microsoft use AI agents to negotiate a Treasury trade
stories.Summary:
Bank of New York Mellon Corp. and Microsoft Corp. used artificial intelligence agents to negotiate a US Treasury trade on November 17, 2026. These automated systems haggled over a price independently before human employees provided the final approval for the transaction. This event is billed by both companies as the first trade of its kind involving AI agents. The process demonstrated that computers can now deliberate and search for middle ground during financial negotiations.

The trade required Microsoft's treasury department to provide an agent with specific boundaries for a satisfactory transaction. BNY implemented a control layer to ensure authorized agents negotiated while maintaining an overlay for mutual confirmation of terms. This system, called the Agentic Negotiation Protocol, allows agents to interact within strict guardrails defined by the bank. BNY intends to expand this technology into other capital market areas such as foreign-exchange payments and repo deals. They also plan to apply these automated workflows to collateral terms and various contractual negotiations.

Laide Majiyagbe, the global head of markets at BNY, stated that this represents the start of an important evolution in the market. She explained that while high-touch human brokerage will not disappear, AI can fill the space between electronic trading and human negotiation. Majiyagbe believes this technology could lower the barrier to entry for players who previously found human capital investments impractical. She noted that the agents currently engage in a level of polite discourse rarely seen on Wall Street desks.

This proof of concept shows that AI can move beyond simple algorithmic trading into the complex art of client grappling. Trading desks already use AI to parse unstructured data and adjust pricing, but this trade marks a shift toward autonomous deliberation. The industry must now determine if these agents can be scaled across different asset classes during treacherous market conditions. Future tests will focus on whether these automated lieutenants can maintain fairness and efficiency in more volatile environments.

stories.Headline: Credo beats estimates for an eighth quarter as analysts set a $204 target
stories.Summary:
Vandita Jadeja wrote about Credo Technology on November 17, 2026, while other reports focused on Nvidia and Anthropic during the same week. Investors tracked Nvidia's fiscal third quarter results on Tuesday and the proposed initial public offering for Anthropic on Wednesday. Anthropic shares were expected to begin trading on Thursday, while the Federal Reserve released October meeting minutes on Wednesday. Retail sales data and a speech by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also occurred during this crucial period. These events influenced sentiment across American stock markets as investors monitored the sustainability of massive artificial intelligence infrastructure investments.

Credo Technology, trading at 141.41 dollars, has a 24/7 Wall St. price target of 204.20 dollars and a buy rating. The company reported first quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of 479 million dollars, which was an increase of 114.7 percent year over year. Non-GAAP earnings per share reached 1.20 dollars, exceeding the consensus of 1.17 dollars, while stock-based compensation reached 87.98 million dollars. Anthropic proposed an IPO priced between 70 and 78 dollars per share to raise 64.4 billion dollars by selling 825 million shares. Nvidia's valuation fell from 5.8 trillion dollars in early October to 3.9 trillion dollars as of Friday, November 14, 2026.

Management at Credo expects total growth above 85 percent and optical revenue exceeding 600 million dollars in fiscal 2027. They guided second quarter revenue to between 525 million and 535 million dollars and a non-GAAP net margin near 50 percent. The company stated that GAAP gross margin guidance of 62.9 to 64.9 percent trails non-GAAP ranges due to non-cash acquisition amortization. LSEG analysts expect Nvidia to report revenue of approximately 109 billion dollars and earnings growth of around 90 percent. These figures help investors determine if massive spending on AI infrastructure is translating into sustained demand for advanced chips.

Nineteen of twenty analysts rate Credo as a buy or strong buy, with a consensus target of 284.05 dollars. The bull case for the stock reaches 332.77 dollars, while the bear case is lower at 166.29 dollars. Investors are concerned that four customers generated 33, 28, 13, and 10 percent of Credo's quarterly revenue, creating high concentration risk. Other affected companies include Broadcom, whose AI semiconductor revenue rose 221 percent, and Marvell Technology, which overlaps in optical interconnects. Astera Labs is the closest pure-play rival to Credo, selling retimers and cable modules to hyperscalers at a 184 P/E.

Credo's stock fell 32.3 percent in one month and 5.5 percent year to date, dropping 54 percent below its 52-week high. The company's first PIC revenue came from a photonics deal, and its non-GAAP gross margin of 68 percent beats Marvell's. Nvidia shares faced pressure recently due to controversies surrounding chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang, impacting the company's overall market capitalization. Anthropic developed the Claude chatbot and could reach a fully diluted valuation of 1.4 trillion dollars at its upper IPO range. Broadcom and Marvell also compete in the AI networking and connectivity layers that support GPU clusters.

Credo will release second quarter results in early December, which may confirm optical growth and the addition of new customers. The OmniConnect launch starting in fiscal 2028 could add thousands of dollars of content per GPU to the company's revenue. 24/7 Wall St. provides price targets for Credo reaching 213.51 dollars in 2027, 248.86 dollars in 2028, and 353.81 dollars by 2030. The articles leave open whether hyperscaler spending changes will move results above or below the current strategic execution path. It remains uncertain if enormous capital expenditures by technology companies on AI infrastructure can generate sufficient returns for investors.

stories.Headline: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, pitching cost per task over raw benchmarks
stories.Summary:
Microsoft AI announced two enterprise coding models, MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, on November 17, 2026, positioning them on cost per task rather than raw benchmark superiority over rival models. MAI Code 2 is aimed at production changes, deep debugging, multi-file implementation, repository-wide reasoning and user interfaces, while the Flash variant targets high-volume jobs such as explaining code, making targeted edits, applying routine fixes and iterating quickly. Microsoft reports that MAI Code 2 delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of its cost and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance at 5% of its cost across four benchmarks. The company states explicitly that neither model has yet been tuned for fundamental science research or very long-horizon agentic work, which defines the release's scope around everyday coding work. Across DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE Atlas and FrontierCode v1.1, Microsoft reports a 63.2% average pass rate and $0.309 average cost per task for MAI Code 2, against 64.1% at $0.761 for GPT-6.1 Sol and 65.3% at $6.306 for Claude Opus 5.5.

All models in the coding comparisons ran at maximum reasoning effort, the cost figures for Microsoft's models use a 50% promotional price, and the company cautions that changing the workload, model configuration, reasoning effort or pricing assumptions can change the comparisons. For MAI Code 2 Flash, Microsoft reports a 61.0% average pass rate and $0.052 average cost per task across DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE Atlas, compared with 55.1% at $0.080 for GPT-6 Luna and 53.9% at $0.319 for Claude Haiku 5.5. In separate blind frontend evaluations covering user interfaces, games, data visualizations, 3D scenes and SVG graphics, Microsoft reports that 258 annotators preferred MAI Code 2 over GPT-6 Sol 67% of the time on aesthetics and functionality. Both models are available in GitHub Copilot, and MAI Code 2 Flash is also in limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry, with releases planned for OpenRouter, Vercel, Hermes, OpenCode and Kilo. Microsoft has further optimized Code 2 Flash into MAI Work Flash for use across Microsoft 365 and Fabric IQ, reporting comparable accuracy and token efficiency with GPT-6 Luna on internal Excel customer-scenario benchmarks and similar quality and token efficiency on frequent PowerPoint tasks.

In Teams evaluations, Microsoft reports higher scores than GPT-6 Luna for decision tracking and knowledge gaps, adapting custom instructions and tool calling, with up to 28% fewer tokens on instruction following and tool calling. For Power BI semantic models, Microsoft reports a 0.77 overall score for MAI Work Flash in offline DAX query-generation evaluations, compared with 0.54 for GPT-6 Astra, 0.45 for GPT-5.6 Sol and 0.30 for Opus 5.5. The release is therefore also a distribution release, since Copilot gets two coding options while a Flash derivative moves into spreadsheets, presentations, chat and analytics. The reported numbers make cost per task the main competitive lever, with promotional pricing and the deliberately narrow workload focus determining how far the comparisons extend. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned releases on OpenRouter, Vercel, Hermes, OpenCode and Kilo and the limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry.

stories.Headline: Dale Gillham warns investors against buying the AI narrative as Nvidia shares fall 18 percent this year
stories.Summary:
Nvidia’s recent quarterly results beat market expectations, yet the company’s shares have fallen about 18 percent for the year, according to a Ticker News report published on 17 November 2026. The decline reflects a broader trend in the technology sector, which has been one of the worst performers on the S&P 500 this year. Dale Gillham of Wealth Within said investors should focus on the future value of companies like Nvidia rather than their current valuations. He argued that the market prices in future potential rather than present value, and he warned against buying on the AI narrative alone. Gillham noted that Apple and Microsoft have also performed poorly this year, while sectors such as pharmaceuticals and energy have posted substantial gains.

He compared the current AI enthusiasm to the lithium market, where hype did not match reality and prices fell despite increased battery use. He also said many big tech companies are spending more on AI than they earn, and he asked whether revenue is coming in fast enough to validate that spending. Security concerns are adding pressure, with some businesses, including the Commonwealth Bank, moving toward internal AI solutions to reduce hacking risks. Gillham advised investors to focus on established businesses with a track record of profitability and to weigh broader economic trends rather than the AI story.

He said the market prices future potential, not present value, and he urged a strategic approach that evaluates individual companies and market dynamics. The report does not say what Nvidia or its executives said in response, and it gives no further dates or figures beyond those above. It also does not say what happens next for the company or its shares. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Replit extends its platform with Microsoft technology for enterprise apps and agents
stories.Summary:
On 17 November 2026 Microsoft published a customer story saying Replit is extending its platform with Microsoft technology to help enterprise teams build applications, connect to governed business data and bring agents into everyday workflows. Replit is building the foundation for self-driving companies, in which people set goals and exercise judgment while agents carry more of the execution work. Replit's Horacio Lopez, Solutions Partner Program Lead, built a partner portal himself using Replit. The portal ran on Microsoft Azure and was connected to the company's customer relationship management system, along with a Solutions Partner directory and application process. Replit President Michele Catasta said AI is fundamentally changing who is becoming capable of creating software.

Replit adapted its architecture to support containerized applications and virtual machine workloads on Azure, with compute, storage and platform services that scale with an application. Identity, networking and organization-managed security capabilities help applications operate within an enterprise environment. Microsoft Foundry supports model orchestration, multi-agent workflows and AI inference, depending on the application's requirements. Using the Rayfin software development kit, Replit lets builders create applications around governed data in Microsoft Fabric without first moving the underlying business records into another data store. Replit uses information about the data's structure plus company-owned semantic metadata to help generate the application, while the SDK provides back-end scaffolding such as data models, authentication and access policies.

Catasta said that as Replit moved further into the enterprise, customers asked for more choice and control on where their applications are running and how they are running. He said Replit expanded to Azure to meet the needs of its enterprise customers while keeping the Replit experience at the center. Luis Héctor Chávez, Chief Technology Officer of Replit, said that for Replit to deploy to customers' cloud it had to essentially do a rearchitecture and rethink how it deploys software. Chávez said Replit's most security-conscious customers need their governed data to never escape Fabric. Lopez said work that might have taken months of an engineer's time took him just a few afternoon sessions, a tenfold to hundredfold shift in the time it takes to turn an idea into something useful.

Chávez described the opportunity as a zero-to-one shift, going beyond building software faster so that more people who understand a problem can begin solving it themselves. Replit's partnerships team had relied on a patchwork of tools that didn't fit the needs of the team or its partners. The team wanted a portal where partners could interact with Replit and track the deals they had referred. Lopez understood the partner experience, the sales process and what the portal needed to do, and he set the direction and evaluated the results, working with colleagues to refine what partners could see and do.

Replit is extending its accessible creation experience to applications while the data remains connected to the organization's Fabric environment. The story lists Replit as the customer, with Azure, Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Fabric as the products, and gives its organization size as 50-999 employees. It gives the country or region as the United States, the business need as AI and Agents, and the industry as Software, Data and Platforms. Replit helps enterprises become self-driving companies, enabling teams to set goals and exercise judgment while agents carry more of the execution work.

Replit is extending that opportunity beyond the first build, connecting its creation experience with the infrastructure, AI capabilities and governed data that applications need in enterprise production. Replit is making it easier not only to create software but to put it to work inside an enterprise through agents, with team oversight. Replit is extending its platform with Microsoft technology to help teams build applications, connect to governed business data and bring agents into everyday workflows. Replit is making it easier not only to create software but to put it to work inside an enterprise through agents, with team oversight.

The story says Replit is extending that opportunity beyond the first build, connecting its accessible creation experience with the infrastructure, AI capabilities and governed data that applications need in enterprise production. It says Replit is building the foundation for self-driving companies, where people define goals, exercise judgment and remain accountable while agents take on more execution and coordination. The story does not give a date for when the Azure, Foundry or Fabric capabilities become available, nor terms, pricing or named enterprise customers. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia shares rise 4% after record revenue exceeds Wall Street expectations
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares rose 4 percent after the company reported record fiscal Q3 2027 results on November 17, 2026. The company reported that demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains exceptionally strong. Revenue reached a record 115.8 billion dollars, which increased more than 103 percent year over year. This total exceeded the consensus estimate of 109.33 billion dollars from Wall Street analysts. Net income hit a record high of approximately 65.3 billion dollars.

The Data Center segment earned 107.6 billion dollars, while Hyperscale revenue reached 60.1 billion dollars. AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise revenue was 47.5 billion dollars, and Edge Computing reached 8.2 billion dollars. Adjusted earnings per share were 2.68 dollars, and the adjusted gross margin was 74.9 percent. Fourth quarter revenue guidance is 130 billion dollars, with operating expenses estimated at 10.7 billion dollars. A 0.25 dollar dividend will be paid on December 23, 2026, to shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

Board chair Harvey Jones stated the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Jones said the board is proactively dealing with immediate consequences and enhancing oversight capacity for shareholders. He declined to answer questions about the circumstances of Huang's resignation and the ongoing investigation. Jones noted a new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will facilitate communication with US officials. The company stated it intends to use 227.3 billion dollars for share repurchases through fiscal 2028.

Investors are focusing on the sustainability of profit margins and risks regarding advanced processor exports to China. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, possibly focusing on shareholder communications rather than financial reporting. Some analysts worry that a modest slowdown in order growth could trigger a substantial market reaction. The company is also facing leadership uncertainty following the departure of its longtime leader, Jensen Huang. Customers beyond the largest cloud providers are now playing an increasingly important role in infrastructure deployment.

The company generated 43.8 billion dollars in free cash flow and returned 28.1 billion dollars to shareholders. Purchase commitments for memory components rose to 390 billion dollars from 279 billion dollars in one quarter. Commitments for cloud service agreements and data center leases increased from 74 billion dollars to 102 billion dollars. Maximum exposure under partner guarantees rose to 118 billion dollars, including 105 billion dollars for SB Energy. Nvidia also disclosed 20 billion dollars in equity investment commitments for AI laboratories and infrastructure partners.

Nvidia will continue its share repurchases, which could more than double on average during the current quarter. The company will manage its 4.25 GW campus in Ohio for OpenAI under 20 year lease agreements. Management did not include Data Center computing chip sales to China in its future revenue forecasts. The articles leave open the full scope of the SEC investigation and the outcome of that probe. It remains unclear if the new leadership team can maintain the company's technology strategy and customer relationships.

stories.Headline: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman says the industry must be extremely careful as models improve other models
stories.Summary:
Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's CEO of AI, said in a Yahoo Finance video interview published on November 17, 2026, that the AI industry still needs to be extremely careful as models increasingly improve other models. He described that capability, known as recursive self-improvement, as dangerous and said he is really nervous about it, noting that Microsoft uses models across its fleet to check for bugs, produce training data and create evaluations. He called the past three months a watershed moment and said people in the industry are not being alarmist, because the situation is very serious. He said proceeding step by step, proving models can be safe before putting them into production, is a rational strategy given how powerful they are.

Suleyman said the obligation falls on Microsoft as both a provider of models and a developer of its own models to ensure guard rails exist, behaviors are aligned and security flaws are addressed, which may mean going slower in order to go faster. Asked whether Anthropic and OpenAI are taking the same approach, he said he believes they are also committed to pacing the frontier, though the industry still has to work out what that means in practice. He said this has been working its way through the system over the last four to six weeks and will mean going slower when the time is right, with labs coordinating to share safety best practices and disclose new types of vulnerabilities found in the alignment process. He said he is completely committed to that approach and that it is why he got into the industry.

Suleyman said Microsoft has not had to hit the brakes on anything on its side so far, but that deploying powerful cyber models requires rigorous testing, which he compared to a wind tunnel that puts a model under all sorts of pressure. He said that to produce a model at the frontier on cyber at 2% of the cost, the company has to test it very rigorously, and that such testing reveals remarkable capabilities, including models finding vulnerabilities in things humans have not found for years or even decades. He said Microsoft therefore has to be very strict about how it deploys those things. The interview followed recent hacks and AI-led cyberattacks, which the article cites as context for the industry's caution.

stories.Headline: Nvidia reports record revenue while board refuses to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported its third quarter financial results on November 18, 2026, showing a significant revenue beat. The company achieved this growth in its first earnings report since the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang. Investors hoped for strong numbers, and the company delivered a total revenue of almost 116 billion dollars. However, the board of directors refused to reinstate Jensen Huang as the chief executive officer. This decision occurred while the company continues to navigate leadership changes and government scrutiny.

The third quarter revenue reached 115.8 billion dollars, which is a 103 percent increase from the previous year. Data center revenue was 107.6 billion dollars, and the GAAP gross margin stood at 74.8 percent. Nvidia guided fourth quarter revenue to 130 billion dollars, assuming no data center compute revenue from China. The cloud backlog grew to 2.5 trillion dollars, and the Vera Rubin platform earned almost 20 billion dollars. The company sold 2.4 billion dollars of older Hopper chips to China before stopping those sales.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that the company's momentum is real and raised next year's growth outlook to 75 percent. Board chairman Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as the chief executive. Jensen Huang stated he would be honored to return to his role in his first public statement since resigning. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded answers within ten days regarding whether illicit sales were used to boost earnings. Commerce Secretary Lutnick has supported chip sales to China, while other officials like Marco Rubio remain hawks.

Over 188,000 people signed an open letter supporting the return of Jensen Huang to the company. Some employees warned the board that the current situation could lead to the loss of irreplaceable talent. The Federal Reserve noted that the largest banks have nearly 1 trillion dollars of exposure to AI build. About 87 percent of the Fed's market contacts now cite AI as a top financial risk. Investors are concerned about the long term future of the company without its visionary founder at the helm.

Nvidia booked 104 billion dollars through its Singapore unit last year, which represents almost half of the company's total revenue. Jensen Huang's daughter and son-in-law were involved in the company's relationship with the firm known as Megaspeed. The SEC is conducting a civil investigation into whether the company's disclosures misled investors during the CEO's departure. A Justice Department criminal investigation is now leading the probe into Megaspeed, which began back in 2024. President Trump may hold as much as 62 million dollars in Nvidia stock while managing cabinet disputes.

The board is searching for a permanent CEO both inside and outside the company as quickly as possible. A new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee was established to manage the company's regulatory challenges. New rules requiring licenses for top chips in Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore take effect in 90 days. Anthropic is preparing to price its IPO on Wednesday, with expectations that the pricing will be higher. The articles leave open whether the board will eventually resolve the backlog of legal and government policy issues.

stories.Headline: Microsoft announces Copilot Workspaces and Autopilot agents at Ignite
stories.Summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces during the keynote for the company's Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, describing it as a collaborative multiplayer surface for Copilot's agentic capabilities. The product, which Microsoft calls the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, is where people and agents build on each other's work, with an agent drafting a section of a document and a person reviewing it. Microsoft said that when a user leaves a comment, an agent picks it up, and the feature is available in Frontier for now. The company also announced Autopilot, a counterpoint agent to Copilot that can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project without waiting for a prompt.

Microsoft said Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses, and that each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager, so IT can block it as needed. The company added that its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, giving security teams a clear audit trail, and that employees will soon be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces. Nadella also announced a command center called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and Teams threads, currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app. Microsoft also said Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a single starting point, similar to Anthropic's recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings.

Microsoft announced Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management to help companies track spending on AI, with Business Analytics in Frontier Public today providing insights on what a company is spending on AI, why, and where it is paying off. In a keynote demo, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents' costs have spiked and which human employee to notify as a result. Microsoft said the tool measures investment in work completed rather than simply tokens, analyzing tasks, how long the work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed. Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model, and leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available.

stories.Headline: OpenAI scales AMD chip fleet to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs
stories.Summary:
OpenAI is scaling its fleet of AMD chips to reduce its reliance on Nvidia GPUs. This effort to diversify infrastructure was announced on November 17, 2026. The company is moving away from a system that runs almost entirely on Nvidia hardware. This shift follows a massive compute deal signed with AMD in October. The company wants to avoid vulnerability to any disruptions in Nvidia's business.

The AMD deal provides 6 gigawatts of capacity, which is five times the 1.2 gigawatts at the Abilene, Texas campus. TensorWave will provide 457 megawatts of capacity across multiple U.S. sites, representing 7.6 percent of the total. OpenAI is also designing its own chip architecture called Jalapeño with Broadcom and planning to buy Google TPU chips. The first gigawatt of AMD capacity arrives in late 2026, with TensorWave following in early 2027. Full deployment is expected by early 2028, while Jalapeño production scales in 2027.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it would be hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang. A TensorWave spokesperson said the company decided to announce the deal during the Supercomputing 2026 conference. This timing helped the company meet potential hires, though they were unsure about the timing given Huang's resignation. The spokesperson noted that they had been trying to determine the right timing for a while. TensorWave must now roughly triple its staff to support this deployment.

Anthropic is affected by these shifts and already uses a more diversified chip base. Its S-1 revealed it relies on Google TPUs, AMD GPUs, Amazon Trainium GPUs, and Nvidia GPUs. Anthropic uses a proprietary orchestration layer to optimize workloads and reduce costs. California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton have also sued OpenAI over safety. Eight states and over 30 lawsuits regarding a Canadian school shooting also target the company.

OpenAI relies almost exclusively on Nvidia GPUs, making it vulnerable to disruptions. Jensen Huang recently resigned as Nvidia CEO, and the board is searching for a replacement. Investigations are underway regarding the possible sale of chips to China. The Nvidia board created an oversight committee to ensure compliance with U.S. export controls. Huang is scheduled to appear before the House in a closed-door hearing on December 1.

OpenAI plans to become less reliant on Nvidia over time through its new partnerships. Jensen Huang posted on X that he would be honored to return as CEO. The Nvidia board told CNBC it is not considering bringing Huang back. OpenAI has invited Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire to inspect its models. The articles leave open whether Huang might still surprise the industry by returning.

stories.Headline: Microsoft unveils cheaper specialized AI models and Copilot Fusion at Ignite to cut business token costs
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced a set of artificial intelligence improvements at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, with one message standing out: the company is focused on making AI cheaper for businesses by offering specialized models for specific tasks. In some cases, tasks that would have taken a company weeks were performed in minutes, according to the report. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said he keeps hearing from enterprises that token spend is going through the roof. The company's pitch centered on giving businesses the best price performance so they can scale their agents, Suleyman said.

During the conference, executives highlighted Microsoft IQ, a new platform designed to help businesses organize and share employees' knowledge, expertise, and tools, with the idea that AI systems learn how a company works and build on that knowledge over time. CEO Satya Nadella highlighted new AI models for coding, cybersecurity, and decision making, including the flagship coding model MAI Code 2, which is designed to handle complex, time-consuming programming tasks, work across multiple files, and understand entire software projects. Nadella also underscored Copilot Fusion, which orchestrates multiple models to deliver frontier-level results at significantly lower costs. Microsoft highlighted a feature that selects the right model for the task, making it easier to maximize output quality while managing the cost of each request.

Nadella kicked off the conference by acknowledging an outage the previous week that spanned regions, saying the company knows the trust placed in its services and takes that responsibility very seriously. He said he knows Microsoft has work to do and that the company is committed to ensuring it learns and continuously improves. Suleyman said Microsoft's commitment is to give customers the very best price performance out there so they can really scale their agents, and he added that the company also knows customers want models that feel truly theirs. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the announcements made at the conference.

stories.Headline: California agency recommends state safety standards and shutdown powers for frontier AI developers
stories.Summary:
California’s Government Operations Agency recommended on 16 November 2026 that the state require large frontier AI developers to meet state-set safety standards, accept ongoing oversight by licensed independent verifiers and face emergency shutdown orders, in a report released on 18 November 2026. Governor Gavin Newsom’s office announced the recommendations on 18 November 2026 under the title AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond, prepared by the California Government Operations Agency with the California Office of Emergency Services and an outside expert group. The 85-page report answers Executive Order N-9-26, which asked for proposals in four areas: standards, independent verification organizations, critical safety incident reporting and emergency shutdown requirements. The governor’s announcement summarises the package as baseline standards for all AI developers, mandatory ongoing third-party oversight, authority to order a shutdown in an emergency and authority to cap recursive self-improvement. The office defines recursive self-improvement as a scenario in which an AI model can design its own successor without human input, and the recommendations are not law.

The report recommends that the state set baseline safety, security and transparency standards for large frontier developers, with independent verification organizations translating them into technical tests and updating them as the science moves. It recommends that every large frontier developer submit to ongoing oversight by licensed IVOs with full access to the people and information they need, with unredacted assessments going to the state, and that developers could contest a state determination in court before it takes effect. It recommends cutting the deadline for most critical incident reports from 15 days to 48 hours, keeping 24 hours for imminent catastrophic risks, adding a near-miss channel, extending whistleblower protection to former employees and contractors, and treating models capable of catastrophic-risk actions as frontier models even if trained with fewer than 10^26 operations. It recommends that each developer maintain a Risk Containment Protocol verified by an IVO, that state officials could order an immediate shutdown on credible evidence of an imminent catastrophic risk or major loss-of-control event, and that the order would stay in force pending judicial review although a developer could seek a temporary restraining order. It recommends that developers report metrics on how much of their AI research and development is automated, including the share of compute devoted to it, and that the state get standby authority to cap recursive self-improvement if it finds a risk of catastrophic harm.

Unite.AI added that the proposals include a quarterly breakdown of how automating developers divide their compute among training, research experiments, safety work and customers, and that open-weight developers would face containment duties only for deployments under their control. The report says the state should draw on organizations outside government, including industry, civil society organizations and universities, to build AI evaluation capacity, and the SB 813 definition of an AI auditor it quotes includes an academic institution. The report says demand for chips has been pricing out talented researchers who are working on vital safety and security issues, and it recommends funding CalCompute, the public cloud cluster that SB 53 floated but which has not been funded, through a surcharge on the fees large frontier developers pay for IVO oversight, reserving capacity for independent safety and security research. The intended users would be researchers doing independent safety and security work, and the report leaves the surcharge level to the legislature. The report says it hopes to inform the legislature’s discussions as the legislature returns next month, and Unite.AI reported that the recommendations are intended to shape legislation when lawmakers return in December 2026.

Newsom said the federal government’s reckless failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American. Government Operations Agency Secretary Nick Maduros said we don’t have to choose between safety and innovation. Expert-group member Rob Reich, a Stanford professor and former senior adviser to the US AI Safety Institute, said there is more oversight of the cafeteria offering sandwiches to employees at a frontier AI developer than of the AI models they design. Gillian Hadfield, a Johns Hopkins professor, said she was pleased the report recommends requiring developers to allow in expert independent evaluators responsible to the state and rapidly building a sector of independent verification organizations. The group also included Alondra Nelson of the Institute for Advanced Study and Jason Goldman, according to the governor’s office.

The report notes that Newsom signed SB 53, the first US law governing frontier AI development, a year ago, and that SB 813 and AB 1405 this autumn created a framework for IVOs and a registry of AI auditors. The report argues that the federal government has not acted, stating that no federal law requires AI companies to follow baseline safety or security standards, undergo independent testing or verification, or shut down their models if they threaten the public. It cites loss-of-control incidents, including an OpenAI incident involving Hugging Face this summer, as evidence that the evidence base has changed. Universities with evaluation, security or AI-safety groups are potential IVO or auditor candidates if the recommendations become law, which would raise questions for research offices about independence, conflicts of interest, confidentiality duties and licensing that the report says IVOs would carry. Institutions that collaborate with frontier developers should also note the whistleblower and incident-reporting proposals, which would extend protections to former employees and contractors.

The next step is legislative: the report says the legislature returns next month, and Unite.AI reported December 2026 as the date lawmakers return. Any bill would have to set the surcharge level, the licensing rules for IVOs and the thresholds for emergency orders, which the report leaves open. The Governor’s office also called on Congress and President Trump to adopt California’s framework or use it as a floor, not a ceiling. The report leaves the surcharge level to the legislature. The recommendations are not law.

stories.Headline: Turkish regulator imposes interim measures on Google over AI news licensing terms
stories.Summary:
The Turkish Competition Authority announced on 2 November 2026 that the Competition Board had opened an investigation into Google's "AI Overviews" and "AI Mode" features. The Board imposed interim measures on Google by a decision of 8 October 2026 under Article 9(4) of Law No 4054 on the Protection of Competition. The Board's concern is twofold: that Google discriminates among comparable news publishers when selecting and licensing their content for its AI features, and that the terms on which that content is used are unfair. AI Overviews and AI Mode went live in Türkiye on 18 February 2026. The Board opened a preliminary inquiry on 27 August, inspected Google's Turkish subsidiary on 1 September and decided, unanimously, on 8 October.

Google has three months to comply, with daily fines thereafter, and may seek judicial review in Ankara. Google's "search generative AI control", a Search Console setting that lets a site withhold its content from AI features without, on Google's account, affecting its ranking elsewhere, was announced on 3 June 2026, the day the CMA's conduct requirement was published. That setting was tested with UK sites first and reached all sites worldwide on 31 August 2026. Google's News AI pilot, announced on 10 December 2025 and said by Google to cover more than 400 publications by October 2026, pays selected publishers for enhanced content used to develop AI features. The global template contains a most-favoured-customer clause that the Turkish version omits.

The Board found a strong suspicion of two abuses under Article 6: discrimination among comparable publishers, both in the selection of sources for AI answers and in the offer and negotiation of contracts, and the imposition of unfair trading conditions. It noted that the same facts may serve both theories. Google must not discriminate among equivalent publishers on criteria that are not objective, transparent and pre-determined. Google must negotiate in good faith with publishers that seek a contract, on objective, verifiable and transparent criteria reflecting the scope and intensity of use, user engagement and the effect on traffic, visibility and advertising revenue. Google must not penalise in ranking, visibility, indexing or traffic a publisher that declines a contract or its terms.

Google must supply publishers periodically with verifiable data on how their content is used and what engagement and traffic it generates. Google must make the AI opt-out exercisable independently of visibility and indexing in other Google services. Google must not worsen existing contracts or apply divergent terms in new ones, and must report compliance to the Authority. On the Board's redacted figures, search engines account for a substantial share of Turkish news sites' traffic, highest for publishers with weaker brands, and Google's share of that search-referred traffic is consistently high. The Board concludes that Google is an unavoidable trading partner for news publishers. The Board also records that AI referrals account for less than 0.01% of publishers' traffic.

The Board found that tying a publisher's choice about AI use to its visibility in Search limited publishers' ability to refuse. The Board found that the opt-out arrived six and a half months after the features did. The Board found that the opt-out's existence does not settle the matter, since not using it is no evidence of a free choice where the consequences for ranking are not predictable. Examining the global template and the Turkish version, the Board found that Google alone decides which publishers are offered a contract, that the text is standard and non-negotiable, and that the fee is derived from brand value and third-party traffic data by an undisclosed method. The Board found that the licence is worldwide, sublicensable and extends to training, that there is a single payment with no commitment to use the content or send traffic, and that attribution and linking are owed only "to the extent provided to similarly situated partners" and "where reasonably practicable".

The Board observes that publishers signed quickly, which shows consent, not competitive terms. The Board derives the unfair-trading-conditions theory from the general prohibition in Article 6 of Law No 4054, noting that the examples listed in Article 6 are not exhaustive. The Board adopts, almost verbatim, the Commission's test from Apple Music Streaming: trading conditions are unfair where they are imposed by a dominant undertaking on its trading partners, harm the interests of those partners or of third parties, including consumers, and are not necessary to achieve a legitimate objective or go beyond what is necessary for it. As in Apple, the Board adds that a finding of unfair conditions suffices and that no separate inquiry into a restriction of competition is required. The Board had said a few paragraphs earlier that competition-law intervention against unfair terms presupposes conduct that is not isolated and that produces appreciable "restrictive effects on the market".

Article 9(4) permits interim measures that preserve the situation prior to the infringement, yet a duty to negotiate on value-reflecting criteria and to supply usage data creates obligations that did not previously exist. That is likely to be Google's first argument before the administrative court. The Ankara 9th Administrative Court's Trendyol judgment states that an interim measure may neither punish the undertaking nor put complainants in a better position than before the alleged infringement, and may not substitute for the final decision. The court annulled the non-discrimination order for want of any analysis of whether the sellers concerned were in comparable situations. The Google decision cites that judgment for its standard of proof, not for its ceiling.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: FTC Solar launches FieldIQ to track solar tracker installation progress with AI
stories.Summary:
FTC Solar, Inc. launched FieldIQ, a construction intelligence offering for projects using FTC Solar trackers, the company announced on Nov. 17, 2026, from Austin, Texas. The offering uses AI to analyze drone and camera imagery, identify installation tasks and provide real-time progress tracking, supported by end-of-day productivity reports. FTC Solar is a provider of solar tracker systems, software and engineering services and trades on Nasdaq under the symbol FTCI. The launch was announced in a press release distributed by GlobeNewswire, and Quiver Quantitative posted its summary on Nov. 17, 2026. FieldIQ is designed for both conventional and robotic installations on FTC Solar tracker sites.

FieldIQ enables engineering, procurement and construction teams to measure crew and robot efficiency, compare productivity against benchmarks and draw on project data across their portfolios. The offering analyzes imagery collected via drone to identify installation tasks and track progress across construction stages, with real-time tracking and end-of-day reports consolidating progress and productivity data. EPC teams can track installation progress, measure crew and robot efficiency, compare against benchmarks and the customer's own project data, inform completion forecasts and use data across projects. FTC Solar was founded in 2017 by a group of renewable energy industry veterans. Interested parties can contact FTC Solar at [email protected] or visit the FTC Solar team at booth C7026 at RE+ 2026.

Anthony Carroll, Chief Executive Officer of FTC Solar, said Pioneer's constructability starts with simplifying installation through fewer connection points, simpler interfaces and a design compatible with both manual and robotic installation. Carroll said FieldIQ extends that value by giving EPCs greater visibility into installation performance. He said it enables customers to combine their field expertise with timely data, supporting the productivity and delivery objectives they set for their projects. Andrew Morse, Vice President of Software at FTC Solar, said EPCs bring deep experience in delivering complex projects and FieldIQ gives them another source of information to support that expertise. Morse said teams can track progress, compare productivity against benchmarks and use that data across their portfolio whether installation is performed by crews, robots or a combination of both.

Morse said FTC Solar's role is to make the information accessible and useful within the way customers manage their work. The press release includes a disclaimer about forward-looking statements, indicating the company may not be able to guarantee the successful implementation and outcomes of FieldIQ. FTC Solar undertakes no duty or obligation to update any forward-looking statements contained in the release as a result of new information. FTCI insiders made 4 purchases and 0 sales in the past 6 months, including Shaker Sadasivam's 3 purchases of 173,956 shares for an estimated $437,838 and Carroll's purchase of 24,745 shares for an estimated $51,469.

FTCI had revenues of $32.8M in Q3 2026, an increase of 26.06% from the same period in the prior year. In the most recent quarter, 14 institutional investors added shares of FTCI stock and 23 decreased their positions. Soros Fund Management LLC added 570,206 shares in Q3 2026 for an estimated $1,225,942, and Gilder Gagnon Howe & Co LLC added 250,785 shares in Q2 2026 for an estimated $1,273,987. Renaissance Technologies LLC removed 93,400 shares in Q2 2026 for an estimated $474,472, and Electron Capital Partners, LLC removed 90,201 shares in Q2 2026 for an estimated $458,221.

Marshall Wace, LLP removed 48,281 shares in Q3 2026 for an estimated $103,804, and Acadian Asset Management LLC removed 40,731 shares in Q2 2026 for an estimated $206,913. HRT Financial LP added 37,748 shares in Q3 2026 for an estimated $81,158. Wall Street analysts issued 2 buy ratings and 0 sell ratings on FTCI in the last several months, with UBS issuing a Buy rating on 09/18/2026 and Roth Capital issuing a Buy rating on 08/12/2026. Two analysts offered price targets in the last 6 months with a median target of $5.3, as Jon Windham from UBS set a target price of $3.6 on 09/18/2026 and Philip Shen from Roth Capital set a target price of $7.0 on 08/12/2026.

FTC Solar's tracker solutions are designed to support performance, reliability, constructability and adaptability across utility-scale solar projects. Solar trackers increase energy production at solar power installations by dynamically optimizing solar panel orientation to the sun. The forward-looking statements are based on current expectations and projections regarding FTC Solar's business, operations and other factors relating thereto. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Treasury and White House officials consider requiring US firms to label use of Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
The Treasury Department and White House science officials discussed requiring US companies to post website notices when using Chinese AI models. Reuters reported this plan on Wednesday, November 19, 2026, as a way to discourage reliance on these models. The proposal would label American adopters like Airbnb but would not impose new restrictions on Chinese developers. No formal rulemaking, text, deadline, or penalty has been announced or enacted by the government yet. The aim is to use reputational costs to name and shame companies that rely on Chinese AI.

The plan would require labels for companies like Airbnb, Anysphere, and DoorDash that use models from developers like Alibaba or Moonshot. House committees sent letters to Airbnb and Anysphere on April 29, and to DoorDash on July 31, 2026. DoorDash was asked for information by August 14 to reduce reliance on models developed in the PRC. Pinterest uses Qwen models for chatbots, and Anysphere's Cursor Composer 2 builds on the Kimi model from Moonshot AI. These labels would not show if data goes to China or if models run on US infrastructure.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent floated the disclosure idea in July and mentioned sanctioning Chinese firms that stole intellectual property. Michael Kratsios, confirmed March 25, 2025, directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy, which issued an April memo. House China Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar welcomed the report, calling disclosure an important step in managing risks. Moolenaar warned that models hosted on US servers can still carry vulnerabilities that the adopter did not choose. He also sponsored the No Adversarial AI Act, H.R. 4142, which was introduced on June 25, 2025.

Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said the company uses Alibaba's Qwen models for its customer service agent, which uses 13 models. Chesky stated in May 2026 that Airbnb does not buy from Alibaba or provide data to Chinese companies. Luma AI CEO Amit Jain told Semafor there was no evidence of change among companies using Chinese models. Booz Allen Hamilton found Qwen3-Coder added 130 percent more vulnerabilities under a US government persona than a neutral one. These findings affect US companies that use open-weight models to save money on infrastructure and development costs.

Yicai reported in September that seven Chinese models rank in the top 10 on OpenRouter by call volume. Epoch AI estimated in May that open-weight models lag closed models by about four months on average. Mozilla's September 15 report put the gap at 4.4 months, while other Chinese models trail by 14 months. Moonshot's Kimi K3 scored 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index but had a 51 percent hallucination rate. China's 2017 National Intelligence Law requires organizations to cooperate with intelligence work, though some dispute its enforcement.

The government must decide if mandatory labels constitute compelled speech under Zauderer v. Office of Disciplinary Counsel or NIFLA v. Becerra. It remains unsettled whether a notice saying a product uses a Chinese model is factual or a political message. Companies may use ML-BOM standards like CycloneDX, ECMA-424, or SPDX, but these rely on free-text strings for lineage. The articles leave open whether the Treasury will move into formal rulemaking or keep the labels voluntary. It is unclear if the administration will pursue de facto bans on foreign open-source models in the future.

stories.Headline: IEC proposes Total Contribution framework to assess AI data center sustainability
stories.Summary:
The International Electrotechnical Commission proposed a broader way to judge the sustainability of AI data centers, according to a report announced on November 17, 2026. The IEC issued its Clean Green Data Centres Strategic Position Paper and Leadership Briefing. The framework is called “Total Contribution.” It considers a facility’s environmental footprint alongside its relationship with the electricity grid, economic productivity and public services. The central idea is that a data center should be assessed as part of a wider system.

The IEC established a Strategic Standards Group on Data Centres to develop consistent metrics, reporting protocols and assurance mechanisms. The announcement does not establish a completed global scoring formula or a binding requirement that every data center adopt zero-water cooling. Power Usage Effectiveness measures total facility energy divided by the energy used by IT equipment. A PUE of 1.2 means the facility consumes 20% more energy than its IT equipment alone. The IEC already publishes ISO/IEC 30134-2:2026, which defines PUE and its measurement, calculation and reporting.

The IEC organizes the proposed framework around four connected dimensions. Energy and grid integration covers demand response, support for grid resilience, and the integration of on-site or new renewable generation. Environmental and resource stewardship covers energy consumption, water use, carbon emissions, circularity, advanced cooling and waste heat recovery. Economic and digital productivity covers the relationship between resource consumption and contributions such as AI-enabled productivity, digital transformation and skilled employment. Societal and regional resilience covers support for healthcare, communications, government and other critical services, together with regional development.

In an earlier IEC contribution to ITU’s AI for Good platform, the organization described the forthcoming paper as a way to identify sustainability and safety gaps in standardization. The IEA’s Powering Artificial Intelligence report says active management of computing loads remains rare. Many operators serve third parties and have limited visibility into or control over the work running inside their facilities. The IEA identifies standardized information exchange across computing customers, infrastructure providers and electricity networks as important to unlocking flexibility. The IEC’s announcement highlights liquid and immersion cooling, direct-current power distribution and power quality for AI infrastructure as areas for standards development.

The U.S. Department of Energy’s data center water-efficiency guidance illustrates a liquid-cooled system that ultimately transfers heat to a cooling tower. Liquid cooling does not by itself establish that a facility consumes no water. A closed equipment loop can coexist with evaporative heat rejection elsewhere in the system. The IEC emphasized treating data centers as active participants in energy systems and examining cooling, water use, electronic waste and lifecycle emissions. A large facility with an excellent PUE can still place substantial demand on a constrained grid.

The next phase will determine how the proposed framework becomes consistent reporting and assurance that operators, utilities and policymakers can use. The report’s ambition is to make those relationships visible. Turning that ambition into comparable, verifiable outcomes is the work ahead. The difficult next step is making the four dimensions comparable. A credible assessment needs to show where impacts occur, who receives the benefits and how claims are measured.

stories.Headline: AMD data center revenue jumps 97% as Google Cloud deploys Epyc chips for TPU systems
stories.Summary:
The Motley Fool published an article on November 15, 2026, by Harsh Chauhan, arguing that Advanced Micro Devices could be the best artificial intelligence stock to buy amid a sell-off. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index had declined 12% over the past three months, and AMD was caught up in that vortex with significant volatility. Concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, which has been key to the semiconductor sector's growth, drove the weakness. AMD's stock fell $51.24, or 8.75%, to $534.06 as of 4:00 PM ET on 11/13/26 on the NASDAQ. The article said the recent weakness opened a great opportunity for investors to buy a top stock at an attractive valuation.

AMD's data center revenue jumped 97% year over year in Q3 to $8.5 billion, driven by tremendous demand for its Epyc server central processing units from hyperscalers and AI companies. Alphabet's Google Cloud division expanded its partnership with AMD to deploy its 5th-generation Epyc server CPUs, security fabric, and x86 software to power its cloud Tensor Processing Unit systems. AMD Epyc will serve as the foundation for Google's TPUs, allowing users to run inference applications. Google Cloud reported a backlog of $561 billion at the end of the third quarter, and the tech giant expects to recognize half of that backlog in the next two years. AMD expects revenue to increase by more than 80% in 2027, fueled by healthy growth in the data center business, where it sees the server CPU total addressable market jump to $220 billion by 2030.

The article's author, Harsh Chauhan, wrote that he would not be surprised to see AMD embark on a stunning long-term rally. He said AMD is emerging as one of the most important players in the AI chip ecosystem. He noted that AMD has partnerships with major hyperscalers and AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and others, in the data center segment. He wrote that these customers should ensure solid long-term revenue growth for AMD, which is precisely what analysts are expecting. Chauhan disclosed that he has no position in any of the stocks mentioned.

The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft. The article said the $52.2 billion revenue estimate for 2026 points to a 51% jump over last year, and the forecast for 2027 and 2028 is also quite solid. Analysts expect AMD's EPS to grow by nearly 70% annually over the long run, and AMD trades at 33 times forward earnings. Assuming AMD clocks even 50% earnings growth in 2029 and 2030, its EPS could reach $57.53 by the end of the decade, using 2028's projected EPS of $25.57 as the base. A price-to-earnings ratio of 20 at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's forward P/E, would send AMD's shares to $1,150 in just over four years, twice AMD's current price.

The article noted that the past few months haven't been pretty for semiconductor stocks, as evidenced by the 12% decline in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the past three months. It said AMD's data center segment has incredible room for growth and that Alphabet is poised to spend aggressively on its cloud computing infrastructure. The article stated that AMD is therefore going to be a direct beneficiary of Alphabet's enormous spending. It said AMD is well-positioned to capitalize on the massive server CPU opportunity. The article added that AMD's revenue growth will filter down to the bottom line as well.

The article said opportunistic investors should capitalize on the recent weakness in the semiconductor sector and buy the stock for long-term gains. The clip carried a timestamp of November 17, 2026, and ran 23 seconds.

The White House responded to the pitch by blasting it as coming from a “far-left” figure and noted that El-Sayed had called the president an “unserious fool.” Fox News placed the story within its midterm elections and Senate coverage, tagging it with Democrats, Donald Trump and healthcare.
